According to Ostrander, the benefit comes not from the assistance itself but from the transfer of responsibility: children who keep receiving the same level of help never learn to apply decoding strategies on their own.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ostrander's claim?
options: Children whose teachers reduced prompts over the semester decoded unfamiliar texts independently better at year's end than children whose teachers kept prompts at a constant level, even though both groups received the same total minutes of guided reading.

Children whose teachers gave frequent prompts throughout the semester read guided texts more accurately during lessons than children whose teachers gave few prompts, though the two groups were not tested on reading alone.

Children whose teachers selected texts slightly beyond their independent level made larger reading gains than children whose teachers selected texts at their independent level, with prompting held constant in both groups.
Children whose teachers withdrew all prompts at the start of the semester decoded unfamiliar texts independently about as well at year's end as children whose teachers never gave prompts at all.
input.explanation: Ostrander의 핵심 주장은 도움 자체가 아니라 도움을 '점진적으로' 줄이는 것이 독립적 해독 능력을 높인다는 것이다. A는 총 지도 시간을 같게 통제한 채 도움을 줄인 집단이 일정하게 유지한 집단보다 독립 해독을 더 잘했다고 보여 주므로 주장을 직접 지지한다. B는 도움을 받는 상태에서의 정확도만 보여 주며 독립 읽기는 측정하지 않았다. C는 근접발달영역에 맞춘 텍스트 난이도의 효과일 뿐 도움을 줄이는 것과는 관계가 없다. D는 도움을 한꺼번에 없애는 것과 아예 주지 않는 것을 비교한 것이라 점진적 철회를 검증하지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: Ostrander's main claim is that the gradual withdrawal of support, not the support itself, is what builds independent decoding. Choice A keeps total guided time the same and shows that children whose prompts were reduced did better on independent decoding than children whose prompts stayed constant, so it directly supports her claim. Choice B only measures accuracy while children were being helped, and it never tests reading alone. Choice C shows that text difficulty within the zone of proximal development matters, but it says nothing about withdrawing support. Choice D compares removing all help at once with never giving help, so it doesn't test gradual withdrawal.
input.design: To answer, students have to connect two parts of the claim: gradual withdrawal and independent performance. Each wrong answer gets one part right: B covers the prompts but not independent reading, C covers the zone of proximal development but not withdrawal, and D covers withdrawal but not the gradual part. All four options use the same sentence frame.

input.passage: In a frequently cited set of experiments, psychologists John Darley and Bibb Latané had participants hear, over an intercom, another person apparently suffering a seizure. The researchers found that the likelihood of a participant seeking help depended heavily on group size: those who believed they were the only listener usually acted within a minute, whereas those who believed that several other listeners were also on the line ______ slower to respond, a pattern the researchers attributed to a diffusion of responsibility among potential helpers.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: was markedly
being markedly
to be markedly
were markedly
input.explanation: 빈칸에는 whereas 절의 주어 'those'에 대응하는 정동사가 필요하다. 'who believed ... on the line'은 those를 수식하는 관계절이므로 그 안의 'listeners'나 'the line'에 끌려서는 안 되며, 복수 주어 those에 맞는 복수 동사 were가 와야 하므로 D가 정답이다. A의 was는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 단수 명사 'line'에 맞춘 단수형이라 복수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. B의 being과 C의 to be는 정동사가 아니어서 whereas 절에 본동사가 없게 된다. 또한 앞 절의 'usually acted'와 대조를 이루려면 시제가 있는 동사가 필요하다.
input.explanation_en: The blank needs the main verb of the whereas clause, whose subject is "those." The phrase "who believed that several other listeners were also on the line" is a relative clause that modifies "those," so the verb has to agree with "those," not with a noun inside that clause. Since "those" is plural, the plural verb "were" is required, which makes D correct. A is a finite verb, but "was" is singular, so it seems to match the nearby noun "line" and does not agree with the plural subject. B ("being") and C ("to be") are not finite verbs, so the clause would have no main verb, even though it needs a tensed verb to contrast with "usually acted."
input.design: 긴 관계절이 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있고, 빈칸 바로 앞에 단수 명사 'line'과 관계절 안의 'were'가 있어 함정이 된다. 정동사 여부와 수 일치를 두 단계로 판단해야 한다.

content.text:
Design: long modifier between subject and verb; plural subject "cooperatives" separated by singular nouns. Options: subject-verb agreement + finite vs nonfinite.

Passage: "In the late nineteenth century, Japanese silk producers faced buyers in Lyon and New York who preferred Italian thread for its consistency. The regional cooperatives that grading inspectors from the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce, working with each village's sericulture association, had begun certifying ______ farmers to raise a single standardized cocoon variety, so that reeled silk from different districts could be sold in uniform lots."

Hmm, complex. Simpler: "The cooperative marketing associations formed in Nagano Prefecture during the 1890s, each of which pooled cocoons from hundreds of small family farms, ______ buyers with silk of uniform grade, an advantage Italian reelers, still selling..., struggled to match."
Options: A "was supplying" (singular attracted by "each"), B "supplying" (no finite verb), C "supplied", D "having supplied".
Need sense check: B partially plausible; D nonfinite. Good.

input.passage: By the 1890s, American hosiery mills demanded raw silk that would not snap on high-speed power looms, and Japanese exporters responded by standardizing cocoon breeds and grading thread before sale. The cooperative marketing associations formed in Nagano Prefecture, each of which pooled cocoons from hundreds of small family farms and sorted them by filament thickness, ______ buyers with silk of consistent grade, an advantage that Italian reelers, who still sold mostly through individual merchants, struggled to match.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: was supplying
supplying
supplied
having supplied
input.explanation: 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "associations"이며, "each of which..." 관계절은 삽입된 수식어일 뿐이므로 빈칸에는 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하다. C의 "supplied"는 과거 시제 정동사로 수 일치와 문장 완결을 모두 만족한다. A는 정동사이지만 가까운 "each"나 "thickness"에 끌린 단수형이라 복수 주어와 맞지 않는다. B와 D는 분사 형태여서 주어에 대응하는 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장을 만든다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of the sentence is the plural noun "associations"; the clause "each of which... thickness" is just an interrupting modifier, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject. C, "supplied," is a past-tense finite verb that works with a plural subject and completes the sentence. A is a finite verb, but it is singular, likely attracted by the nearby "each" or "thickness," so it doesn't agree with "associations." B and D are participle forms, which leave the subject without a main verb and create a sentence fragment.
input.design: 긴 삽입 관계절(단수 'each', 'thickness' 포함)로 주어와 동사를 분리해 수 일치 함정을 만들고, 분사 오답 둘로 정동사 필요성 판단을 추가해 두 단계 판단을 요구했다.

input.passage: In a series of studies on the Dunning-Kruger effect, psychologists asked participants to complete tests of logical reasoning, grammar, and humor recognition and then to estimate how well they had performed. The participants whose scores placed them in the bottom quartile across these very different domains ______ their own performance, often ranking themselves above the sixtieth percentile.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: consistently overestimated
consistently overestimating
having consistently overestimated
who consistently overestimated
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The participants"이고, 그 뒤의 "whose scores ... domains"는 주어를 꾸미는 긴 관계절이므로 주절에는 정동사가 필요하다. A는 과거형 정동사 "overestimated"를 제공해 문장을 완성한다. B의 현재분사와 C의 완료분사는 정동사가 아니어서 주절이 완성되지 않는다. D는 관계대명사 "who"로 또 하나의 수식절을 만들 뿐이라 여전히 주절 동사가 없다. 따라서 정답은 A이다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The participants," and the long clause "whose scores ... domains" just modifies that subject, so the main clause still needs a finite verb. A gives you the past-tense finite verb "overestimated," which completes the sentence. B (a present participle) and C (a perfect participle) aren't finite verbs, so the main clause stays incomplete. D adds "who," which turns the phrase into another modifying clause, so there's still no main verb. That makes A the answer.
input.design: 긴 관계절이 주어와 빈칸 사이에 끼어 있어 정동사 필요성을 놓치기 쉽게 했다. 분사·관계절 오답은 앞에 나온 관계절처럼 그럴듯해 보이도록 만들었다.

input.passage:
Listeners new to Indian classical music often assume that a raga performance is either strictly composed or entirely spontaneous. In fact, it is neither. A raga specifies a set of pitches, characteristic ascending and descending patterns, and certain phrases that must recur, and many of its intervals derive from simple whole-number frequency ratios, such as the 3:2 relationship that defines the perfect fifth. These constraints are fixed long before any musician sits down to play.

Yet within those limits, performers are expected to invent. In the slow opening section known as the alap, a sitarist may spend half an hour exploring a single raga, deciding moment by moment which pitch to linger on, how to bend toward the next, and when to introduce a signature phrase. Musicologist Martin Clayton has argued that this freedom is meaningful precisely because the boundaries are so precise: listeners recognize a performer's originality by hearing how inventively the musician moves while never stepping outside the raga's rules.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: In raga performance, a fixed system of mathematically grounded rules provides the very structure that gives a musician's spontaneous invention its significance.
In raga performance, the alap section allows musicians to abandon the pitch patterns and recurring phrases that govern the rest of the piece.
In raga performance, the whole-number frequency ratios behind the intervals matter more to listeners than any choices the musician makes while playing.
In raga performance, musicians are judged mainly by how long they can sustain the slow opening section before introducing a signature phrase.
input.design: 정답을 고르려면 첫 단락의 고정된 수학적 규칙과 둘째 단락의 즉흥을 연결해 둘이 서로를 의미 있게 만든다는 관계를 파악해야 한다. 오답들은 alap, 비율, 연주 길이 같은 실제 세부를 쓰지만 그 관계를 왜곡한다.
input.explanation: 지문은 라가가 수학적 비율에 근거한 고정 규칙을 갖지만, 그 정밀한 경계 덕분에 연주자의 즉흥이 의미를 갖는다고 말하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 alap을 언급하지만, 지문은 연주자가 라가의 규칙을 결코 벗어나지 않는다고 하므로 틀렸다. C는 정수 비율이라는 세부를 쓰지만, 청중은 연주자의 창의적 선택을 통해 독창성을 알아본다고 했으므로 지문과 반대된다. D는 '30분'이라는 세부를 과장한 것으로, 지문은 지속 시간을 평가 기준으로 제시하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: A is correct because the text describes fixed rules, some based on mathematical ratios, and then argues that these precise limits are exactly what make a performer's improvisation meaningful. B mentions the alap, but the text says performers never step outside the raga's rules, so they don't abandon its patterns. C picks up the detail about whole-number ratios, but it contradicts the text, which says listeners notice originality through the musician's inventive choices. D stretches the half-hour detail too far: the text never says performers are judged by how long the opening lasts.

input.passage: When a drop of water rests on a freshly waxed car hood, it beads up into a nearly round shape. Scientists describe this behavior by measuring the contact angle, the angle formed where the edge of the drop meets the surface. On hydrophobic materials such as wax, this angle is often greater than 90 degrees ______ on glass, which water wets easily, the same drop spreads out and the angle becomes much smaller.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: degrees; however,
degrees, however,
degrees however
degrees, however
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "On hydrophobic materials ... 90 degrees"와 뒤 "on glass ... much smaller"는 각각 완전한 독립절이다. "however"는 접속부사라서 두 독립절을 혼자 연결할 수 없으므로, 앞에 세미콜론을 두고 뒤에 쉼표를 찍은 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 쉼표와 접속부사만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
input.explanation_en: The part before the blank ("On hydrophobic materials ... 90 degrees") and the part after it ("on glass ... much smaller") are both independent clauses. "However" is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction, so it can't join two independent clauses by itself. That makes A correct: a semicolon before "however" and a comma after it. B and D join the two clauses with only a comma and "however," which creates a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, so it creates a run-on sentence.
input.design: 이 문항은 독립절 두 개가 접속부사 however로 이어지는 경계 하나만 묻는다. 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스 두 가지와 무종지문 하나로 구성한 흔한 오개념이다.

input.passage: In the 1970s, linguist Charles Fillmore challenged the view that a word's meaning can be captured by a short list of defining features. He observed that a word such as "sell" makes sense only against a larger background scene, which he called a frame: a commercial transaction involving a buyer, a seller, goods, and money. Words like "buy," "pay," "cost," and "charge" all call up this same frame, but each one highlights a different participant. Saying that a book "cost" twenty dollars, for example, places the goods and the price in the foreground while leaving the buyer in the background. Fillmore argued that listeners interpret sentences by activating such frames, and that this is why a sentence can convey information it never states outright: hearing "She spent the afternoon on land," a listener infers a sea voyage, because "on land" evokes a frame that contrasts land with sea, whereas "on the ground" would suggest a contrast with air.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Fillmore showed that words referring to commercial transactions are harder for listeners to interpret than words referring to physical locations.
Fillmore argued that listeners understand a sentence mainly by identifying the defining features of each word and combining them.
Fillmore proposed that words get their meaning from the background scenes they evoke, which lets listeners grasp more than a sentence explicitly says.
Fillmore claimed that verbs such as "buy" and "sell" have identical meanings because they refer to the same participants in a transaction.
input.explanation: 지문은 단어의 의미가 정의적 특징 목록이 아니라 그 단어가 불러일으키는 배경 장면(frame)에 의존하며, 이 때문에 청자가 명시되지 않은 정보까지 추론한다는 Fillmore의 주장을 중심으로 하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 상거래와 장소 예시를 모두 언급하지만, 두 예시는 해석의 난이도를 비교하려는 것이 아니라 같은 원리를 보여 주는 사례이다. B는 Fillmore가 반박한 견해, 즉 정의적 특징 목록 관점을 그의 주장으로 뒤바꿔 놓았다. D는 같은 프레임이라는 점은 맞지만, 지문은 각 동사가 서로 다른 참여자를 부각한다고 했으므로 의미가 동일하다는 진술은 틀렸다.
input.explanation_en: C is correct because the text centers on Fillmore's claim that a word's meaning depends on the background scene, or frame, it evokes rather than on a list of defining features, and that this is how listeners infer information a sentence never states. A mentions both the commercial and location examples, but the text uses them to illustrate one principle, not to compare how hard they are to interpret. B takes the view Fillmore rejected, the defining-features list, and presents it as his own argument. D is right that these verbs share a frame, but the text says each verb highlights a different participant, so calling their meanings identical is wrong.
input.design: 오답 A와 D는 지문의 실제 예시(상거래·장소, 동일한 프레임)를 바탕으로 삼았고, B는 Fillmore가 반박한 견해를 뒤집어 넣어 훑어 읽는 학생을 노렸다. 정답은 정의 단계와 추론 단계를 연결해야 고를 수 있다.

input.passage: In the late sixteenth century, Viceroy Francisco de Toledo reorganized the mita, a rotational labor draft that Spanish officials adapted from an earlier Andean practice, to supply workers for the silver mines of Potosí. Indigenous communities that had already been bound to Spanish encomenderos through tribute obligations ______ the shafts of Cerro Rico, a mountain whose ore helped finance the Spanish Crown for generations.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: now had to send one-seventh of their adult men each year into
now had to send one-seventh of their adult men each year, into
now, had to send one-seventh of their adult men each year; into
now had to send one-seventh of their adult men each year: into
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "Indigenous communities"이고, "that had already been bound ... obligations"는 그 주어를 한정하는 필수 관계절이며, 동사는 "had to send"이다. 전치사구 "into the shafts"는 동사 send의 방향을 나타내므로 동사와 끊으면 안 된다. 따라서 문장부호가 없는 A가 정답이다. B는 send와 into 사이에 쓸데없는 쉼표를 넣어 동사와 전치사구를 끊는다. C는 주어와 동사 사이에 쉼표를 넣고, 독립절이 뒤따르지 않는데도 세미콜론을 쓴다. D의 콜론은 앞에 완전한 절이 있어 보여도 동사와 꼭 필요한 전치사구를 갈라놓으므로 틀렸다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "Indigenous communities." The clause "that had already been bound ... obligations" is an essential relative clause that restricts that subject, and the verb is "had to send." The phrase "into the shafts" tells where the men are sent, so it has to stay attached to "send." That's why A, with no punctuation, is correct. B adds an unnecessary comma between "send" and "into," which cuts the verb off from its phrase. C puts a comma between the subject and verb, and it uses a semicolon even though no independent clause comes after it. D might look fine because a complete clause comes before the colon, but the colon still separates the verb from a phrase it needs, so D is wrong.
input.design: 긴 필수 관계절이 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어 절의 경계를 잘못 볼 수 있다. 또 빈칸 앞부분이 완전한 절처럼 보여서 콜론, 세미콜론, 쉼표 오답이 그럴듯해 보인다.

content.text:
Design: long subject with modifier, subject-verb agreement plus finite verb need.

Passage: "In the late eighteenth century, landowners in northern Scotland began financing curing yards, cooperages, and harbor piers along the coast. The investment, which many estate managers justified as a way to employ tenants displaced by agricultural changes, ______ the region's capacity to export salted herring to markets in the Baltic and the Caribbean."

Options: A "having greatly expanded" (no finite verb), B "were greatly expanding" (plural agreement with tenants/changes), C "greatly expanding", D "greatly expanded". Need distractors partly right: B is finite but wrong number; A/C nonfinite. Fine.

input.passage: In the late eighteenth century, landowners in northern Scotland began financing curing yards, cooperages, and harbor piers along the coast. The investment, which many estate managers defended as a way to employ tenants displaced by agricultural changes, ______ the region's capacity to export salted herring to markets in the Baltic and the Caribbean.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: having greatly expanded
were greatly expanding
greatly expanding
greatly expanded
input.explanation: 주어는 단수 명사 'The investment'이고, 그 뒤의 'which ... changes' 관계절은 삽입된 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하며, D의 'greatly expanded'가 이 조건을 충족한다. B는 정동사이긴 하지만 복수형 'were'가 관계절 속 'tenants'나 'changes'에 이끌린 오류로, 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다. A와 C는 분사 형태여서 주절에 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of the main clause is the singular noun "The investment." The clause "which ... changes" is just an interrupting modifier. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, and D, "greatly expanded," does exactly that. B is a finite verb, but its plural "were" looks like it agrees with the nearby plural nouns "tenants" or "changes" instead of with the actual subject. A and C are participles, so choosing either one leaves the main clause without a finite verb, and the sentence is incomplete.
input.design: 긴 삽입 관계절 속 복수 명사가 오답 B(복수 정동사)를 유인한다. 학생은 두 단계를 거쳐야 한다. 먼저 정동사가 필요하다는 것을 알아야 하고(A, C 배제), 다음으로 진짜 주어와 수가 맞는지 확인해야 한다.

content.text:
Design: a long appositive/modifier then clause boundary.

Passage: "In The Weary Blues (1926), Langston Hughes did not simply describe the music he heard in Harlem's clubs. The collection's title poem, which follows a pianist through a slow, mournful song on Lenox Avenue, borrows the repeated lines of the twelve-bar blues and the loose cadence of everyday speech______ the result is verse that seems less written than performed."

Blank between independent clauses. Correct: "; as a result," no... keep simple. Options: A ", the result" — comma splice. B ": the result" hmm, the blank is before "the result". Options: A "speech, and, the result" awkward. Let's make options: A ", " (splice), B ";" correct, C " and" (no comma — run-on? with coordinating conjunction lacking comma, SAT treats as error), D ", which" -> "which the result is" ungrammatical. Fine; partially plausible ones: A and C.

input.passage: In The Weary Blues (1926), Langston Hughes did not simply describe the music he heard in Harlem's clubs. The collection's title poem, which follows a pianist through a slow, mournful song on Lenox Avenue, borrows the repeated lines of the twelve-bar blues and the loose cadence of everyday speech______ the result is verse that seems less written than performed.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: and
, which
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 비필수 관계절을 지나 주어 'poem'과 동사 'borrows'를 갖춘 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'the result is verse...'도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C는 등위접속사 앞에 쉼표가 없어 두 독립절이 표준 규칙에 맞게 연결되지 않는다. D는 'which' 뒤에 'the result is'가 붙어 관계절이 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: Look past the long nonessential clause ("which follows... Lenox Avenue") and you'll find that the text before the blank is a complete independent clause (subject "poem," verb "borrows"). The text after the blank, "the result is verse...," is also an independent clause. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C uses "and" with no comma before it, so the two independent clauses aren't joined correctly. D makes "which the result is verse..." a relative clause that doesn't work grammatically.
input.design: The long nonessential relative clause pulls attention away from the main subject and verb, so the student has to confirm that there are two independent clauses. A and C are each close to a correct join but are each missing something; D looks like a relative clause but doesn't work.

input.passage: When a magnetic field is applied to an iron-cobalt alloy, the material's magnetic domains rotate to align with the field, and the alloy physically stretches by a few hundred parts per million. Engineers at several sensor manufacturers, including a small firm in Ohio that builds vibration harvesters for bridges, ______ the elongation does not increase indefinitely: once nearly all domains are aligned, further increases in field strength produce almost no additional change in length.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: have noted, however;
have noted, however, that
have noted; however,
have noted, however, and
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "Engineers"이고, 긴 동격 삽입구가 주어 뒤에 들어가 있다. 동사 "have noted"는 목적어가 필요하므로 "that"이 뒤의 명사절(the elongation does not increase...)을 이끌어야 하며, "however"는 쉼표 사이에 삽입되는 것이 맞다. 따라서 정답은 B이다. A와 C는 세미콜론을 쓰는데, 세미콜론 앞부분 "Engineers ... have noted (however)"는 목적어가 없어 독립절이 될 수 없으므로 틀리다. D는 "and"로 두 절을 연결하지만 "have noted"의 목적어가 여전히 없어서 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "Engineers," and a long appositive phrase comes right after it. The verb "have noted" needs an object, so "that" has to introduce the noun clause that follows (the elongation does not increase...), and "however" belongs inside a pair of commas. That makes B the answer. A and C use a semicolon, but the part before the semicolon, "Engineers ... have noted (however)," has no object, so it can't stand on its own as an independent clause. D joins the clauses with "and," but "have noted" still has no object, so the sentence doesn't work.
input.design: 긴 동격 삽입구로 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓고, 접속부사 however를 함께 넣었다. 그래서 학생은 세미콜론이 맞는지와 have noted에 목적어가 필요한지를 두 단계로 판단해야 한다.

input.passage: Historians often credit the Congress of Vienna (1814–1815) with keeping the peace in Europe for decades, but the negotiators were not mainly trying to punish France. Austria's foreign minister, Klemens von Metternich, and Britain's Viscount Castlereagh were both concerned that one power might again dominate the continent. Their worry was not only France: Russia, with its huge army, had come out of the Napoleonic Wars stronger than ever. A badly weakened France would leave a gap in central and western Europe that Russia might fill. So the Congress returned France to roughly its 1792 borders, let it keep its standing as a great power, and built up states such as Prussia and the Netherlands along France's frontiers. These arrangements suggest that the negotiators' main goal was ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: to keep any single state, whether France or Russia, from gaining enough power to overwhelm the others.
to weaken France so much that it could never again threaten its neighbors.
to make Russia the main guard against any new French expansion.
to bring Europe's borders back to exactly where they had been before the French Revolution.
input.explanation: 지문은 협상가들이 프랑스를 벌하는 것보다 한 국가의 대륙 지배를 막는 데 신경 썼고, 러시아도 걱정했으며, 프랑스를 강대국으로 남겨 두면서 국경 지역 국가들을 강화했다고 말한다. 이 두 정보를 이으면 목표는 어떤 단일 국가도 압도적이 되지 못하게 하는 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 프랑스 견제라는 부분만 맞지만, 프랑스가 강대국 지위를 유지했다는 내용과 어긋난다. C는 러시아를 오히려 위협으로 본 지문과 반대된다. D는 1792년 국경을 언급하지만 '대략'에 해당하는 것은 프랑스뿐이고, 프로이센 등을 키운 일은 단순 복원이 아니다.
input.explanation_en: The passage says the negotiators cared less about punishing France than about stopping any one power from dominating, and that they worried about Russia too. France kept its great-power standing, while its neighbors were made stronger. Put those two facts together and the goal is clearly to keep any single state from overwhelming the others, so A is correct. B gets the check on France partly right, but it doesn't fit with France being allowed to stay a great power. C is the opposite of the passage, which treats Russia as a danger, not a guard. D picks up the 1792 borders, but only France went back to roughly those lines, and building up Prussia and the Netherlands was not a simple return to the past.
input.design: To get the answer, students have to connect two facts: the worry about Russia and the fact that France stayed strong. Skimmers may fall for B (the France focus) or D (the 1792 borders), since each is partly supported by the passage.

input.passage:
Text 1
Many sustainability campaigns try to change everyday habits, such as how often people do laundry, by giving individuals information about energy use. The assumption is that once people know the facts, they will choose to act differently. According to this view, a person's attitudes and decisions are the main drivers of routine behavior.

Text 2
Sociologist Theodore Schatzki and other practice theorists argue that routines are not mainly the product of individual choices. Instead, practices like laundry are shaped by shared rhythms: work schedules, school timetables, and expectations about clean clothes. Because these timings are woven into daily life, information alone rarely shifts habits; the surrounding schedules and social norms must change too.
input.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the assumption described in Text 1?
options: By claiming that it overlooks how shared schedules and norms keep routines in place
By claiming that it overlooks how little energy household laundry actually uses
By claiming that it overlooks how eager most people are to learn about energy use
By claiming that it overlooks how quickly people abandon habits once informed
input.explanation: Text 1은 정보를 받으면 개인이 선택을 바꿔 습관이 달라진다고 가정한다. Text 2는 루틴이 근무·학교 일정 같은 공유된 리듬과 사회 규범에 묶여 있어 정보만으로는 잘 바뀌지 않는다고 주장하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Text 2가 세탁의 에너지 사용량을 전혀 다루지 않으므로 틀렸다. C는 사람들이 정보를 배우고 싶어 하는지에 대한 언급이 없으므로 틀렸다. D는 정보를 받으면 습관을 빨리 버린다는 내용인데, 이는 정보만으로는 습관이 잘 바뀌지 않는다는 Text 2의 주장과 정반대이다.
input.explanation_en: Text 1 assumes that once people get information, their individual choices change and their habits change with them. Text 2 argues that routines are tied to shared rhythms, like work and school schedules, and to social norms, so information alone rarely changes them. That makes A the answer. B is wrong because Text 2 never talks about how much energy laundry uses. C is wrong because Text 2 says nothing about whether people want to learn about energy. D is wrong because it says informed people drop their habits quickly, which is the opposite of what Text 2 claims.
input.design: Text 2가 Text 1의 가정을 직접 반박하므로 한 단계만 추론하면 된다. 네 선택지 모두 "By claiming that it overlooks how..." 같은 틀을 쓰고, 오답은 지문에 없는 주장이거나 Text 2와 반대되는 흔한 오개념으로 구성했다.

content.text:
Design: subject-verb agreement after a long intervening modifier, plus finite verb vs. nonfinite.

Passage: "Painted at Papunya in the early 1970s, the dot works of artists such as Clifford Possum Tjapaltjarri encode ancestral journeys across specific tracts of land, so that a canvas functions less as a picture than as a map of sacred sites. The rapid acquisition of these paintings by major Western museums and auction houses, which had previously classified Aboriginal objects as ethnography rather than fine art, ______ critics to ask whether institutional acceptance has obscured the works' spiritual meanings."

Subject: "acquisition" singular → "has prompted". Options:
A) has prompted
B) have prompted (agrees with houses/museums — plural attraction)
C) prompting (nonfinite, no main verb)
D) to prompt

All in the same frame. Good.

input.passage: Painted at Papunya in the early 1970s, the dot works of artists such as Clifford Possum Tjapaltjarri encode ancestral journeys across specific tracts of land, so that a canvas functions less as a picture than as a map of sacred sites. The rapid acquisition of these paintings by major Western museums and auction houses, which had long classified Aboriginal objects as ethnography rather than fine art, ______ critics to ask whether institutional acceptance has obscured the works' spiritual meanings.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: has prompted
have prompted
prompting
to prompt
input.explanation: 두 번째 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "acquisition"이고, "of these paintings by ... houses, which ... fine art"는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 긴 수식어구이다. 따라서 이 문장에는 단수 주어와 수가 일치하는 정동사가 필요하며, A의 "has prompted"가 이 조건을 충족한다. B는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "museums and auction houses"에 수를 맞춘 것이어서 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. C와 D는 분사와 부정사여서 주어 "acquisition"에 연결될 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of the second sentence is the singular noun "acquisition." Everything from "of these paintings" through "fine art" is a long modifier that comes between the subject and its verb. That means the sentence needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, and A, "has prompted," is the only choice that does this. B is a finite verb, but it matches the nearby plural "museums and auction houses" instead of the actual subject, so the subject and verb don't agree. C is a participle and D is an infinitive, so either one leaves "acquisition" without a main verb and makes the sentence incomplete.
input.design: 긴 전치사구와 관계절 끝에 복수 명사를 두어, 훑어 읽으면 복수 동사(B)를 고르도록 했다. 학생은 먼저 정동사가 필요하다는 것을 판단하고(C와 D 배제), 그다음 수 일치를 확인해야 한다.

input.passage: When a thin slice of quartz is squeezed, a small voltage appears across its faces; when a voltage is applied instead, the crystal flexes slightly. Engineers exploit this two-way piezoelectric behavior in oscillator circuits, where a quartz wafer cut to precise dimensions vibrates at a single resonant frequency. The stability of that frequency, which drifts by only a few parts per million even as the surrounding temperature rises and falls over the course of a day, ______ why quartz oscillators keep time in nearly every wristwatch and computer.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: explains
explaining
explain
having explained
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The stability'이고, 'which drifts ... over the course of a day'는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 관계절이다. 문장에는 아직 정동사가 없으므로 단수 주어에 맞는 정동사 A 'explains'가 필요하다. C 'explain'은 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'parts'나 'quartz oscillators'에 이끌린 복수형이어서 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다. B 'explaining'과 D 'having explained'는 분사여서 문장에 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The stability," and the clause "which drifts ... over the course of a day" just interrupts between the subject and its verb. The sentence still needs a main verb, so you need the singular finite verb in A, "explains." C, "explain," is a finite verb, but it's plural. It might sound right if you match it to nearby plural nouns like "parts" or "quartz oscillators," but it doesn't agree with the singular subject. B, "explaining," and D, "having explained," are participles, so with either one the sentence has no main verb and is incomplete.
input.design: 긴 비제한 관계절을 주어와 동사 사이에 넣고 복수 명사(parts, temperature 이후 oscillators)를 근처에 두어, 정동사인지 판단한 뒤 주어 수 일치까지 확인해야 정답을 고를 수 있게 했다.

input.passage: Historians agree that the refrigerated railcar, perfected in the late 1870s, allowed Chicago packers such as Gustavus Swift to slaughter cattle in the Midwest and ship dressed beef to eastern cities. They disagree about why the packers came to dominate the trade. Economic historian Mary Yeager argues that the railcar alone did not suffice: Swift also had to build a chain of icing stations, branch warehouses, and sales offices, because railroads and local butchers that profited from shipping live cattle refused to cooperate. In her account, the packers' control over every stage from slaughter to sale was a forced response to resistance. __Other scholars, however, point out that by the 1890s rival packers who faced little such resistance built nearly identical networks anyway.__ For these scholars, owning the entire chain simply lowered costs in ways that made it attractive regardless of opposition.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence suggesting that the explanation Yeager offers for the packers' integrated networks may not account for why such networks spread.
It presents evidence suggesting that resistance from railroads and butchers was even stronger than Yeager acknowledges.
It presents evidence suggesting that the refrigerated railcar was less important to the packers' success than historians generally agree.
It presents evidence suggesting that later packers copied Swift's networks because they hoped to avoid conflict with local butchers.
input.explanation: 정답 A: Yeager는 수직 통합이 저항에 대한 '어쩔 수 없는 대응'이라고 본다. 밑줄 문장은 저항이 거의 없던 경쟁 업체들도 같은 네트워크를 만들었다고 지적하는데, 이는 저항이 원인이라는 설명에 맞지 않는 사례이므로 Yeager의 설명에 대한 반론 근거 역할을 한다(지문은 '반박'이라는 말을 직접 쓰지 않으므로 두 입장의 차이로 추론해야 한다). B: 두 입장을 뒤바꾼 오답이다. 이 문장은 저항이 약했던 경우를 말하므로 Yeager의 강조점을 강화하지 않고 오히려 약화한다. C: 한쪽 입장만 근거로 삼은 오답이다. 냉장 화차의 중요성은 양측이 모두 동의하는 전제이고, 논쟁의 대상은 통합이 일어난 원인이다. D: 지문에 없는 새로운 동기를 지어낸 오답이다. 경쟁 업체들은 저항을 거의 겪지 않았고, 다른 학자들은 비용 절감을 이유로 든다.
input.explanation_en: A is correct. Yeager says the packers controlled the whole chain as a forced response to resistance. The underlined sentence notes that rival packers who faced little resistance built the same networks anyway. That case doesn't fit her explanation, so the sentence works as evidence against it. The text never says "rebut," so you have to infer this from how the two views differ. B swaps the two positions: the sentence describes weak resistance, which undercuts Yeager's emphasis instead of strengthening it. C relies on only one side's view: both sides accept that the railcar mattered, and the debate is about why integration happened. D makes up a motive the text never gives: the rivals faced little resistance, and the scholars point to cost savings, not a wish to avoid conflict.
input.design: Yeager는 통합을 저항에 대한 대응으로 보지만, 밑줄 문장은 저항이 없던 경우를 제시한다. 이 문장이 Yeager의 설명을 반박하는 역할이라는 점을 직접 말하지 않고 추론하게 했다. 오답은 입장 뒤바꾸기, 한쪽 입장만 근거로 쓰기, 지문에 없는 반응 지어내기로 구성했다.

input.passage: In the seventeenth century, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) sought total control of the trade in cloves and nutmeg, spices that grew almost nowhere but the Maluku Islands. To keep prices high, company officials, directing operations from their headquarters at Batavia on Java, ordered clove trees on every island outside approved plantations cut down ______ armed fleets known as hongi expeditions sailed among the outer islands each year to uproot any seedlings planted without company permission.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: and,
, meanwhile,
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'company officials ... ordered ... cut down'은 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'armed fleets ... sailed ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이므로 두 절을 바르게 잇는 세미콜론을 쓴 B가 정답이다. 쉼표만 쓴 A는 두 독립절을 쉼표로 이어 붙인 comma splice이다. C는 등위접속사 and를 썼지만 쉼표가 and 뒤에 와서 'and'와 주어 'armed fleets' 사이를 부적절하게 끊는다. D의 meanwhile은 접속부사이지 접속사가 아니라서, 앞에 쉼표만 두면 여전히 comma splice가 된다.
input.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "company officials ... ordered clove trees ... cut down," make an independent clause, and the words after it, "armed fleets ... sailed ...," make a second independent clause with its own subject and verb. A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses, so B is correct. A puts only a comma between the two clauses, which is a comma splice. C uses the conjunction "and," but the comma comes after "and," which wrongly separates the conjunction from the subject "armed fleets." D uses "meanwhile," which is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction, so putting only a comma in front of it still makes a comma splice.
input.design: Long interrupting modifier (directing operations from Batavia) and a long object phrase obscure where the first independent clause ends; distractors include a conjunctive-adverb splice and a misplaced comma with a conjunction, each partially plausible.

input.passage: Historians have long debated what drove ordinary villagers in northern China to join the Boxer movement in 1899–1900. One traditional account emphasizes religious antagonism: the Boxers, it holds, were motivated chiefly by hostility toward Christian missionaries and converts. Historian Lin Wei offers an alternative view. She argues that economic disruption caused by foreign concessions, especially the railways and river shipping that put local cart drivers, boatmen, and porters out of work, was the primary factor that turned rural discontent into armed mobilization.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Lin Wei's argument?
options: Boxer recruitment was highest in counties where newly built foreign-run transport lines had replaced traditional hauling trades, even when those counties had few Christian converts.
Boxer recruitment was highest in counties with large Christian communities, regardless of whether foreign-run transport lines had been built there.
Boxer recruitment was highest in counties where foreign-run transport lines had been built, but only where missionaries had also founded churches in the same years.
Boxer recruitment was roughly equal in counties with and without foreign-run transport lines, though former boatmen often held leadership roles.
input.explanation: 린 웨이는 운송업 일자리를 없앤 경제적 혼란이 동원의 주된 원인이었다고 주장한다. A는 운송 노선이 전통적 운반업을 대체한 지역에서 기독교인이 적어도 가담률이 높았다고 하므로, 종교적 요인과 분리된 경제적 요인을 보여 주장을 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 종교 중심의 전통적 설명을 지지한다. C는 운송 노선이 교회와 함께 있을 때만 효과가 있었다고 하므로 종교 요인과 구분되지 않아 경제 요인이 주된 원인임을 보여주지 못한다. D는 운송 노선 유무가 가담률에 차이를 만들지 않았다고 하므로 오히려 주장을 약화시키며, 지도자 역할은 대중 동원과 별개의 문제다.
input.explanation_en: Lin Wei argues that economic disruption, meaning lost transport jobs, was the main reason people mobilized. Choice A ties high recruitment to places where traditional hauling trades were replaced, even when few Christians lived there. That separates the economic factor from the religious one, so A directly supports her claim. Choice B backs the traditional religious account instead. Choice C says transport lines mattered only where churches also appeared, so you can't tell the economic cause apart from the religious one. Choice D shows recruitment didn't change with transport lines, which actually weakens her claim, and who held leadership roles is a separate issue from how many people joined.
input.design: 모든 선택지를 같은 '모집률이 가장 높았던 지역' 틀로 쓰고, C는 교란 요인을, D는 부분 관련 세부를 넣어 정독해야 A를 고를 수 있게 했다.

input.passage: A single glass lens bends blue light more strongly than red light, so the colors in an image come to a focus at slightly different distances and objects appear edged with colored fringes. In the 1700s, opticians found that pairing a converging lens of crown glass with a weaker diverging lens of flint glass could largely cancel this effect. Optical engineer Mariela Ostrowski argues that the pairing works not because flint glass bends light more strongly overall, but because flint glass spreads colors apart (its dispersion) much more than crown glass does relative to how much it bends light. On this view, the weak flint lens can undo the crown lens's color spread while removing only part of its focusing power, so the pair still brings light to a focus.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ostrowski's argument?
options: Doublets made from a crown glass and a flint glass with much higher overall bending power produced less color fringing than single crown lenses did, regardless of the dispersion of the flint glass used.
Pairing a crown lens with a flint lens reduced color fringing in a doublet, but the doublet focused light less strongly than the crown lens used alone.

Pairing a crown lens with a flint lens that bent light as strongly as the crown but spread colors only slightly more failed to correct fringing, whereas a flint whose bending power was similar but whose dispersion was far greater corrected it.
Pairing a crown lens with a second crown lens of the same glass reduced color fringing only when the second lens was shaped to cancel nearly all of the first lens's focusing power.
input.explanation: 오스트로프스키의 주장은 교정의 핵심이 전체 굴절력이 아니라 굴절력 대비 분산 비율이라는 것이다. C는 굴절력을 비슷하게 맞춘 채 분산만 바꿨을 때 분산이 큰 플린트만 교정에 성공했음을 보여 주므로 이 주장을 직접 지지한다. A는 분산과 관계없이 굴절력이 높은 플린트만으로 효과가 났다는 결과라서 오히려 주장을 약화시킨다. B는 이중렌즈의 초점력이 줄어든다는 사실만 보여 줄 뿐, 그 원인이 분산인지 굴절력인지 가려 주지 못한다. D는 같은 유리로는 초점력을 거의 다 없애야만 교정된다는 결과로 주장과 어울리긴 하지만, 플린트 유리의 분산이 원인이라는 점을 직접 검증하지는 않는다.
input.explanation_en: Ostrowski's claim is that what makes the correction work is flint glass's dispersion relative to its bending power, not its overall bending power. C keeps bending power about the same and changes only dispersion, and only the high-dispersion flint corrects the fringing, so it isolates exactly the factor she names. A says higher bending power reduced fringing no matter what the dispersion was, which actually points against her view. B only shows that the doublet focuses light less strongly, and it doesn't tell you whether dispersion or bending power is responsible. D fits her reasoning in a general way, but it involves only crown glass, so it never tests whether flint's dispersion is the cause.
input.design: To answer correctly, you have to separate the claimed cause (dispersion relative to bending power) from a competing one (overall bending power). A and B use real features of doublets, and D partly fits the reasoning, so each has to be compared against the controlled contrast in C before it can be ruled out.

input.passage:
When Louis XIV revoked the Edict of Nantes in 1685, he expected the decision to strengthen France by uniting its subjects under a single faith. Roughly 200,000 Huguenots, as French Protestants were called, instead fled the country despite laws forbidding their departure. Many settled in Protestant states such as the Dutch Republic, England, and Brandenburg-Prussia, where rulers welcomed them with tax exemptions and offers of citizenship.

Historians note that the refugees were not a random sample of the French population. Many were skilled silk weavers, watchmakers, printers, and merchants, and they brought trade techniques and commercial networks with them. In Berlin, Huguenot newcomers at one point made up about a fifth of the city's residents and helped establish industries that had barely existed there before. In this way, a policy meant to make France stronger ended up transferring valuable expertise to its rivals.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Louis XIV's 1685 decision prompted an exodus of skilled Protestants whose talents benefited the competing states that took them in.
Louis XIV's 1685 decision succeeded in uniting France under one faith because most Huguenots chose to leave rather than resist.
Louis XIV's 1685 decision was quickly reversed once Protestant rulers began offering tax exemptions to French refugees.
Louis XIV's 1685 decision mattered most for Berlin, which grew from a small town into a major capital because of Huguenot settlers.
input.explanation: 지문은 칙령 폐지로 숙련된 위그노들이 망명했고, 그들의 기술이 프랑스의 경쟁국들에 이익이 되어 정책 의도와 반대 결과가 났다는 것이 핵심이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 많은 위그노가 떠났다는 사실은 맞지만, 지문은 정책이 의도대로 성공했다고 보지 않고 역효과를 강조한다. C의 세금 면제는 지문에 나오지만, 칙령이 철회되었다는 내용은 없다. D는 베를린 사례를 다루지만 그것은 근거로 든 한 예시일 뿐이고, 작은 마을이 대도시로 성장했다는 주장도 지문에 없다.
input.explanation_en: The text explains that revoking the edict drove skilled Huguenots abroad, and that their expertise ended up strengthening France's rivals, the opposite of what Louis XIV intended. That makes A the answer. B gets right that many Huguenots left, but the text treats the policy as backfiring, not succeeding. C mentions the tax exemptions from the text, but nothing says the decision was reversed. D focuses on Berlin, which is only one supporting example, and the text never says Berlin grew from a small town into a major capital.
input.design: 정답은 두 단락(망명+숙련 기술→경쟁국 이익)을 연결해야 하며, 오답 B·C·D는 지문의 실제 세부(대규모 이주, 세금 면제, 베를린)를 끌어와 부분적으로 맞아 보이게 했다.

input.passage: Flying buttresses, the external stone arms that brace the upper walls of Gothic cathedrals, are usually explained as a structural necessity: by carrying the outward thrust of high vaults away from the walls, they allowed builders to open those walls with vast windows. Architectural historian Lena Marchetti argues that this account is incomplete. In her view, masons at some cathedrals elaborated buttresses beyond what stability required, treating them as a visible expression of the building's aspirations rather than merely as hidden engineering. If Marchetti is right, at least some buttresses should show design choices that cannot be explained by load-bearing demands alone.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marchetti's argument?
options: Structural modeling of several cathedrals shows that their buttresses carry pinnacles and carved tracery adding weight well beyond what is needed to counter vault thrust, placed mainly on facades facing the town's main approach.
Structural modeling of several cathedrals shows that their buttresses carry pinnacles whose added weight is precisely what is needed to redirect vault thrust safely down into the foundations.
Structural modeling of several cathedrals shows that their buttresses were enlarged after early cracks appeared in the upper walls, allowing the builders to install larger stained-glass windows.

Structural modeling of several cathedrals shows that their buttresses were often hidden from street view by surrounding buildings, though contemporary writers praised the cathedrals' soaring interiors.
input.explanation: 마르케티의 주장은 일부 버트레스가 하중 지지만으로는 설명되지 않는 설계 선택, 즉 미적·상징적 표현을 보여준다는 것이다. A는 장식이 구조적 필요를 넘어서고, 그 장식이 사람들 눈에 가장 잘 띄는 정면에 집중되어 있음을 보여 주므로 두 조건을 모두 충족한다. B는 피너클이 언급되지만 그 무게가 정확히 구조적 필요에 맞으므로 오히려 전통적 설명을 뒷받침한다. C는 큰 창을 위한 구조적 보강일 뿐 표현적 의도를 보여 주지 않는다. D는 버트레스가 보이지 않았다는 내용이어서 '눈에 보이는 표현'이라는 주장과 어긋난다.
input.explanation_en: Marchetti claims that some buttresses show design choices that load-bearing demands alone can't explain, meaning they were visible expressions and not just engineering. A gives you both pieces: decoration that goes beyond what the structure needs, concentrated on the facades people would see most. B also mentions pinnacles, but their weight matches the structural need exactly, so it actually backs the traditional explanation. C describes reinforcement that made bigger windows possible, which is a purely structural reason. D says the buttresses were often hidden from view, which works against the idea that they were meant as visible expression.
input.design: Distractors share A's sentence frame and use features like pinnacles and windows, so students have to check two things at once: whether the feature goes beyond structural need and whether it was made to be seen.

input.passage:
Text 1
Perovskite solar cells built from mixed halide crystals let engineers tune the bandgap simply by swapping iodide for bromide. Because laboratory measurements show that a cell's bandgap shifts smoothly and predictably as the bromide fraction rises, and because that bandgap stays fixed once the film is made, researchers can choose a single mixed composition matched to the upper layer of a tandem cell. Such compositions, the author concludes, offer a straightforward route toward record photovoltaic efficiency.

Text 2
When materials scientist Lena Okafor shone continuous light on mixed iodide-bromide perovskite films, she found that within minutes the halide ions migrated and separated into iodide-rich and bromide-rich pockets. The iodide-rich regions, which have a narrower bandgap, trapped charge carriers, so the voltage the film produced fell well below what its initial measured bandgap predicted. The effect largely reversed when the films were kept in the dark.
input.question: Based on the texts, which part of Text 1's reasoning would the author of Text 2 most likely challenge?
options: The claim that mixed halide compositions offer a straightforward route toward record photovoltaic efficiency
The claim that mixed halide cells are suited for use in the upper layer of a tandem cell
The claim that the bandgap measured in the laboratory shifts as the bromide fraction rises
The claim that a film's bandgap remains unchanged once the film has been made
input.explanation:
정답 D: Text 1의 결론은 '조성을 한 번 정하면 밴드갭이 고정된다'는 가정에 기대고 있다. Text 2는 빛을 받으면 할라이드가 분리되면서 실제 유효 밴드갭이 바뀐다는 관찰을 내놓아 바로 이 가정을 겨냥한다.
A: 결론 자체에 해당한다. Text 2가 이 결론을 약하게 만드는 것은 맞지만, 직접 공격하는 대상은 결론이 아니라 결론을 받치는 가정이다.
B: 탠덤 셀 상층에 쓴다는 것은 Text 1의 부수적인 세부일 뿐이며, Text 2는 이 점을 다루지 않는다.
C: Text 2는 처음 측정한 밴드갭이 조성에 따라 달라진다는 점을 전제로 삼고 있으므로 오히려 이 부분에 동의한다.
input.explanation_en:
D is correct. Text 1's conclusion depends on the assumption that a film's bandgap stays fixed once the film is made. Text 2 shows that under light the halides separate, so the film's effective bandgap changes. That observation targets this assumption directly.
A is the conclusion itself. Text 2 does weaken it, but only indirectly, by undermining the assumption it rests on.
B is a side detail about tandem cells, and Text 2 never addresses it.
C is something Text 2 actually accepts: it relies on the idea that the initially measured bandgap depends on composition.
input.design: Text 1의 결론은 '밴드갭은 만든 뒤에 고정된다'는 숨은 가정에 기대고, Text 2는 빛을 받으면 상이 분리된다는 관찰로 그 가정을 무너뜨린다. 오답은 결론 자체(A), 부수 세부(B), Text 2가 동의하는 부분(C)으로 구성했고, 네 선택지 모두 같은 'The claim that…' 틀로 썼다.

input.passage: When a small group of Irish nationalists seized buildings in Dublin during Easter week of 1916, most Dubliners regarded the rebellion as a reckless failure: it was crushed within six days, and some residents jeered at captured rebels as they were marched through the streets. __Over the following weeks, however, British authorities court-martialed and executed fifteen of the rising's leaders, often after secret proceedings that newspapers described in grim detail.__ Public sympathy shifted sharply toward the executed men, and in the 1918 general election the separatist party Sinn Féin, which had played little role in the rising itself, won a large majority of Ireland's seats. Historians therefore argue that the rising's influence on the push for Irish independence came less from the rebellion than from the response it provoked.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces the development that connects the rising's initial unpopularity to the later change in public opinion, which in turn supports the historians' claim about where the rising's influence came from.
It explains why the rising was crushed so quickly, which accounts for the scorn that Dubliners initially showed the rebels.
It presents the electoral success of Sinn Féin as evidence that the executions directly benefited the party that organized the rising.
It states the main argument of the text, which the account of the 1918 election then illustrates with a specific example.
input.explanation: 정답 A: 밑줄 문장(처형)은 '반란이 처음엔 비웃음을 샀다'와 '여론이 바뀌어 1918년 선거에서 승리했다'를 이어 주는 연결 고리이다. 이 연결이 다시 '영향력은 반란 자체보다 그에 대한 대응에서 나왔다'는 결론을 뒷받침한다. 즉 두 단계를 거치는 역할이다. B: 앞 문장과만 연결한 한 단계짜리 해석이다. 처형은 진압이 끝난 뒤의 일이라 진압이 빨랐던 이유를 설명하지 않는다. C: 다음 문장(선거)의 역할과 헷갈린 것이다. 게다가 지문에 따르면 Sinn Féin은 봉기에서 한 역할이 거의 없었으므로 '봉기를 조직한 정당'이라는 설명도 틀렸다. D: 지문 전체의 목적과 이 문장 하나의 기능을 뒤바꾼 것이다. 핵심 주장은 마지막 문장에 나오고, 밑줄 문장은 그 주장을 받쳐 주는 사건일 뿐이다.
input.explanation_en:
Choice A is correct. The underlined sentence describes the executions, and they're the link between two things: the rising's early unpopularity (people jeered at the rebels) and the later shift in public sympathy that led to Sinn Féin's 1918 victory. That chain then supports the final claim that the rising mattered mainly because of the response it provoked. To see this role, you have to connect two steps.

Choice B only looks one step back. The executions happened after the rising had already been crushed, so they can't explain why it was crushed so quickly.

Choice C mixes up the underlined sentence with the next sentence, which is the one about the election. It also contradicts the text: Sinn Féin "played little role in the rising itself," so it didn't organize it.

Choice D confuses the text's overall purpose with the job of this one sentence. The main argument comes in the last sentence. The underlined sentence gives an event that supports that argument.
input.design: I built a chain of four parts: early scorn → executions (underlined) → shift in opinion and the election → the historians' conclusion. The correct answer requires connecting two links. The wrong answers are B, a role based on only one step; C, confusion with the neighboring sentence; and D, a swap between the text's overall purpose and this sentence's function.

input.passage: In the 1830s, the silk weavers of Lyon, known as canuts, worked mostly in small household workshops, where a master weaver owned a few looms and hired journeymen. After the canuts staged major uprisings in 1831 and 1834 over the low piece rates paid by silk merchants, the industry gradually shifted toward rural factories filled with mechanized looms. Some economic historians argue that the strikes themselves drove this shift: by this account, merchants who had experienced repeated work stoppages in the city deliberately moved production to places where they could control a workforce more directly, even though mechanized looms in that era were not clearly cheaper to run than urban hand weaving.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the economic historians' argument?
options: Mechanized looms installed in rural factories during the 1840s produced plain silk cloth at a substantially lower cost per meter than hand looms operated in Lyon's household workshops.
Merchants' letters from the 1840s show that firms whose Lyon workshops had halted during the 1831 and 1834 uprisings opened rural factories at higher rates than firms that had faced no stoppages.
Records show that the number of household workshops in Lyon fell steadily throughout the 1850s and 1860s, while the number of rural silk factories in the surrounding region rose.
Several canuts who took part in the 1834 uprising later took jobs in rural silk factories, where they reported earning piece rates similar to those they had received in Lyon.
input.design: 정답은 파업 경험과 공장 이전을 직접 연결하는 비교 증거이고, 오답은 비용 설명(대안 가설), 단순 추세, 노동자 이동 등 부분적으로 관련된 사실로 구성했다.
input.explanation: 이 주장의 핵심은 merchants가 파업을 겪었기 때문에 직접 통제하려고 일부러 농촌 공장으로 생산을 옮겼다는 인과관계이다. B는 봉기 때 작업 중단을 겪은 회사가 그렇지 않은 회사보다 농촌 공장을 더 많이 열었다는 내용이므로 파업 경험과 이전을 직접 연결해 주장을 뒷받침한다. A는 기계화가 더 싸서 이전했다는 대안 설명을 제시하므로 오히려 주장을 약화시킨다. C는 이 전환이 일어났다는 사실만 보여 줄 뿐, 원인이 파업이었다는 것은 보여 주지 못한다. D는 노동자들의 이후 행적과 임금에 관한 내용이라 merchants의 동기와는 관련이 없다.
input.explanation_en: The argument is a cause-and-effect claim: merchants moved production to rural factories because they had lived through strikes and wanted more direct control. B links the two directly, since firms whose workshops were shut down during the uprisings opened rural factories more often than firms with no stoppages, so B supports the argument. A gives another explanation, lower costs, which cuts against the claim that cost wasn't what drove the shift. C only shows that the shift happened. It doesn't show that strikes caused it. D is about what workers did and earned later, so it tells you nothing about why the merchants acted.

input.passage: In the early fourteenth century, serious literature in Italy was expected to be written in Latin, the language of the Church, the universities, and classical authors such as Virgil. Dante Alighieri nonetheless composed the Divine Comedy in the Florentine vernacular. Some scholars have read this choice as a simple bid for a wider audience, since far more people could follow Tuscan speech than Latin. __Yet Dante had already argued, in his unfinished treatise De vulgari eloquentia, that the vernacular was nobler than Latin because it was learned naturally rather than through rules imposed by schooling.__ Seen in light of that earlier claim, the poem's language looks less like a concession to ordinary readers than a deliberate assertion that a living tongue could carry the weight of theology and philosophy once reserved for Latin.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that Dante's vernacular poem in fact reached a larger audience than Latin works of the period did.
It states the text's main conclusion that Dante's language choice was a challenge to Latin's literary authority.
It describes the cultural expectation that the Divine Comedy departed from, showing how unusual Dante's decision was.
It introduces a view Dante held earlier, which the text uses to complicate one interpretation and support a different one.
input.explanation:
정답 D: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 앞의 '독자층 확대' 해석에 제동을 걸고, 『속어론』에서 Dante가 이전에 밝힌 견해를 제시한다. 마지막 문장은 이 견해를 근거로 삼아 다른 해석(라틴어 권위에 대한 의도적 도전)을 내놓는다. 즉 앞 해석을 흔드는 것과 결론을 뒷받침하는 것, 두 단계를 잇는 역할이다.
A(한 단계만 본 역할/오독): 이 문장은 실제 독자 수에 대한 증거가 아니다. 오히려 '더 많은 독자'라는 해석과 거리를 두려고 쓰였다.
B(전체 목적과 문장 기능을 뒤바꿈): 라틴어 권위에 도전했다는 결론은 마지막 문장에서 나온다. 밑줄 문장은 그 결론의 근거일 뿐이다.
C(인접 문장과 혼동): 라틴어가 당연시되던 관습을 설명하는 것은 첫 문장의 역할이다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer, D: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet," which pushes back on the reading that Dante just wanted a wider audience. It then brings in a view Dante had stated earlier, in De vulgari eloquentia. The last sentence uses that earlier view as grounds for a different reading: Dante was deliberately challenging Latin's authority. So the sentence does two linked jobs. It weakens one interpretation and supports another.
A is wrong because the sentence gives no evidence about how many people actually read the poem. In fact, it moves the argument away from the audience explanation.
B is wrong because it mixes up the text's overall conclusion with this sentence's job. The conclusion comes in the final sentence. The underlined sentence only provides the basis for it.
C is wrong because explaining the expectation that serious literature be written in Latin is what the first sentence does, not the underlined one.
input.design: 이 문항은 해석 제시→단서 제시→재해석으로 이어지는 흐름으로 짰다. 정답을 고르려면 밑줄 문장이 앞 해석을 흔드는 동시에 뒤 결론을 받친다는 두 단계를 함께 봐야 한다. 오답은 지시대로 세 가지로 구성했다: 한 단계만 본 역할(A), 전체 결론과 문장 기능을 뒤바꾼 것(B), 인접한 첫 문장의 역할과 혼동한 것(C).

input.passage:
Text 1
Historians often credit the collapse of the British railway share mania of the mid-1840s with prompting new rules for protecting investors. But an account of why a regulation emerged is persuasive, I would argue, only if it can show that lawmakers' own records connect the rule to the crisis; a rule that merely follows a crash in time, without such documented links, may have been driven by older concerns that the crash simply made convenient to cite.

Text 2
In 1844 and 1845, speculators poured money into hundreds of proposed railway companies, many of which never laid a mile of track. When share prices fell sharply in 1847, thousands of small investors were ruined. Within a few years, Parliament had tightened requirements for company accounts and audits. The sequence makes clear that the mania's collapse was what produced Britain's early investor protection laws.
input.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the conclusion presented in Text 2?
options: As well supported, since Text 2 shows that the losses suffered by thousands of small investors were severe enough to demand a legislative remedy
As partly supported, since the short interval between the 1847 price collapse and the new accounting requirements counts as some evidence of a documented link
As insufficiently supported, since Text 2 relies on the order of events without citing any evidence of what motivated the lawmakers who passed the rules
As doubtful, since financial regulations are usually written long before a crisis occurs and are rarely changed quickly in response to one
input.explanation:
Text 1의 저자는 규제가 생겨난 이유에 대한 설명이 설득력을 가지려면 입법자들의 기록이 규제를 위기와 연결해 보여야 한다는 기준을 제시한다. 시간상 뒤따랐다는 것만으로는 부족하다는 것이다. Text 2는 "The sequence makes clear"라고 하며 사건의 순서에만 기대어 결론을 내리므로, Text 1의 기준에서는 근거가 부족하다(C).
A: Text 2 자신의 기준(피해가 컸다는 점)으로 평가한 것이다. 피해 규모는 입법 동기를 기록으로 증명하지 못한다.
B: 두 저자의 기준을 섞은 것이다. 시간 간격이 짧다는 점을 기록상 연결의 일부로 쳐주지만, Text 1은 시간상 선후 관계를 기록 증거로 명시적으로 인정하지 않는다.
D: 지문과 관계없는 일반 통념이다. Text 1은 규제가 위기에 반응해 생길 수 있음을 부정하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en:
Text 1's author sets a standard: an explanation of why a regulation emerged is persuasive only if the lawmakers' own records tie the rule to the crisis. A rule that simply comes after a crash doesn't meet that standard. Text 2 bases its conclusion on sequence alone ("The sequence makes clear"), so by Text 1's standard it is insufficiently supported. That makes C correct.
A judges the conclusion by Text 2's own reasoning, that the losses were severe. But severe losses don't show what actually motivated the lawmakers.
B mixes the two authors' standards. It counts the short time gap as partial evidence of a documented link, but Text 1 explicitly rejects timing as a substitute for records.
D relies on a general assumption that isn't in the texts. Text 1 never says regulations can't respond quickly to crises.
input.design: Text 1 sets a criterion (an explanation needs documented lawmaker motives, not just timing). Text 2 concludes from sequence alone. The wrong answers apply Text 2's own criterion (A), a blend of the two criteria (B), and general assumptions (D).

input.passage: By the fourteenth century, merchants of the Hanseatic League had developed a remarkably consistent method for evaluating wool shipped through their trading posts. The grading system used by Hanseatic agents in Bruges, which sorted bales of English and Flemish wool into ranked classes according to fiber length, cleanliness, and color, ______ buyers in distant ports such as Novgorod and Riga to purchase shipments without inspecting them in person.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: allowing
were allowing
have allowed
allowed
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The grading system'이고, 'used by ... Bruges'와 'which ... color' 수식어구 뒤에 이 주어의 정동사가 와야 한다. 그리고 지문 전체가 14세기 과거 상황을 서술하므로 단수 주어와 맞는 과거형 정동사 D 'allowed'가 정답이다. A 'allowing'은 분사라서 정동사가 아니므로 문장이 완성되지 않는다. B 'were allowing'은 과거 시제는 맞지만 가까이 있는 복수 명사(bales, classes)에 끌린 복수형이라 단수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C 'have allowed'는 복수형이고 현재완료라서 수 일치와 시제가 모두 틀렸다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The grading system." It is followed by two long modifiers ("used by ... Bruges" and "which ... color"), and only after them does the main verb appear. The passage describes the fourteenth century, so the blank needs a singular, past-tense main verb, and that is D, "allowed." A, "allowing," is a participle, not a main verb, so the sentence would be incomplete. B, "were allowing," is in the past tense, but it is plural, probably pulled toward nearby plural nouns like "bales" and "classes," so it doesn't agree with the singular subject. C, "have allowed," is wrong twice: it is plural and in the present perfect, so neither its number nor its tense fits.
input.design: 긴 수식어구 사이에 복수 명사를 넣어 훑어 읽으면 B를 고르게 했다. 비교해야 배제되는 오답은 B(시제는 맞고 수가 틀림)와 C(그럴듯한 정동사)이고, A는 분사로 만든 함정이다.

input.passage: In Edo-period Japan, ukiyo-e prints were produced through a division of labor among several specialists. A designer drew the image on thin paper, a carver pasted that drawing onto a cherry-wood block and cut away everything but the lines, and a printer ______ successive blocks with pigment to build up color one layer at a time. The resulting images of kabuki actors and courtesans from the Yoshiwara pleasure quarter could be sold cheaply in large numbers.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: inking
inked
who inked
having inked
input.explanation: 이 문장은 "A designer drew..., a carver pasted... and cut..., and a printer ___" 형태로 독립절 세 개가 병렬로 이어진다. 세 번째 절의 주어 "a printer"에도 앞의 drew, pasted와 같은 과거형 정동사가 필요하므로 B "inked"가 정답이다. A "inking"과 D "having inked"는 분사여서 세 번째 절에 정동사가 없게 된다. C "who inked"는 "a printer"를 꾸미는 관계절이 되어, 역시 세 번째 절에 주절 동사가 남지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: This sentence links three independent clauses in parallel: "A designer drew..., a carver pasted... and cut..., and a printer ___." The third clause has its own subject, "a printer," so it needs a past-tense main verb that matches drew and pasted. That's why B, "inked," is correct. A, "inking," and D, "having inked," are participles, so the third clause would have no main verb. C, "who inked," turns the words after "a printer" into a relative clause that just describes the printer, which also leaves the third clause without a main verb.
input.design: 이 문항은 긴 병렬 구조 안에서 세 번째 절에 정동사가 필요하다는 점을 알아보게 하는 문제다. 분사(A, D)와 관계절(C)은 동사처럼 보이기 때문에, 문장을 훑어 읽기만 하면 맞는 답처럼 느껴진다.

input.passage: Ionic liquids—salts that remain liquid near room temperature—are attractive battery electrolytes because they resist breaking down at the high voltages that would decompose conventional solvents. Their drawback is that their ions tend to cling together in tightly bound cation-anion pairs, and a bound pair is electrically neutral, so it carries no net charge toward either electrode. Chemist Lena Marwick and colleagues modified a common ionic liquid by attaching a bulky side group to its cation, which keeps the anion from approaching closely. Compared with the unmodified liquid, the modified version showed a markedly higher fraction of free, unpaired ions, while its resistance to decomposition at high voltage was unchanged. If the free-ion measurements are accurate, the researchers' findings suggest that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the modified liquid would tolerate higher voltages than the unmodified liquid, since the bulky side group shields the ions from breaking down.
the modified liquid should conduct current more effectively than the unmodified liquid without giving up the voltage stability that makes ionic liquids useful.
the modified liquid would conduct current less effectively than the unmodified liquid, since bulky cations are likely to move more slowly through the electrolyte.
the modified liquid should replace conventional solvents in all batteries, since ion pairing was the only obstacle to using ionic liquids as electrolytes.
input.explanation: 지문은 결합된 이온쌍은 중성이라 전하를 운반하지 못한다고 설명하므로, 자유 이온 비율이 높아지면 전도성이 향상될 것으로 추론된다. 또 고전압 분해 저항은 변하지 않았다고 했으므로 B가 두 정보를 모두 연결한다. A는 전압 안정성이 '변하지 않았다'는 진술과 모순된다. C는 큰 양이온이 느리게 움직일 수 있다는 그럴듯한 추론이지만 지문은 이동 속도에 대해 아무 정보도 주지 않으며, 자유 이온 증가라는 핵심 근거를 무시한다. D는 이온쌍 형성이 유일한 장애라거나 모든 배터리에 적용된다는, 지문이 뒷받침하지 않는 과도한 일반화이다.
input.explanation_en: The passage says bound ion pairs are neutral and carry no charge, so a higher fraction of free ions should mean better conduction. It also says high-voltage stability was unchanged, so B links both facts correctly. A contradicts the statement that decomposition resistance did not change. C sounds reasonable because bulky ions might move slowly, but the passage says nothing about ion speed, and C ignores the key evidence about free ions. D overgeneralizes: the passage never says ion pairing is the only obstacle or that the liquid suits all batteries.
input.design: 이온쌍 중성성→전도성 추론과 전압 안정성 불변 정보를 연결해야 정답이 나오도록 했고, 오답은 한쪽 정보만 쓰거나 외부 가정을 끌어오거나 과잉 일반화하는 방식으로 구성했다.

input.passage: In the early 1920s, Arnold Schoenberg devised a method for organizing atonal music: a composer arranges all twelve pitches of the chromatic scale into a fixed order, called a row, and no pitch may recur until the other eleven have sounded. Because every pitch appears equally often, no single note can emerge as a "home" tone the way the tonic does in a major or minor key. Some critics have argued that Schoenberg's real goal was to make his music sound as random as possible. Yet Schoenberg insisted that every melody and chord in a piece be derived from its row, so that even passages that seem unrelated share the same underlying intervals. Taken together, these features suggest that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the method was meant to replace the unity once supplied by a home key with a different source of coherence, not to abandon coherence altogether.
the method was meant to give one carefully chosen pitch the central role that the tonic had played, so that listeners could still sense a home tone.
the method was meant to free composers from any fixed ordering of pitches, so that each passage could be written independently of the others.
the method was meant to make pieces sound random to listeners, since equal use of all twelve pitches prevents any note from standing out.
input.design: 두 정보(조성 중심 제거 + 모든 소재를 음렬에서 파생)를 연결해야 결론이 나온다. D는 비평가 주장과 첫 정보에 부분적으로 맞고, B·C는 지문 일부 표현을 왜곡해 비교가 필요하다.
input.explanation: 지문은 음렬 기법이 '중심음'을 없앤다는 점과, 모든 선율·화음이 음렬에서 파생되어 공통 음정을 공유한다는 점을 제시하므로, 조성을 대신하는 새로운 통일성의 원천을 만든 것이라는 A가 결론으로 가장 적절하다. D는 첫 번째 정보와 비평가의 주장에는 맞지만, 'Yet'으로 시작하는 문장이 바로 그 무작위성 해석을 반박하므로 틀리다. B는 조성의 역할을 언급하지만, 모든 음이 똑같이 자주 나와 중심음이 생길 수 없다는 지문 내용과 모순된다. C는 고정된 음 순서와 모든 악절이 음렬에서 파생된다는 점 모두와 정면으로 충돌한다.
input.explanation_en: The passage gives two facts: the row keeps any pitch from acting as a home tone, and every melody and chord comes from the row, so they all share the same intervals. Put together, these support A: the row takes over the unifying job the home key used to do. D matches the first fact and the critics' view, but the sentence beginning with "Yet" pushes back against that randomness reading, so D is wrong. B mentions the tonic's role, but it contradicts the passage, which says every pitch appears equally often, so no home tone can emerge. C conflicts with both the fixed order of the row and the rule that every passage comes from it.

content.text: Design: subject-verb agreement after long modifier. Subject "The central claim... " singular? Let's do: "The idea that newcomers learn by gradually moving from peripheral to full participation in communities of practice, rather than by absorbing abstract knowledge in classrooms, ______ much of Lave and Wenger's 1991 study." Options: A) have shaped (plural agreement with "communities/classrooms"), B) shaping (participle, no main verb), C) shaped (correct, past singular-neutral... past tense works for any number — too easy?). Better: C "underpins" singular present vs A "underpin", B "underpinning", D "having underpinned". Context: present tense fine.

input.passage: In their 1991 book Situated Learning, anthropologist Jean Lave and computer scientist Etienne Wenger examined apprenticeships among Yucatec midwives, Liberian tailors, and navy quartermasters. The notion that newcomers acquire expertise by moving gradually from peripheral tasks toward full participation in communities of practice, rather than by absorbing abstract rules in classrooms, ______ much of the later research on how knowledge is transferred in workplaces.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: underpin
underpinning
underpins
having underpinned
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The notion'이고, 뒤에 이어지는 that절과 'rather than' 구는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어에 맞는 정동사가 필요하므로 C(underpins)가 정답이다. A는 정동사이긴 하지만 빈칸 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'classrooms'나 'communities'에 맞춘 복수형이라 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. B와 D는 분사 형태여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되므로 완전한 문장이 되지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The notion." The that-clause and the "rather than" phrase after it only modify that subject. So the blank needs a main verb that agrees with a singular subject, which makes C ("underpins") correct. A is a main verb, but it's plural, so it matches nearby nouns like "classrooms" or "communities" instead of the actual subject. B and D are participle forms, which would leave the sentence with no main verb at all.
input.design: 긴 that절과 rather than 구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어, 동사 바로 앞의 복수 명사에 맞추도록 유도한다. 학생은 진짜 주어를 찾고(1단계), 정동사가 필요한지 판단해야(2단계) 정답을 고를 수 있다.

input.passage: By the fifteenth century, the Arsenal of Venice employed thousands of workers to build the city's war galleys. Instead of having one crew construct a ship from keel to rigging, the Arsenal kept standardized hulls moving along a canal, past warehouses where specialized teams added oars, weapons, and provisions in sequence. Historians often credit this arrangement with the Arsenal's famous speed: in 1574, workers reportedly assembled a complete galley in a single day. Yet economic historian Frederic Lane noted that the Arsenal also stockpiled prefabricated parts for years in advance, storing hundreds of interchangeable hulls and fittings so that a fleet could be outfitted quickly in a crisis. Because a one-day galley depended on components that had already taken months of labor to produce, the 1574 feat suggests that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the Arsenal's rapid output reflected advance preparation of parts as much as the sequential arrangement of final assembly.
the Arsenal's rapid output reflected the sequential arrangement of final assembly more than any advance preparation of parts.
the Arsenal's rapid output reflected a shortage of skilled workers rather than the advance preparation of parts.
the Arsenal's rapid output reflected a decline in the quality of galleys rather than the sequential arrangement of final assembly.
input.design: 순차 조립 설명과 Lane의 사전 비축 증거라는 두 정보를 연결해야 하며, 오답 B는 지문 앞부분의 통념만 훑은 독자를 노리고 C·D는 같은 문장 틀에 지문에서 뒷받침되지 않는 요인을 넣었다.
input.explanation: 지문은 처음에 순차 조립 방식이 속도를 냈다는 통념을 소개한 뒤, Lane이 지적한 부품 사전 비축을 덧붙이고 하루 만의 건조가 이미 몇 달의 노동이 들어간 부품에 의존했다고 말한다. 따라서 그 속도는 조립 방식만큼이나 사전 준비 덕분이었다는 A가 논리적인 결론이다. B는 지문 앞부분의 통념만 반영하고 Lane의 반론을 무시한다. C는 숙련공 부족을 언급하지만 지문은 수천 명의 전문 인력을 묘사한다. D의 품질 저하는 지문 어디에도 근거가 없다.
input.explanation_en: The passage first gives the common view that sequential assembly explains the Arsenal's speed. Then it adds Lane's point that parts were stockpiled ahead of time, and it notes that the one-day galley depended on components that had already taken months to make. That makes A the logical conclusion: the speed came from advance preparation as much as from how final assembly was arranged. B repeats only the common view from the start of the passage and ignores Lane's counterpoint. C mentions a shortage of skilled workers, but the passage describes thousands of specialized workers. D's claim that quality declined has no support anywhere in the passage.

input.passage: For centuries, Antwerp's diamond cutters passed their techniques from master to apprentice within tightly organized guilds, and much of that knowledge was never written down. Economic historians argue that this tacit expertise helped the city ______ its lead in gemstone processing: even when rival centers gained access to the same rough stones and similar tools, they struggled to match the precision of Antwerp's polished diamonds, because the skills themselves could not easily be copied or exported.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: establish
advertise
surrender
sustain
input.explanation: 지문은 경쟁 도시들이 같은 원석과 도구를 얻은 '뒤에도' 안트베르펜의 정밀함을 따라잡지 못했다고 하므로, 이미 가진 우위를 계속 '유지하다'는 뜻의 D(sustain)가 정답이다. A(establish)는 우위와 관련은 있지만 처음 '확립'하는 것을 뜻하고, 지문은 경쟁이 생긴 뒤의 지속을 강조한다. B(advertise)는 명성과 관련된 듯 보이지만 지문은 홍보가 아니라 모방하기 어려운 기술 이야기다. C(surrender)는 우위를 '포기하다'라는 뜻이라 지문 논리와 정반대다.
input.explanation_en: The text says rival centers still couldn't match Antwerp's precision even after they got the same stones and tools, so the tacit skills helped the city keep a lead it already had. That makes D ("sustain") the answer. A ("establish") is about advantage too, but it means creating the lead in the first place, while the text is about the lead lasting once competition showed up. B ("advertise") might seem to fit because of reputation, but the passage is about skills that are hard to copy, not about promotion. C ("surrender") means giving up the lead, which is the opposite of what the passage describes.
input.design: 오답 A·B가 '우위'와 부분적으로 연결되지만, 경쟁자 등장 '이후에도'라는 시간적 단서와 연결해야 지속의 의미가 확정되도록 했다.

input.passage: In the early nineteenth century, the Russian-American Company and Britain's Hudson's Bay Company (HBC) competed for furs along the Pacific coast of North America. Some historians argue that the HBC prevailed not because it paid trappers more but because of its supply network: by moving goods overland and by sea from its own depots, the HBC could keep Indigenous trading partners reliably stocked with blankets, tools, and food, while Russian posts depended on irregular shipments from distant Siberian ports. According to this view, trappers chose the HBC because it was dependable, not because its prices were better.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' argument?
options: Records from several coastal posts show that the HBC paid trappers noticeably more goods per pelt than Russian posts did during the years when its share of the trade grew fastest.
