Records from several coastal posts show that trappers moved their pelts to the HBC in years when Russian supply ships arrived late, even though the two companies paid about the same amount of goods per pelt.
Records from several coastal posts show that Russian posts received shipments from Siberia only once or twice a year, a schedule that remained unchanged throughout the period.
Records from several coastal posts show that the HBC built more depots along the coast than the Russian-American Company did, though most of those depots opened after the competition had ended.
input.explanation: 역사가들의 주장은 두 가지예요. 공급이 믿을 만했기 때문에 HBC가 이겼고, 가격 때문은 아니었다는 것이죠. B는 러시아 보급이 늦어진 해에 사냥꾼들이 HBC로 옮겨 갔고, 그 해 두 회사의 지불 가격이 비슷했다는 내용이라 두 부분을 모두 뒷받침해요. A는 더 높은 가격이 원인일 수 있다고 보여 주므로 오히려 주장을 약화해요. C는 러시아 보급이 불규칙했다는 배경만 확인할 뿐, 사냥꾼들의 선택과는 연결되지 않아요. D는 HBC의 보급망을 다루지만, 거점 대부분이 경쟁이 끝난 뒤에 생겼기 때문에 HBC의 승리를 설명할 수 없어요.
input.explanation_en: The historians make two claims: the HBC won because its supply was dependable, and its prices were not the reason. Choice B supports both parts. Trappers moved to the HBC in the years when Russian supply ships arrived late, and the two companies paid about the same per pelt, so price can't explain the switch. Choice A points to higher pay as the cause, which actually weakens the argument. Choice C only confirms that Russian shipments were infrequent, without connecting that to what trappers chose. Choice D is about the HBC's network, but most of those depots opened after the competition had ended, so they couldn't explain how the HBC won.
input.design: This is a two-step judgment: the reader must check both the supply-reliability claim and the rejection of price as the cause. C and D each match part of the argument but still fail on closer reading: C never links supply problems to trappers' choices, and D's depots came after the competition ended.

input.passage: In Discipline and Punish (1975), Michel Foucault argued that Jeremy Bentham's Panopticon, a circular prison in which a single guard tower overlooks every cell, was less important as a building than as a model of modern power. Because inmates could never confirm whether the tower was occupied at any given moment, they had to assume constant observation. The result, Foucault contended, was a shift in where control was ______ prisoners gradually took on the guard's gaze and began policing their own behavior.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: located, the
located: the
located the
located, and that the
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The result ... was a shift in where control was located"는 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 "the prisoners gradually took on..."도 독립절이며 '변화'의 구체적 내용을 설명한다. 따라서 앞 절을 부연 설명하는 두 독립절을 연결하는 콜론을 쓴 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 연결 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 이어 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 "and that"이 앞 문장에 "that"절이 없는데도 병렬 구조처럼 보이게 만들어 문법적으로 맞지 않고, 의미상으로도 '변화'의 내용을 설명하는 관계가 사라진다.
input.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "The result ... was a shift in where control was located," make up a complete independent clause, and "the prisoners gradually took on..." is another independent clause that explains what that shift was. A colon is the right way to join a clause to a second clause that explains it, so B is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, so it creates a comma splice. C runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds "and that," which sets up a parallel "that" clause even though no earlier "that" clause exists, so the sentence breaks down grammatically and loses the explanatory link.
input.design: 빈칸 앞 절이 'where control was located'라는 내포절을 포함해 끝이 모호하게 보이도록 했고, 앞뒤가 모두 완전한 절인지 확인한 뒤 그 관계가 설명적인지도 따져야 답을 고를 수 있다. 오답인 쉼표 연결, 무종지문, 가짜 병렬 구조는 모두 같은 틀로 만들었다.

content.text:
Design: a long appositive with internal commas, after the subject, then main verb... Let's build an independent clause + long modifier + boundary.

Passage: "Lead-free solders such as SAC305, an alloy of tin, silver, and copper adopted after restrictions on lead in electronics, behave differently from older tin-lead solders under thermal cycling. As a circuit board repeatedly heats and cools, mismatched expansion between the chip and the board strains each joint______ microscopic cracks typically initiate near the brittle intermetallic layer at the joint's interface, where the coarsening tin grains concentrate stress."

Correct B: "joint; over hundreds of cycles," — the blank is after "joint". Options: A "joint, over hundreds of cycles," (comma splice) B "joint; over hundreds of cycles," C "joint; over hundreds of cycles" (missing comma after intro phrase—acceptable? that's arguably fine in Standard English... risky). Better make options differ in boundary: A "joint, over hundreds of cycles," B "joint. Over hundreds of cycles," C "joint over hundreds of cycles," D "joint, and over hundreds of cycles". D: missing comma after phrase not strictly error... SAT treats "and over hundreds of cycles microscopic..." — ambiguous. Make D "joint and, over hundreds of cycles," — that's actually correct-ish? "strains each joint and, over hundreds of cycles, microscopic cracks initiate" — compound clauses without comma before and; SAT generally accepts? Risky. Use D: "joint: over hundreds of cycles" without closing comma? Hmm. Use D "joint, over hundreds of cycles;" — wrong semicolon placement. Good.

input.passage: Lead-free solders such as SAC305, an alloy of tin, silver, and copper widely adopted after restrictions on lead in electronics, respond differently than older tin-lead solders to thermal cycling. As a circuit board repeatedly heats and cools, the mismatched expansion of the chip and the board strains each solder ______ microscopic cracks typically initiate near the brittle intermetallic layer at the joint's interface, where coarsening tin grains concentrate stress.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: joint, over hundreds of cycles,
joint. Over hundreds of cycles,
joint over hundreds of cycles,
joint, over hundreds of cycles;
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "As a circuit board ... strains each solder joint"는 독립절이고, 뒤의 "microscopic cracks typically initiate..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 따라서 두 절 사이에 강한 경계가 필요하며, B는 마침표로 문장을 나누고 도입구 "Over hundreds of cycles" 뒤에 쉼표를 두어 옳다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 경계 표시 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on이다. D는 세미콜론을 썼지만 위치가 잘못되어, 수식구 "over hundreds of cycles"가 앞 절에 쉼표로만 붙어 경계가 엉뚱한 곳에 생긴다.
input.explanation_en: Before the blank, "As a circuit board ... strains each solder joint" is an independent clause, and after it, "microscopic cracks typically initiate..." is another independent clause with its own subject and verb. You need a strong boundary between them, and B gives you one: a period splits the two sentences, and a comma follows the introductory phrase "Over hundreds of cycles." A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, so it's a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses at all, so it's a run-on. D does use a semicolon, but in the wrong place. It attaches "over hundreds of cycles" to the first clause with just a comma, so the break lands where it doesn't belong.
input.design: 긴 동격 삽입구와 종속절 도입부 뒤에서 두 독립절 경계를 판단해야 하며, 도입 전치사구가 어느 절에 속하는지까지 확인해야 D·A를 배제할 수 있다.

input.passage: Carbon nanotubes are tiny cylinders made of carbon atoms arranged in a honeycomb pattern. Each atom forms strong sp² bonds with three neighbors, and these bonds resist being pulled apart ______ engineers add the tubes to plastics and other materials to make composites that are both light and remarkably strong.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: extremely well,
extremely well
extremely well, and,
extremely well. As a result,
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "these bonds resist being pulled apart extremely well"과 빈칸 뒤 "engineers add the tubes..."는 각각 독립절이다. D는 마침표로 두 절을 나누고 "As a result,"로 다음 문장을 시작하므로 올바르다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 이어 붙인 run-on 문장이다. C는 "and" 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣었고, 이미 앞에 "and"로 연결된 절이 있어 문장 구조가 어색해진다.
input.explanation_en: Look at both sides of the blank: "these bonds resist being pulled apart extremely well" and "engineers add the tubes..." are both independent clauses. D is correct because it ends the first sentence with a period and starts a new one with "As a result," so the clauses are properly separated. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. B puts the clauses together with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. C adds an unnecessary comma after "and," and since the sentence already has a clause joined by "and," the structure becomes awkward.
input.design: 독립절 두 개의 경계만 판단하면 되는 쉬운 문항으로, 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스, run-on, 잘못 찍힌 쉼표처럼 학생들이 흔히 하는 실수로 구성했다.

input.passage: In the 1830s, many French critics judged a novel or poem chiefly by whether it improved its readers, praising works that taught civic virtue and condemning those that seemed frivolous. In the preface to his 1835 novel Mademoiselle de Maupin, Théophile Gautier mocked this standard, arguing that art should be valued for its beauty alone rather than for any lesson it delivers. __He pointed out that the most useful room in a house is the latrine, yet no one considers it the most beautiful.__ For Gautier, the comparison exposed a confusion at the heart of moralist criticism: usefulness and beauty are separate qualities, so measuring a poem by its practical benefit is like admiring a building for its plumbing. This position, later summarized as "l'art pour l'art," or "art for art's sake," became a rallying point for writers who resisted demands that literature serve social ends.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a complaint that moralist critics raised against Gautier's preface, which the text then refutes.
It describes a practical concern that led Gautier to abandon his earlier view that art should instruct its readers.
It offers an example of the frivolous subject matter that moralist critics condemned in works like Gautier's novel.
It provides an illustration that Gautier used to support his claim that a work's value does not depend on its usefulness.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 가장 유용한 방이 가장 아름답지는 않다는 비유로, 바로 다음 문장이 이 비유가 유용성과 아름다움이 별개라는 고티에의 주장을 뒷받침한다고 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 비판가들이 등장하지만 이 문장은 그들의 불만이 아니라 고티에 자신의 논거이다. B는 고티에가 이전에 교훈적 예술관을 가졌다가 버렸다는 내용이 지문에 없다. C는 '경박하다'는 비판이 언급되지만, 밑줄 문장은 소설 소재의 예가 아니라 논증용 비유이다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence is a comparison: the most useful room isn't the most beautiful one. The next sentence explains that Gautier used this comparison to show that usefulness and beauty are separate qualities, so D is correct. A is wrong because the sentence is Gautier's own argument, not a complaint from moralist critics. B is wrong because the text never says Gautier once believed art should instruct and later changed his mind. C is wrong because even though the text mentions critics condemning "frivolous" works, the sentence is an analogy meant to support an argument, not an example of a novel's subject matter.
input.design: To answer, students need to connect the underlined analogy to the next sentence, which explains what it means. The distractors borrow real details from the passage (critics, frivolous works, instruction) but get the sentence's role wrong.

input.passage: When certain crystals such as quartz or sucrose are crushed or scratched, they emit brief flashes of light, a phenomenon known as triboluminescence. According to one widely studied model, the fracturing of the crystal lattice separates electric charges along newly formed surfaces, and electrons trapped at structural defects near those surfaces ______ with vacant sites, releasing energy as visible photons.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: recombines
recombining
having recombined
recombine
input.explanation: 빈칸은 'and' 뒤 두 번째 독립절의 동사 자리이며, 주어는 복수 명사 'electrons'이다. 'trapped at structural defects near those surfaces'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이므로 복수 정동사 D(recombine)가 맞다. A는 바로 앞 단수 명사 'defects'가 아닌 'surfaces'나 수식어에 끌린 단수형으로, 복수 주어와 수 일치가 맞지 않는다. B와 C는 분사형이라 절에 정동사가 없게 되어 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The blank is the main verb of the second independent clause after "and," and that clause's subject is the plural noun "electrons." The phrase "trapped at structural defects near those surfaces" only modifies the subject, so the plural finite verb in D (recombine) is correct. A is a singular verb, so it doesn't agree with the plural subject. B and C are participle forms, which would leave the clause without a main verb and make the sentence incomplete.
input.design: 긴 분사 수식어구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어 주어 파악(복수 electrons)과 정동사 필요성을 함께 판단해야 한다.

input.passage: Historians have long credited Italian merchants with inventing double-entry bookkeeping, the system in which every transaction is recorded twice, once as a debit and once as a credit. Economic historian Lien Vercauteren argues, however, that the system's spread across northern Europe owed less to Italian instruction than to the practical needs of Flemish cloth merchants in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. Because these merchants bought wool from England, paid weavers in Ghent and Bruges, and sold finished cloth at fairs in Antwerp, they often relied on agents and partners who never met one another. Vercauteren found that ledgers kept by such firms gradually converged on a shared layout, with matching columns and standardized headings, even among merchants who had no known contact with Italian teachers. In her view, this uniformity arose because a ledger that any partner could read at a glance made it easier to settle debts and detect errors among people separated by distance.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Flemish cloth merchants learned double-entry bookkeeping directly from Italian teachers and then spread the method throughout northern Europe.
Flemish cloth merchants adopted standardized ledgers mainly because trading with England required them to follow English record-keeping rules.
Flemish cloth merchants kept ledgers with matching columns chiefly to reduce the cost of paying weavers in Ghent and Bruges.
Flemish cloth merchants' reliance on distant partners, rather than Italian influence, may explain why their business records became uniform.
input.design: 정답은 지문의 대조 구조(이탈리아 영향 vs 실무 필요)와 결론(원거리 협업 → 통일성)을 연결해야 하며, 오답은 지문의 세부(이탈리아, 영국, 직조공)를 부분적으로 끌어와 같은 문장 틀로 구성했다.
input.explanation: D가 정답이다. 지문은 복식부기의 확산이 이탈리아 가르침보다 서로 떨어진 파트너들과 거래해야 하는 플랑드르 상인의 실무적 필요 때문이었고, 그래서 장부 양식이 통일되었다는 Vercauteren의 주장을 다룬다. A는 지문에 나오는 이탈리아를 언급하지만, Vercauteren이 바로 부정하는 전통적 견해이다. B는 영국 양모 거래를 언급하지만 영국식 기록 규칙에 대한 내용은 없다. C는 직조공 임금 지급이라는 세부를 끌어오지만, 지문이 제시한 이유는 비용 절감이 아니라 부채 정산과 오류 발견이다.
input.explanation_en: D is correct. The text presents Vercauteren's argument that double-entry bookkeeping spread because Flemish merchants worked with distant partners, not because Italians taught them, and that this need made their ledgers uniform. A mentions the Italians, who do appear in the text, but it restates the traditional view that Vercauteren argues against. B brings in the wool trade with England, but the text never says anything about English record-keeping rules. C picks up the detail about paying weavers, but the text says the standard layout helped partners settle debts and catch errors, not that it lowered costs.

input.passage: In fourteenth-century Florence, large banking houses such as the Bardi and Peruzzi were organized as single partnerships in which every partner was personally liable for all of the firm's debts. When Edward III of England defaulted on enormous loans in the 1340s, both houses collapsed, and their partners lost personal fortunes along with the firms. By the early fifteenth century, the Medici had adopted a different structure: each branch in cities such as Bruges, London, and Venice was set up as a legally separate partnership, with its own contract and its own local partners, and the main Florentine firm held a controlling share in each. Historian Raymond de Roover noted that when the Medici's London branch failed in the 1470s after lending heavily to English royalty, creditors could pursue only the assets of that branch. This suggests that the Medici's arrangement ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: kept branches from lending to royal borrowers, which removed the type of risk that had ruined the Bardi and Peruzzi
kept a loss at one branch from spreading to the rest of the network, which shielded the family from the kind of collapse that had ruined the Bardi and Peruzzi
kept local partners from sharing in branch profits, which gave the Florentine firm more capital than the Bardi and Peruzzi had held
kept the Florentine firm from controlling its branches, which left the family with less authority than the Bardi and Peruzzi had held
input.explanation: 지문은 Bardi와 Peruzzi가 단일 파트너십이라 채무 불이행 하나로 회사 전체가 무너졌지만, Medici는 지점마다 법적으로 분리된 계약을 맺어 런던 지점이 파산했을 때 채권자가 그 지점 자산만 청구할 수 있었다고 설명한다. 이 두 정보를 연결하면 B처럼 손실이 한 지점에 갇혀 전체로 번지지 않았다는 결론이 나온다. A는 런던 지점이 실제로 왕실에 대규모 대출을 했으므로 틀렸다. C는 지점마다 현지 파트너가 있었다는 점은 맞지만 이익 배분이나 자본 규모는 지문에 나오지 않는다. D는 피렌체 본사가 각 지점의 지배 지분을 가졌다는 내용과 정면으로 어긋난다.
input.explanation_en: The passage contrasts two setups. The Bardi and Peruzzi were single partnerships, so one default destroyed the whole firm. The Medici branches were separate legal partnerships, so when London failed, creditors could reach only London's assets. Putting these facts together gives B: a loss at one branch stayed at that branch. A is wrong because the London branch did lend heavily to English royalty. C mentions the real local partners, but the passage says nothing about how profits were shared or how much capital the firm had. D contradicts the passage, which says the Florentine firm held a controlling share in each branch.
input.design: To answer, students must link the Bardi/Peruzzi collapse to the London branch failure. Each wrong answer uses a real detail from the passage (royal lending, local partners, control) but draws the wrong conclusion from it, and all four choices use the same sentence frame.

content.text: Easy 수 일치 문항: 주어 "network"(단수), 짧은 수식어 "of cooperatives".

input.passage: In rural Finland, many small landowners pool their forests through cooperatives that jointly own pulp mills. Instead of sending timber profits to distant investors, the network of cooperatives ______ earnings back to member families, helping to support schools and shops in remote villages.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: returns
return
are returning
have returned
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "network"이고, "of cooperatives"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 동사도 단수형이어야 하므로 A "returns"가 정답이다. B "return", C "are returning", D "have returned"는 모두 복수 동사형이어서, 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "cooperatives"에 동사를 잘못 맞춘 것이다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "network." The phrase "of cooperatives" only describes it. A singular subject needs a singular verb, so choice A, "returns," is correct. Choices B ("return"), C ("are returning"), and D ("have returned") are all plural verb forms. They wrongly agree with the nearby plural noun "cooperatives" instead of the real subject.
input.design: 짧은 전치사구 하나가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있는 주어-동사 수 일치 문항이다. 오답 세 개는 모두 가까운 복수 명사에 동사를 맞춘 형태로, 학생들이 흔히 하는 실수를 반영했다.

input.passage: Commissioned by the Gonzaga family for performance at the Mantuan court in 1607, Claudio Monteverdi's L'Orfeo is often cited as the earliest opera still regularly staged today. The score, which combines expressive solo recitative with richly orchestrated choruses and instrumental interludes that Monteverdi specified in unusual detail for particular instruments, ______ composers of the period that drama set to music could sustain an entire evening's entertainment.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: convincing many
having convinced many
convinced many
to convince many
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'The score'이고, 'which ... instruments'는 긴 관계절일 뿐이므로 주절에는 정동사가 필요하다. C의 'convinced'는 과거시제 정동사로 주어 'The score'와 짝을 이뤄 문장을 완성한다. A의 'convincing'과 B의 'having convinced'는 분사여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다. D의 'to convince'는 부정사여서 역시 주절의 동사가 될 수 없다. 관계절 안의 'specified'를 주절 동사로 착각하면 A나 B를 고르기 쉽다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The score," and "which ... instruments" is just a long relative clause, so the main clause still needs a finite verb. C, "convinced," is a past-tense finite verb that pairs with "The score" and completes the sentence. A ("convincing") and B ("having convinced") are participles, so the sentence would be left without a main verb. D ("to convince") is an infinitive, so it can't serve as the main verb either. If you mistake "specified" inside the relative clause for the main verb, A or B can look correct.
input.design: 긴 관계절이 주어와 빈칸을 갈라놓아 관계절 속 동사를 주절 동사로 착각하게 만들었다. 오답 A, B는 분사형이라 그럴듯하게 읽힌다.

input.passage: After Rhodesia's 1965 unilateral declaration of independence, the United Nations imposed sanctions meant to cripple the colony's economy, and tobacco, its leading export, was a prime target. Some economists later argued that the sanctions failed broadly, since Rhodesia's overall output kept growing into the early 1970s as manufacturers replaced lost imports with local goods. Historian Mira Castellanos offers a narrower assessment. Examining marketing board records, she found that tobacco growers, unlike manufacturers, could not substitute domestic buyers for foreign ones: the crop had to be sold abroad, typically through intermediaries routing it via South Africa and Mozambique at steep discounts. __Castellanos documents that, during the sanctions period, the average price Rhodesian growers received per kilogram fell by nearly half, even in years when total economic output rose.__ She concludes that the sanctions did not cripple Rhodesia's economy as a whole but did severely damage sectors whose supply chains depended on foreign buyers.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It provides evidence that sanctions severely weakened the Rhodesian economy as a whole, contradicting the economists who claimed the sanctions failed.
It provides evidence that sanctions inflicted serious harm on an export sector reliant on foreign buyers even while the broader economy expanded.
It provides evidence that tobacco growers suffered price losses, without bearing on how other sectors or the overall economy fared under sanctions.
It provides evidence that the rise in Rhodesia's total output caused the decline in the prices tobacco growers received for their crop.
input.explanation: 정답 B: 밑줄 문장은 담배 가격이 거의 절반으로 떨어졌다는 사실과, 그 시기에도 전체 생산은 증가했다는 사실을 함께 제시한다. 이는 '경제 전체는 무너지지 않았지만 해외 구매자에 의존하는 부문은 큰 타격을 입었다'는 Castellanos의 결론과 범위가 정확히 일치한다. A: 근거가 경제 전체의 약화까지 입증한다고 과장했다. 밑줄 문장은 오히려 전체 생산이 증가했다고 밝힌다. C: 가격 하락 부분만 반영하고 '전체 생산이 증가한 해에도'라는 비교 정보를 빠뜨려 너무 좁게 해석했다. 이 비교가 바로 부문별 피해와 경제 전체의 성과를 구분하는 근거다. D: 인과 관계를 잘못 설정했다. 지문에서 가격 하락의 원인은 제재와 할인된 우회 판매이며, 생산 증가는 원인이 아니라 대조되는 배경일 뿐이다.
input.explanation_en: B is correct. The underlined sentence pairs two facts: growers' prices fell by nearly half, and this happened even while total output rose. Together, these facts support exactly what Castellanos concludes: sanctions didn't cripple the whole economy, but they badly hurt sectors that depended on foreign buyers. A goes too far. The sentence actually says overall output rose, so it can't show that the whole economy was weakened. C reads the sentence too narrowly. It ignores the comparison with rising total output, and that comparison is what separates the damage to one sector from how the economy performed overall. D gets the cause wrong. The text blames the price drop on sanctions and discounted resale through intermediaries. Rising output is presented as a contrast, not as the cause.
input.design: 근거(가격 하락과 전체 생산 증가의 동시 발생)는 부분 입증 역할을 하며, 이것이 결론의 범위와 정확히 맞는다. 오답은 각각 경제 전체로의 과장, 대조 정보를 뺀 좁은 해석, 인과 방향을 뒤바꾼 해석에 기반한다.

input.passage: Potassium-argon (K-Ar) dating estimates the age of a volcanic rock by measuring how much argon-40 has built up from the radioactive decay of potassium-40 since the rock crystallized. The method assumes that molten lava releases essentially all of its argon gas, so that the "clock" starts at zero when the rock solidifies. Geochemist Lena Okafor has proposed that this assumption fails for some lavas that cool quickly underwater: in her view, the high water pressure keeps preexisting argon from escaping, so these rocks begin with "excess" argon and yield K-Ar ages that are older than their true crystallization ages.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
options: Basalt that erupted underwater at great depth in a historically recorded eruption a few decades ago gives K-Ar ages of several hundred thousand years, while basalt from the same eruption that flowed onto land gives ages near zero.

Basalt that erupted on land in a historically recorded eruption a few decades ago gives K-Ar ages of several hundred thousand years, while basalt from the same eruption that flowed underwater gives ages near zero.
Basalt that erupted underwater at great depth contains more potassium-40 than basalt that erupted on land, which causes argon-40 to build up faster in the underwater samples after they solidify.
Basalt that erupted underwater at great depth gives K-Ar ages that closely match the ages given by a separate dating method that does not depend on argon.
input.explanation: Okafor의 가설은 깊은 수중에서 빨리 식은 용암이 기존 아르곤을 잡아 두어 실제보다 오래된 연대가 나온다는 것이다. A는 나이를 알고 있는 최근 분출에서 수중 시료만 지나치게 오래된 연대를 보이고 육상 시료는 정상적이라는 내용이므로, 수중 조건이 오류의 원인임을 직접 보여 준다. B는 같은 틀이지만 수중과 육상이 뒤바뀌어 있어 가설과 반대 방향이다. C는 오래된 연대의 원인을 칼륨 양이 많아 고화 후 아르곤이 더 빨리 쌓이는 것으로 설명하므로, 처음부터 있던 과잉 아르곤 메커니즘과 다르다. D는 수중 시료의 연대가 정확하다는 것을 보여 주므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다.
input.explanation_en: Okafor claims that lava cooling quickly deep underwater traps preexisting argon, so its K-Ar ages come out too old. A fits this: in an eruption of known recent age, only the underwater samples give far-too-old ages, while the land samples are correct, which points to the underwater setting as the cause. B uses the same setup but flips land and underwater, so it points the opposite way. C explains older ages by extra potassium making argon build up faster after the rock solidifies, which is a different mechanism from argon trapped at the start. D shows the underwater ages are accurate, so it weakens the hypothesis instead of supporting it.
input.design: To get the answer, you have to connect two things: an eruption of known age and a comparison between underwater and land samples. B is the same finding with the settings swapped, which catches students who skim. C names the right environment but gives a different mechanism.

input.passage: In the thirteenth century, a merchant traveling from Genoa to the fairs of Champagne faced a costly problem: carrying chests of silver coins across the Alps invited robbery, and coins minted in one city often had uncertain value in another. Genoese bankers addressed this by refining the bill of exchange, a written order in which a banker in one city promised that a partner in a distant city would pay the bearer a fixed sum in local currency. Historians have often celebrated the bill mainly as a safer way to move money. Yet the bankers' records suggest its larger effect lay elsewhere. Because payment came weeks after the bill was issued and in a different currency, the exchange rate written on the bill could quietly build in a charge for the delay. That let bankers earn what was in effect interest at a time when Church law condemned openly charging it, and it made lending over long distances both profitable and permissible.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Genoese bankers created the bill of exchange chiefly to protect merchants from robbers on Alpine routes to the Champagne fairs.
Genoese bankers relied on the bill of exchange mainly to settle the uncertain value of coins minted in different cities.
Genoese bankers used the bill of exchange in a way that hid a fee for the time before payment, which made long-distance lending workable under religious rules.
Genoese bankers depended on the bill of exchange because Church law required merchants to pay debts only in local currency.
input.design: 지문 앞부분의 안전·통화 문제(오답 A, B의 부분 근거)를 지나 'Yet' 이후의 전환된 주장을 파악해야 정답이 되도록 했다. D는 지문 속 단어(Church law, local currency)를 섞어 그럴듯하게 만들었다.
input.explanation: 지문은 어음이 흔히 안전한 송금 수단으로 평가되지만, 'Yet' 이후에 더 큰 효과가 따로 있었다고 주장한다. 그 효과란 환율 안에 지급 지연에 대한 대가를 넣어 교회법을 어기지 않고 사실상 이자를 받을 수 있었다는 점이다. 따라서 정답은 C이다. A와 B는 지문 앞부분에 나오는 문제를 말하지만, 지문은 그것이 주된 의의가 아니라고 반박한다. D는 교회법이 현지 통화 지급을 요구했다고 하는데, 이는 지문에 없는 내용이다.
input.explanation_en: The text says the bill of exchange is usually praised as a safer way to move money, but after "Yet" it argues that the bill's larger effect lay elsewhere. That effect was building a charge for delayed payment into the exchange rate, which let bankers earn interest without breaking Church law. So C is correct. A and B describe problems mentioned at the start, but the text explicitly says those were not the main significance. D claims Church law required payment in local currency, and the text never says that.

input.passage: The Peace of Westphalia, signed in 1648, is often credited with inventing the modern system of sovereign states, in which each government holds supreme authority within its own borders. Historian Andreas Osiander and others have questioned this view. They note that the treaties said little about sovereignty as an abstract principle; instead, they settled specific disputes over territory, religion, and the constitution of the Holy Roman Empire, and they even gave foreign powers such as Sweden and France the right to help guarantee the empire's internal arrangements. Such provisions hardly fit a model of fully independent states. Still, these scholars concede that the settlement mattered: by confirming that rulers could determine the official religion of their lands, it removed one of the main justifications for outside intervention and helped end a century of religious warfare. On this reading, Westphalia advanced the idea of sovereignty without establishing it, and the clear principle later attributed to it was largely built up by nineteenth- and twentieth-century writers looking back.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Because the Peace of Westphalia allowed foreign powers to guarantee arrangements within the Holy Roman Empire, it actually weakened the authority of rulers and prolonged religious conflict.
The Peace of Westphalia created the modern system of sovereign states by declaring that each government holds supreme authority within its own borders.
Historians now agree that the Peace of Westphalia had little lasting importance, since its provisions dealt mainly with narrow territorial and constitutional disputes.
Although the Peace of Westphalia helped end religious wars and moved Europe toward sovereignty, its reputation as the clear origin of the sovereign state system was mostly shaped by later writers.
input.explanation: 지문은 베스트팔렌 조약이 주권 국가 체제를 '발명'했다는 통념을 반박하면서도, 이 조약이 종교 전쟁을 끝내고 주권 개념을 진전시켰음은 인정한다. 그리고 명확한 원칙이라는 평판은 후대 저술가들이 만들어 낸 것이라고 결론짓는다. 이 두 내용을 모두 담은 D가 정답이다. A는 외국 보증권이라는 세부 내용을 활용하지만, 지문은 조약이 종교 전쟁을 끝내는 데 기여했다고 말하므로 '분쟁을 연장했다'는 서술은 지문과 반대된다. B는 지문이 반박하는 통념을 그대로 되풀이한다. C는 구체적 분쟁이라는 근거를 쓰지만, 학자들이 조약의 중요성을 인정한다는 점(the settlement mattered)과 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The text pushes back on the common claim that Westphalia invented the sovereign state system. At the same time, it grants that the treaty helped end religious warfare and moved Europe toward sovereignty, and it concludes that the treaty's image as a clear origin point was mostly created by later writers. D is correct because it includes both of these points. A uses a real detail, the foreign guarantee rights, but the text says the treaty helped end religious wars, so it did not prolong them. B simply restates the traditional view that the text disputes. C picks up the point about specific disputes, but it ignores the scholars' admission that the settlement mattered.
input.design: 통념과 그에 대한 반박, 그리고 양보를 함께 종합해야 풀 수 있게 했다. A와 C는 지문의 실제 세부 내용을 근거로 삼지만 결론을 왜곡하고, B는 첫 문장만 훑어 읽은 학생이 고르도록 만든 함정이다.

input.passage: Completed in the early 1300s under the patronage of the Ilkhanid rulers Ghazan and Öljeitü, Rashid al-Din's Jami' al-tawarikh ("Compendium of Chronicles") is often described as the first attempt at a world history. Some scholars have treated the work mainly as a vehicle for Persian literary tradition, with Mongol patrons simply paying for it. Historian Leyla Marandi argues instead that the Mongol court actively shaped how the history was put together. According to Marandi, the project's reliance on oral and written materials held by the Mongol elite, especially the restricted genealogical record known as the Altan Debter, shows that Rashid al-Din's method depended on access only the court could grant.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marandi's argument?
options: Passages in the Jami' al-tawarikh describing Mongol genealogy are written in an elevated Persian prose style closely modeled on earlier Persian court chronicles.
Copies of the Jami' al-tawarikh were produced in a workshop in Tabriz that Rashid al-Din funded from his own estates, and many were sent to cities across the Ilkhanate.
Sections of the Jami' al-tawarikh on Mongol lineages contain details found in no surviving source other than records that could be consulted only with the khan's permission.
Rashid al-Din's accounts of Chinese and Indian history draw heavily on informants who traveled to the Ilkhanid court as merchants and diplomats.
input.explanation: 마란디의 주장은 이 저작의 방법이 궁정만이 허락할 수 있는 접근권, 즉 제한된 몽골 계보 기록에 의존했다는 것이다. C는 칸의 허가가 있어야만 볼 수 있는 기록에만 나오는 세부 내용이 이 저작에 들어 있다고 하므로, 궁정이 허락한 접근권과 저술 방법을 직접 연결한다. A는 페르시아 문학 전통의 영향을 보여 주므로 오히려 마란디가 반박하는 견해에 가깝다. B는 필사본 제작과 배포에 관한 내용이며, 자금도 궁정이 아니라 라시드 앗딘 개인에게서 나왔다. D는 궁정을 찾은 정보 제공자를 언급하지만 몽골 엘리트의 제한된 자료와는 관련이 없고, 궁정의 허가가 필요했다는 점도 보여 주지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: Marandi argues that the work's method depended on access that only the court could grant, namely access to restricted Mongol genealogical records. Choice C says the work contains details found only in records that could be consulted with the khan's permission, which directly ties the method to access granted by the court. Choice A points to the influence of Persian literary tradition, so it actually fits the view Marandi rejects. Choice B is about how copies were produced and distributed, and the money came from Rashid al-Din himself, not the court. Choice D mentions informants who visited the court, but they have nothing to do with the Mongol elite's restricted materials, and nothing shows that court permission was required.
input.design: To answer, students have to connect two ideas: Marandi's claim is about access to restricted sources, and the answer must show that the court controlled that access. Choices B and D both mention the court, but you have to compare them closely with the claim to rule them out.

input.passage: Popular accounts often describe the Glorious Revolution of 1688 as the moment England's Parliament simply replaced a defiant king with a cooperative one. When James II fled and William of Orange and Mary accepted the throne, however, the more lasting change lay in the terms attached to their accession. The Bill of Rights of 1689 declared that the monarch could not suspend laws, levy taxes, or maintain a standing army in peacetime without Parliament's consent. Historians note that these limits did not immediately strip William of real power; he still directed foreign policy and chose his own ministers. Yet because the crown now depended on annual parliamentary approval for both revenue and the army, later monarchs found that governing without Parliament had become practically impossible. Over the following decades, this dependence, more than any single dramatic act in 1688, gradually turned Parliament into the dominant institution in English government.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The Glorious Revolution mattered mainly because Parliament succeeded in removing James II and installing monarchs who were more willing to cooperate with it.
The Glorious Revolution's lasting significance came from conditions that made the crown financially and militarily reliant on Parliament, which over time shifted power toward Parliament.
The Glorious Revolution's lasting significance came from the Bill of Rights, which immediately stripped William of his authority over foreign policy and ministers.
The Glorious Revolution's lasting significance came from William's skill at directing foreign policy, which persuaded later monarchs to share power with Parliament.
input.explanation: 지문은 1688년 혁명을 단순한 왕의 교체로 보는 통념을 반박하고, 즉위 조건(권리장전)이 왕을 재정·군대 면에서 의회에 의존하게 만들었으며 이 의존이 수십 년에 걸쳐 의회 우위를 낳았다고 주장하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 지문이 '대중적 설명'으로 소개한 뒤 반박하는 견해이다. C는 권리장전을 언급하지만, 지문은 그것이 윌리엄의 권력을 즉시 빼앗지 않았다고 명시하므로 틀렸다. D는 윌리엄이 외교를 지휘했다는 세부 사항을 쓰지만, 그것이 권력 이동의 원인이었다는 내용은 지문에 없다.
input.explanation_en: The text pushes back on the popular idea that 1688 was just a swap of kings. It argues that the terms of the accession, set out in the Bill of Rights, made the crown depend on Parliament for money and for an army, and that this dependence slowly made Parliament dominant over the following decades. That makes B correct. A restates the "popular account" that the text introduces only to argue against it. C mentions the Bill of Rights, but the text says outright that these limits did not immediately strip William of power. D uses the detail that William directed foreign policy, but the text never says this caused power to shift to Parliament.
input.design: 오답 A·C·D는 지문 속 진짜 세부(통념, 권리장전, 윌리엄의 외교권)를 끌어와 정답과 같은 문장 틀로 썼기 때문에, '즉시가 아닌 점진적 변화'와 '의존'이라는 두 정보를 연결해야만 배제할 수 있다.

input.passage: Only a small portion of the poetry of Sappho, who lived on the Greek island of Lesbos around 600 BCE, has survived, often as torn scraps of papyrus or short lines quoted by later writers. Even so, these remains are enough to show that she was a skilled inventor of rhythm. The four-line stanza now named after her, the "Sapphic stanza," was so ______ that poets writing centuries later, including the Roman poet Catullus, copied its pattern in their own work.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: fragile
influential
obscure
brief
input.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 'so ~ that' 구문은 수백 년 뒤 카툴루스 같은 시인들이 그 형식을 따라 썼다는 결과를 제시하므로, 빈칸에는 다른 이들에게 영향을 미쳤다는 뜻의 B가 들어가야 한다. A(깨지기 쉬운)는 파피루스 조각이 훼손되었다는 앞 내용과 연결되어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 연 형식이 약하다는 것으로는 후대 시인들이 모방한 이유가 되지 않는다. C(잘 알려지지 않은)는 후대 시인들이 널리 모방했다는 사실과 정반대이다. D(짧은)는 '네 줄 연'이라는 표현과 관련 있어 보이지만, 짧다는 것만으로는 후대 시인들이 따라 쓴 결과를 설명하지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: The "so ___ that" structure tells you the blank must explain why poets centuries later, like Catullus, copied the stanza's pattern, so the stanza must have had a strong effect on others. That makes B the best answer. A is tempting because the papyrus scraps were torn, but a stanza being fragile wouldn't make later poets imitate it. C means little known, which is the opposite of a pattern that later poets widely copied. D may seem right because the stanza has only four lines, but being short doesn't explain why later poets copied it.
input.design: 'so ~ that' 인과 구조 하나가 직접 단서가 되는 쉬운 문항이다. 오답은 지문의 표면 정보(훼손된 파피루스, 네 줄)와 연결되어 그럴듯해 보이도록 만들었다.

input.passage: Historians often trace the Dutch Republic's seventeenth-century commercial dominance to its spice voyages, but economic historian Jan de Vries points to a humbler source: herring. Dutch fleets cured their catch with salt at sea, so the fish stayed edible for months and could be sold across Europe. The steady profits from this trade did not merely supplement merchants' incomes; they ______ the later ventures, supplying the capital that paid for ships, warehouses, and the long-distance expeditions often credited with creating the Golden Age.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: overshadowed
resembled
underwrote
postponed
input.explanation: 지문은 청어 무역의 이윤이 단순한 부수입이 아니라 선박과 창고, 원거리 원정에 쓸 자본을 '공급했다'고 말하므로, 재정적으로 뒷받침했다는 뜻의 C(underwrote)가 정답이다. A(overshadowed)는 청어가 향신료 무역보다 과소평가되었다는 지문의 대비 구도와 얼핏 맞아 보이지만, 무엇이 무엇을 가렸는지가 아니라 자금 공급 관계를 설명하는 문맥과 맞지 않는다. B(resembled)는 두 사업이 모두 무역이라는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 'supplying the capital'이 나타내는 인과·자금 관계를 담지 못한다. D(postponed)는 '나중의(later)' 사업이라는 시간 표현에 끌린 오답으로, 이윤이 사업을 가능하게 했다는 내용과 정반대다.
input.explanation_en: The text says the herring profits were more than extra income: they supplied the capital for ships, warehouses, and expeditions. That means they financially backed the later ventures, so C (underwrote) is correct. A (overshadowed) might seem to fit because the passage contrasts herring with the spice voyages, but the blank describes a funding relationship, not one trade outshining the other. B (resembled) sounds reasonable since both were commercial activities, but it leaves out the cause-and-effect link that "supplying the capital" sets up. D (postponed) is tempting because of the word "later," but it says the opposite of what the text means, since the profits made those ventures possible.
input.design: 빈칸 뒤 분사구(supplying the capital)와 'did not merely supplement' 대비를 함께 읽어야 풀리게 했다. 오답 A·D는 지문의 대비 구도와 'later'라는 단어에서 부분적인 근거를 얻게 만들었다.

content.text:
Design: passage about Basquiat; long appositive/modifier then clause boundary.

Passage: "Before he exhibited in galleries, Jean-Michel Basquiat wrote cryptic aphorisms on Lower Manhattan walls under the tag SAMO©, a collaborative project with his friend Al Diaz. By 1982, however, his canvases were selling for thousands of dollars ______ the artist, rather than abandoning his street-born skepticism, began scrawling crossed-out words and copyright symbols across his paintings to question the very market that now prized them."

Correct: "dollars; yet" ... need options with first word not "dollars". Options: punctuation combos only. Correct B: "; yet". Hmm, ", and" could also be correct... avoid. Options: A ", yet," hmm. Let's do: A ", yet" — actually ", yet" is correct too. Use options without conjunction for clean: A ", " (comma splice), B "; ", C " " (fused), D ", which" ... "which the artist began" ungrammatical. Medium: tempting since "the artist, rather than..., began" long interrupter. Fine. Options: A ",", B ";", C "and", D ", while" — ", while" would be grammatical. Use D ", the canvases" no. D: "—and so" grammatical-ish. Keep D as no punctuation. C: ", and" is correct... Use C: "and," → "dollars and, the artist..." wrong. OK.

input.passage: Before he ever exhibited in a gallery, Jean-Michel Basquiat wrote cryptic aphorisms on Lower Manhattan walls under the tag SAMO©, a collaborative project with his friend Al Diaz. By 1982, his canvases were selling to collectors for thousands of dollars______ the artist, rather than abandoning his street-born skepticism, began scattering crossed-out words and copyright symbols across his paintings to question the very market that now prized them.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: and,
input.design: 빈칸 뒤 독립절의 주어와 동사 사이에 긴 삽입구(rather than...)가 끼어 있어서, 뒤쪽이 독립절이라는 것을 알아보기 어렵게 했다. 쉼표 하나만 쓴 오답과 접속사 뒤에 쉼표를 잘못 붙인 오답은 겉보기에는 그럴듯하다.
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'his canvases were selling...'은 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤도 삽입구를 빼면 'the artist began scattering...'인 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 접속사 없이 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 맞으므로 정답은 B이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 절을 이어서 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C는 접속사 and 뒤에 쉼표를 둬서 주어 the artist를 앞 절과 떼어 놓고, 그 쉼표는 삽입구를 닫는 쉼표와 짝도 맞지 않는다. D는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "his canvases were selling...," is an independent clause. Take out the interrupting phrase after the blank and you get "the artist began scattering...," which is also an independent clause. A semicolon is the right way to join two independent clauses without a conjunction, so B is correct. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts a comma after "and," which cuts the subject "the artist" off from the first clause, and that comma doesn't pair correctly with the commas around the interrupting phrase. D runs the two clauses together with no punctuation, which makes a run-on sentence.

content.text:
Design: long modifier between subject and verb; subject singular "distinction"; also need finite verb vs participle.

Passage: "Sociologist Basil Bernstein argued that children from working-class and middle-class homes often learn different ways of speaking. His distinction between "restricted" codes, which rely on meaning shared within a close group, and "elaborated" codes, which spell out meaning explicitly for any listener, ______ researchers a way to explain why schools, which reward explicit speech, may favor some students over others."

Options: A "offered" B "have offered" C "offering" D "were offering". B plural agreement with codes — wrong. D plural too. C participle no main verb. A correct past singular. Fine, also "to offer" could be alternative but keep.

input.passage: In the 1960s and 1970s, British sociologist Basil Bernstein studied how children from different social classes learn to use language. His distinction between "restricted" codes, which depend on meanings already shared within a close-knit group, and "elaborated" codes, which spell out meaning explicitly for listeners of any background, ______ researchers a way to explain why schools, which tend to reward explicit and context-free speech, might favor middle-class students over their working-class peers.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: offered
have offered
offering
were offering
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "distinction"이고, 그 뒤의 긴 전치사구와 관계절("between ... codes, which ... and ... codes, which ...")은 수식어일 뿐이므로 단수 주어에 맞는 정동사가 필요하다. A는 단수 주어와 함께 쓸 수 있는 과거형 정동사이므로 정답이다. B와 D는 정동사이긴 하지만 빈칸 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "codes"에 일치시킨 복수형이라 단수 주어 "distinction"과 맞지 않는다. C는 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "distinction." Everything after it up to the blank ("between ... codes, which ... and ... codes, which ...") is a modifier, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject. A is a past-tense finite verb that works with a singular subject, so it's correct. B and D are finite verbs, but they're plural forms that match the nearby noun "codes," not the singular subject "distinction." C is a participle, which leaves the sentence without a main verb, so it isn't a complete sentence.
input.design: 긴 전치사구와 두 관계절이 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어, 가까운 복수 명사 codes에 끌리는 오답(B, D)과 정동사가 빠지는 분사 오답(C)이 모두 그럴듯하게 보이도록 만들었다. 정답을 고르려면 주어를 찾는 단계와 동사의 수를 확인하는 단계, 두 단계가 필요하다.

input.passage: Lawrence Kohlberg proposed that moral reasoning develops through an ordered sequence of stages, and he classified people not by the decisions they reach on moral dilemmas but by the justifications they offer. In the famous "Heinz dilemma," a man considers stealing a drug he cannot afford to save his dying wife. Under Kohlberg's scheme, two people who both say Heinz should steal could be placed at very different stages: one might argue that Heinz would get in trouble with his wife's family if she died, while another might appeal to the principle that human life outweighs property rights. Suppose a researcher surveys a group of adolescents and an older group of adults, and finds that the same proportion in each group answers that Heinz should steal the drug. Based on Kohlberg's approach, the researcher should conclude that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the adults have reasoned at a more advanced stage than the adolescents, since they are older and have had more opportunities for development.
the two groups have reasoned at the same stage, since they reached matching verdicts on the dilemma at matching rates.
this finding alone cannot show whether the two groups differ in their stage of moral reasoning, since it says nothing about the justifications given.
the dilemma is unsuitable for measuring moral development, since it failed to produce a different verdict rate in each group.
input.explanation: 지문에 따르면 콜버그는 결론(훔칠지 여부)이 아니라 그 결론의 근거로 단계를 분류하고, 같은 답도 서로 다른 단계에서 나올 수 있다. 따라서 답한 비율이 같다는 자료만으로는 단계 차이를 판단할 수 없으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 나이에 따른 발달이라는 그럴듯한 전제에 기대지만, 근거 자료 없이 단계를 단정한다. B는 같은 결론을 같은 단계로 보는 것으로, 지문의 핵심 원칙과 정면으로 어긋난다. D는 답의 비율 차이를 측정의 기준으로 삼는데, 콜버그 방식에서 딜레마는 근거를 이끌어내는 도구이므로 이 결과가 딜레마의 부적합함을 보여주지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The passage says Kohlberg sorts people into stages by the justifications they give, not by their verdicts, and that the same verdict can come from very different stages. Because of that, matching rates of "steal" answers can't tell you whether the groups differ in stage, so C is correct. A leans on a plausible assumption about age and development, but it decides the stages without any data on reasoning. B treats the same verdict as meaning the same stage, which directly contradicts the passage's main point. D judges the dilemma by whether it produced different verdict rates, but in Kohlberg's approach the dilemma is a tool for drawing out reasoning, so this result doesn't show the dilemma is unsuitable.
input.design: To answer, students have to connect two pieces of information: the rule that stages are classified by justification, and the survey data, which report only verdict rates. Choice A, based on age, and choice B, based on matching verdicts, will tempt students who skim.

content.text:
Design: subject-verb agreement after a long modifier. Example: "The finding that people who are told they must adopt a particular view often embrace the opposite position, a response that psychologists attribute to a perceived threat to personal freedom, ______ researchers designing public health campaigns to favor less controlling language."
Subject is "finding" (singular) → main verb needed: "has led". Distractors: "have led" (plural agreement with freedom? no—plural attracts "psychologists"/"people"), "leading" (participle, no finite verb), "having led".
Correct B: "has led". A: "have led". C: "leading". D: "to lead".

input.passage: Reactance theory, first proposed by psychologist Jack Brehm in 1966, holds that people resist messages that seem to threaten their freedom to choose. The repeated observation that audiences told they "must" adopt a particular view often move toward the opposite position, a pattern documented in studies of everything from recycling appeals to dietary advice, ______ many designers of public campaigns to replace commands with gentler, choice-affirming language.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: have prompted
has prompted
prompting
to prompt
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'observation'이며, 그 뒤의 that절과 동격 삽입구는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 문장에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하므로 B의 'has prompted'가 정답이다. A는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사(audiences, studies, appeals)에 끌린 복수형이라 주어와 수가 맞지 않는다. C의 분사 'prompting'과 D의 부정사 'to prompt'는 정동사가 아니어서 주절에 서술어가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "observation." The that-clause and the appositive phrase after it are only modifiers. So the sentence needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, which makes B, "has prompted," correct. A is a finite verb, but it's plural, likely pulled in by nearby plural nouns like "audiences," "studies," and "appeals," so it doesn't agree with the subject. C (a participle) and D (an infinitive) aren't finite verbs, so with either one the main clause has no predicate and the sentence is incomplete.
input.design: 긴 동격절·삽입구로 주어와 동사를 멀리 떨어뜨리고, 빈칸 바로 앞에 복수 명사들을 배치해 수 일치 판단과 정동사 필요 여부 판단을 둘 다 요구했다.

input.passage: In the 1920s, German artist Käthe Kollwitz increasingly abandoned etching, a technique that allows fine tonal gradations, in favor of woodcuts and lithographs, which produce bold, simplified forms. Some critics have read this shift as a purely aesthetic turn toward Expressionist style. Yet Kollwitz's own letters show that she wanted her images of hunger, grief, and unemployment in Weimar Germany to circulate as posters and inexpensive prints among working-class viewers, many of whom encountered art only on street walls or in union halls. Moreover, woodcuts and lithographs could be printed in far larger editions and at lower cost than etchings, whose copper plates wear down after relatively few impressions. Taken together, these points suggest that Kollwitz's change in technique ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: reflected mainly her growing admiration for the bold forms favored by other Expressionist artists of the period.
was motivated at least partly by a practical goal of reaching a broad audience, not by stylistic preference alone.
was intended to make her images of suffering more technically refined than her earlier etchings had been.
allowed her to sell her prints to wealthy collectors at higher prices than her etchings had commanded.
input.explanation: 지문은 콜비츠가 노동계급 관객에게 작품을 널리 퍼뜨리고 싶어 했다는 점과, 목판화·석판화가 더 많은 부수를 더 싸게 찍을 수 있다는 점을 연결하므로, 기법 전환에 실용적 목적이 있었다는 B가 정답이다. A는 비평가들의 순수 미학적 해석을 되풀이할 뿐이며, 지문은 'Yet'으로 이 해석에 반박한다. C는 목판화가 미세한 계조가 아니라 단순한 형태를 만든다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. D는 부유한 수집가가 아니라 저렴한 판화와 노동계급 관객을 강조하는 지문과 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The passage links two facts: Kollwitz wanted her work to circulate widely among working-class viewers, and woodcuts and lithographs could be printed in larger, cheaper editions. Put together, these point to B, a practical aim of reaching a broad audience. A just repeats the critics' purely aesthetic reading, which the passage pushes back on with "Yet." C gets it backwards, because the passage says woodcuts produce simplified forms, while etching is the technique with fine gradations. D clashes with the passage's focus on cheap prints and working-class audiences, not wealthy collectors.
input.design: 수신자 의도와 매체의 경제성이라는 두 정보를 연결해야 결론에 도달하도록 했고, 비평가 견해(A)와 기법 특성 오독(C)을 부분 근거 오답으로 배치했다.

input.passage: In the early twentieth century, several German optical firms (among them makers of microscope objectives, camera lenses, and surveying instruments) agreed to pool their patents on specialized glass formulas______ arrangement allowed smaller workshops to build precision instruments to shared specifications without fear of costly infringement suits.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: formulas, the
formulas the
formulas and the
formulas; the
input.explanation: 괄호 속 삽입구를 빼고 보면 빈칸 앞 "several German optical firms ... agreed to pool their patents on specialized glass formulas"는 독립절이고, 뒤의 "the arrangement allowed ..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. C는 등위접속사 and를 썼지만, 긴 두 독립절을 연결할 때 표준 영어에서 요구하는 and 앞 쉼표가 없다.
input.explanation_en: If you set aside the parenthetical, the text before the blank, "several German optical firms ... agreed to pool their patents on specialized glass formulas," is an independent clause. The text after it, "the arrangement allowed ...," is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so D is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B puts the clauses together with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. C uses the coordinating conjunction "and" but leaves out the comma that Standard English requires before it when it joins two long independent clauses.
input.design: The parenthetical list puts distance between the subject and the clause boundary, so a quick reader might miss that two independent clauses meet at the blank. Choice C (a conjunction with no comma) and choice A (a comma with no conjunction) each get part of the rule right, so you have to compare them against D to rule them out.

input.passage: Superabsorbent polymers, the cross-linked polyacrylate networks found in diapers and agricultural soil additives, can absorb hundreds of times their own mass in pure water. The density of cross-links strongly governs this capacity. A lightly cross-linked hydrogel, whose chains can stretch far apart as water rushes ______ swells to a larger final volume but reaches equilibrium more slowly than a densely cross-linked one.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: in,
in;
in
in, and
input.design: "whose"로 시작하는 비제한 관계절이 주어와 동사 "swells" 사이에 끼어 있어, 그 관계절을 닫는 쉼표를 찾아야 한다. 수식어 안의 "as" 절 때문에 절이 끝나는 위치가 헷갈리게 했고, 쉼표+등위접속사나 세미콜론 같은 그럴듯한 오답을 넣었다.
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "A lightly cross-linked hydrogel"이고 동사는 "swells"이다. 그 사이에 "whose"로 시작하는 비제한 관계절이 들어가 있으며, 앞쪽에 쉼표가 있으므로 뒤쪽에도 쉼표가 있어야 관계절이 닫힌다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 세미콜론을 쓰는데, 세미콜론 앞부분이 독립절이 아니고 뒷부분에도 주어가 없으므로 틀렸다. C는 닫는 쉼표가 없어 삽입구가 끝나지 않으며, "rushes in swells"가 하나로 이어진 것처럼 읽힌다. D는 "and"를 붙여 "swells"를 관계절 안의 두 번째 동사로 만들기 때문에 주어 "hydrogel"에 맞는 본동사가 없어진다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "A lightly cross-linked hydrogel," and its verb is "swells." Between them sits a nonrestrictive clause that begins with "whose." That clause opens with a comma, so it also needs a comma to close it, which makes A correct. B uses a semicolon, but the words before it aren't an independent clause, and the words after it have no subject. C leaves out the closing comma, so the inserted clause never ends and "rushes in swells" runs together. D adds "and," which turns "swells" into a second verb inside the relative clause, so the subject "hydrogel" is left with no main verb.

input.passage:
Text 1
In a series of school studies, students who were praised for their effort ("You worked hard on that") persisted longer on difficult puzzles than students praised for their intelligence ("You're so smart"). Researchers argue that effort praise teaches students that ability can grow, and that this belief makes them treat setbacks as chances to learn. Because the belief comes first and the persistence follows, the researchers conclude that schools should train teachers to replace intelligence praise with effort praise.

Text 2
A follow-up team tracked students who got effort praise in the same way and measured both their beliefs about ability and their persistence. Persistence rose in many students whose beliefs about ability did not change at all. Interviews pointed to something else: students read effort praise as a sign that the adult was paying close attention and expected them to keep going, and they kept going to meet that expectation. The team agrees that effort praise tends to produce more persistence than intelligence praise does.
input.question: Based on the texts, which part of the reasoning in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely dispute?
options: The finding that students praised for effort kept working on hard puzzles longer than students praised for intelligence did
The claim that students persist longer because effort praise first changes what they believe about whether ability can grow
The recommendation that schools train teachers to use effort praise in place of intelligence praise
The choice to measure students' persistence with difficult puzzles rather than with regular classroom assignments
input.design: Text 1의 결론(교사 훈련 권고)은 '신념 변화가 끈기를 낳는다'는 인과 가정에 기대고 있다. Text 2는 끈기가 신념 변화 없이도 나타났다는 관찰로 이 가정을 약하게 만든다. 오답은 Text 2가 동의하는 효과(A), 결론 자체(C), 부수적인 방법 세부(D)로 구성하고, 네 선택지 모두 'The ~ that/to ...' 같은 문장 틀로 맞췄다.
input.explanation:
정답 B: Text 1은 노력 칭찬이 먼저 '능력은 자랄 수 있다'는 신념을 만들고 그 신념 때문에 끈기가 생긴다는 인과 경로를 가정한다. Text 2는 능력에 대한 신념이 전혀 바뀌지 않은 학생들에게서도 끈기가 늘었고, 실제 이유는 어른의 기대에 부응하려는 마음이었다고 보고한다. 따라서 Text 2가 직접 겨냥하는 것은 이 인과 가정이다.
A 오답: Text 2는 노력 칭찬이 더 큰 끈기를 낳는다는 점에 분명히 동의한다(마지막 문장).
C 오답: Text 1의 결론 자체다. Text 2의 설명대로라도 노력 칭찬은 여전히 효과가 있으므로, Text 2가 이 권고를 반박한다고 볼 근거는 없다. Text 2가 문제 삼는 것은 그 이유다.
D 오답: 측정 방법이라는 부수적 세부이고, Text 2는 이에 대해 아무 말도 하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer, B: Text 1 assumes a specific chain of cause and effect. First, effort praise changes students' belief that ability can grow, and then that belief makes them persist. Text 2 found that persistence rose in many students whose beliefs about ability never changed. Those students kept going to meet an adult's expectation. That observation attacks exactly this assumed mechanism.
A is wrong because Text 2 openly agrees that effort praise produces more persistence than intelligence praise does.
C is wrong because it is Text 1's conclusion, not the assumption behind it. Even if Text 2's explanation is right, effort praise still works, so Text 2 gives no reason to reject the recommendation. It only questions why the praise works.
D is wrong because the use of puzzles is a minor detail of method, and Text 2 never mentions it.

input.passage: In SDS-PAGE, proteins are first coated with sodium dodecyl sulfate, a detergent that gives each molecule a roughly uniform negative charge per unit length. When an electric field is applied across the polyacrylamide gel, the coated proteins migrate toward the positive electrode, the gel's tangled mesh of polymer strands slowing larger molecules more than smaller ______ the end of a run, proteins of different sizes have separated into distinct bands that researchers can compare against a ladder of known molecular weights.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ones, by
ones, and, by
ones by
ones. By
input.design: 빈칸 앞에 독립절 + 긴 독립분사구(absolute phrase)를 두어 절 경계를 흐리게 했다. 학생은 이 분사구가 독립절이 아니라는 점을 알아본 뒤, 뒤에 새 독립절이 시작된다는 것까지 확인해야 한다.
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 독립절 "the coated proteins migrate..."에 독립분사구 "the gel's tangled mesh ... slowing larger molecules more than smaller ones"가 붙은 구조이다. 빈칸 뒤 "by the end of a run, proteins ... have separated..."는 또 하나의 독립절이므로 두 절을 마침표로 나눈 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on 문장이고, "smaller ones by the end"로 잘못 읽힐 수도 있다. B는 등위접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣었고, and가 분사구와 독립절을 이어 주게 되어 병렬 구조도 어긋난다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank is an independent clause ("the coated proteins migrate...") followed by an absolute phrase ("the gel's tangled mesh ... slowing larger molecules more than smaller ones"). The text after the blank ("by the end of a run, proteins ... have separated...") is a second independent clause, so you need to separate the two with a period, which makes D correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C fuses the two clauses with no punctuation at all, creating a run-on that could also be misread as "smaller ones by the end." B puts an unnecessary comma after "and," and it uses "and" to join an absolute phrase to an independent clause, so the two parts aren't parallel.

input.passage: In the fourteenth century, English kings faced a persistent problem: wool was the kingdom's most valuable export, but taxing thousands of scattered growers and traders was nearly impossible for a royal administration with few officials. The solution that emerged was the Staple, a system that required most raw wool bound for foreign markets to pass through a single designated town—eventually Calais—where a licensed company of merchants held the exclusive right to sell it. Although historians often describe the Staple as a privilege that enriched a narrow merchant elite, its more important function was administrative. By funneling the trade through one location controlled by a small group, the crown could collect export duties efficiently, and the Staplers themselves, in exchange for keeping their monopoly, frequently advanced loans to the king secured against future customs revenue. The merchants' profits, in other words, were the price the crown paid for a reliable mechanism of revenue collection.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The Staple mainly benefited a small group of English merchants, who used their control of the wool trade at Calais to earn large profits.
The Staple was created because English wool had become so valuable that foreign buyers were willing to travel to a single town to purchase it.
The Staple served primarily as a means for the crown to gather money from the wool trade, with merchant privileges functioning as compensation for that service.
The Staple allowed English kings to borrow money from merchants, which reduced the crown's need to tax wool exports at all.
input.explanation: 지문은 Staple이 흔히 상인 엘리트의 특권으로 묘사되지만 실제 더 중요한 기능은 왕실의 세입 징수 수단이었고, 상인의 이익은 그 대가였다고 주장하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 지문이 반박하려는 통념(상인 엘리트의 부)을 중심 내용으로 삼아 틀렸다. B는 양모의 가치라는 세부를 다루지만, 지문은 제도가 생긴 이유를 외국 구매자가 아니라 과세의 어려움으로 설명한다. D는 대출을 언급하지만, 대출은 미래 관세 수입을 담보로 한 것이어서 과세를 대체하지 않았으므로 틀렸다.
input.explanation_en: The text grants that the Staple is often described as a privilege for a merchant elite, but it argues that the system's more important job was helping the crown collect revenue, and that merchant profits were the price paid for this. That makes C correct. A treats the common view the text pushes back on as if it were the main point. B picks up the detail about wool's value, but the text says the system came about because taxing the trade was hard, not because foreign buyers were willing to travel. D brings up the loans, but those loans were secured against future customs revenue, so they relied on taxing wool rather than replacing it.
input.design: To answer, a reader has to connect the concession ("although historians...") to the claim that follows and then to the final sentence. The wrong answers each reuse a real detail from the text (merchant profits, wool's value, loans) but misplace it.

input.passage: In the fifteenth century, the Medici family of Florence built a banking enterprise with branches in cities such as Rome, Venice, Geneva, Bruges, and London. Historians once credited the bank's reach mainly to the family's close ties with the papacy, which deposited large sums with the Medici and used them to move church revenues across Europe. Yet economic historian Raymond de Roover argued that the organization of the network mattered at least as much. Each branch was set up as a separate partnership in which a local manager invested his own capital and shared in the profits, so a loss in one city could not automatically drag down the others. Branches also settled accounts with one another through bills of exchange, letting a merchant pay in Bruges and collect funds in Florence without shipping coins. In de Roover's view, this structure turned a family business into something closer to an international system for transferring money and managing risk.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: According to one scholar, the way the Medici arranged their branches, rather than papal connections alone, explains how the bank came to function as a cross-border financial system.
According to one scholar, the Medici relationship with the papacy was the main reason the bank was able to open branches in cities across Europe.
According to one scholar, bills of exchange were first invented by Medici managers so that merchants could avoid the dangers of transporting coins.
According to one scholar, separate partnerships made Medici branch managers more loyal to their own cities than to the family in Florence.
input.explanation: 지문은 예전 역사가들의 설명(교황청과의 관계)을 소개한 뒤, de Roover가 분리된 파트너십과 환어음 결제 같은 지점망 조직이 적어도 그만큼 중요했고, 이것이 메디치 은행을 국제 송금·위험 관리 체계로 만들었다고 주장했다는 내용이 중심이다. 그래서 A가 정답이다. B는 지문이 de Roover와 대비시키는 예전 견해를 그의 주장인 것처럼 제시한다. C는 지문에 나오는 환어음을 언급하지만, 메디치가 이를 발명했다는 말은 지문에 없다. D는 분리된 파트너십이라는 세부 정보를 바탕으로, 지문에 근거가 없는 충성심 문제를 추론한다.
input.explanation_en: The text first gives an older explanation for the bank's success (its ties to the papacy). It then presents de Roover's argument that the way the network was organized, through separate partnerships and settlements by bill of exchange, mattered at least as much and turned the bank into an international system. That is why A is correct. B gives the older view that the text sets against de Roover as if it were his own claim. C mentions bills of exchange, which do appear in the text, but the text never says the Medici invented them. D starts from the detail about separate partnerships but draws a conclusion about loyalty that the text doesn't support.
input.design: To find the main idea, you have to link the contrast between the older view and de Roover's argument with the organizational details. Wrong choices B, C, and D each take a real detail from the passage and twist or misattribute it.

input.passage: The Implicit Association Test (IAT) asks participants to sort words and faces into paired categories as quickly as possible, using only two keys. Psychologist Anthony Greenwald and his colleagues, who introduced the test in 1998 after years of studying how speed can reveal mental shortcuts ______ that slower responses to certain pairings expose automatic associations a person may not consciously endorse.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: shortcuts; argued
shortcuts, argued
shortcuts—argued
shortcuts argued
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "Psychologist Anthony Greenwald and his colleagues"이고 동사는 "argued"이다. 그 사이에 있는 "who introduced ... mental shortcuts"는 비제한적 관계절이며, 쉼표로 열었으므로 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론을 써서 주어와 동사를 갈라놓고, 세미콜론 앞뒤 어느 쪽도 독립절이 되지 못한다. C의 대시는 수식어를 닫는 부호로 쓸 수는 있지만, 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 대시로 닫으면 부호 짝이 맞지 않는다. D는 닫는 부호가 없어서 관계절이 어디서 끝나는지 분명하지 않다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "Psychologist Anthony Greenwald and his colleagues," and its verb is "argued." Between them is a nonessential relative clause ("who introduced ... mental shortcuts"), and since it opens with a comma, it has to close with a comma too. That makes B correct. A uses a semicolon, which cuts the subject off from its verb, and neither side of the semicolon is an independent clause. C's dash could close a modifier, but you can't close an interruption with a dash after opening it with a comma, because the punctuation has to match. D leaves out the closing punctuation, so the reader can't tell where the relative clause ends.
input.design: 긴 비제한적 관계절이 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어서 경계를 놓치기 쉽다. 그래서 수식어를 닫는 부호를 고르려면 짝 맞추기와 주어-동사 연결을 둘 다 확인해야 한다. 대시와 세미콜론 오답에도 그럴듯해 보이는 근거가 있다.

content.text:
Design: subject-verb agreement after a long modifier with an intervening plural noun, plus finite verb vs. participle.

Passage: "In his treatises on Noh performance, the fifteenth-century actor and playwright Zeami Motokiyo argued that the most moving moments onstage often occur when an actor does nothing at all. This interval of stillness, which later scholars associated with the concept of ma, or meaningful negative space, between the chanted lines and measured steps of a performer ______ the audience to sense an emotion that no gesture could fully express."

Subject: "This interval" (singular). Intervening: "lines and steps of a performer". Need finite singular verb: "invites".
Options: A) invite (plural agreement with lines/steps), B) inviting (participle, no main verb), C) invites, D) having invited (nonfinite).

input.passage: In his treatises on Noh performance, the fifteenth-century actor and playwright Zeami Motokiyo argued that the most moving moments onstage often occur when an actor does nothing at all. This interval of stillness, which later scholars linked to the concept of ma, or meaningful negative space, between the chanted lines and measured steps of a performer ______ the audience to sense an emotion that no gesture could fully express.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: invite
inviting
invites
having invited
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'This interval'이고, 그 뒤의 관계절과 전치사구('between the chanted lines and measured steps of a performer')는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'lines and steps'에 수를 맞춘 형태라 단수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. B와 D는 분사 형태여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "This interval." The relative clause and the prepositional phrase that follow it ("between the chanted lines and measured steps of a performer") only modify that subject. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, which makes C correct. A is a finite verb, but it agrees with the nearby plural nouns "lines and steps," not with the singular subject. B and D are participles, so with either one the sentence has no main verb and isn't complete.
input.design: To solve this, students have to find the main subject behind a long modifier that contains plural nouns. Then they have to pick a finite verb over a participle. A tempts students who match the verb to the nearest noun, and B and D tempt students who mistake the long subject for a modifier.

input.passage: Economists have long noticed that homeowners often refuse to sell their houses for less than they originally paid, even when market prices have clearly fallen. Researchers explain this pattern with the idea of loss aversion: people feel the pain of losing money more strongly than the pleasure of gaining the same amount. __In one study of condominium sales in Boston during the 1990s, owners facing a loss set asking prices well above those of similar units and waited much longer for buyers.__ This evidence suggests that the original purchase price acts as an anchor, shaping sellers' decisions long after it stops reflecting what a home is actually worth.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a theory that the rest of the text goes on to reject.
It describes a problem that the final sentence offers a way to solve.
It presents a specific finding that supports the explanation given earlier.
It raises a question about loss aversion that the text leaves unanswered.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞에서 제시한 손실 회피 설명을 뒷받침하는 구체적 연구 결과(보스턴 콘도 판매 사례)를 제시하며, 다음 문장도 "This evidence"로 이를 증거로 받는다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 오답인데, 이론은 밑줄 앞에서 이미 소개되었고 글은 그 이론을 반박하지 않는다. B는 오답인데, 마지막 문장은 해결책이 아니라 결론적 해석을 제시한다. D는 오답인데, 밑줄 문장은 질문을 던지지 않고 사례를 보고한다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence gives a specific study result (Boston condo sales) that backs up the loss-aversion explanation introduced earlier, and the next sentence calls it "This evidence." So C is correct. A is wrong because the theory was introduced before the underlined sentence, and the text never rejects it. B is wrong because the final sentence offers a conclusion, not a solution. D is wrong because the underlined sentence reports a finding rather than raising a question.
input.design: Simple claim-then-evidence structure with an explicit "This evidence" cue; distractors are typical structure misreadings in parallel "It + verb" frames.

input.passage: Before 1832, many English parliamentary seats belonged to "rotten boroughs," tiny constituencies such as Old Sarum that had almost no residents yet still returned two members to the House of Commons. Meanwhile, fast-growing manufacturing towns like Manchester and Birmingham had no representatives of their own. The Great Reform Act of 1832 took seats away from many rotten boroughs and gave them to these industrial towns, and it also extended the vote to men who occupied property worth at least £10 a year. Some historians have nonetheless argued that the Act left the political influence of the landed aristocracy largely intact. They note that most of the redistributed seats still went to county and small-town constituencies where landlords dominated, and that the £10 property requirement excluded most factory workers in the new urban seats. If these historians are correct, then the Act's main effect was probably that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: industrial workers in Manchester and Birmingham became the largest group of voters in the House of Commons elections that followed.
landowners lost most of their control over county constituencies, even though they kept their hold on small towns.
middle-class urban property holders gained a voice in Parliament while power stayed mostly with the existing landed elite.
rotten boroughs were preserved mostly unchanged, since the redistributed seats were taken from county constituencies instead.
input.explanation: 이 역사가들은 개정 이후에도 지주 귀족의 영향력이 대체로 유지되었고, 10파운드 재산 요건 때문에 공장 노동자 대부분이 배제되었다고 본다. 그렇다면 투표권을 새로 얻은 사람은 일정 재산을 가진 도시 중산층이었고 권력은 여전히 지주층에 있었다는 결론이 나오므로 C가 정답이다. A는 노동자가 배제되었다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. B는 카운티에서 지주가 우세했다는 진술과 모순된다. D는 이 법이 부패 선거구의 의석을 빼앗았다는 지문 내용과 어긋난다.
input.explanation_en: These historians argue that the landed aristocracy kept most of its influence and that the £10 property requirement kept most factory workers from voting. That means the new voters were urban middle-class property holders, while power stayed mostly with landowners, so C is correct. A goes against the point that workers were excluded. B contradicts the claim that landlords dominated the county seats. D goes against the passage, which says the Act took seats away from rotten boroughs.
input.design: To answer, students have to put two pieces of evidence together: landlords kept their dominance, and the property requirement shut out workers. Each wrong answer bends one detail from the passage just enough to sound plausible.

input.passage: In 1960 the French artist Yves Klein patented a binder that kept dry ultramarine pigment almost as vivid as loose powder, and he called the color International Klein Blue. He then painted dozens of nearly identical canvases in it. Yet when he exhibited eleven of these blue monochromes in Milan in 1957, he priced each one differently, insisting that what buyers paid for was the "pictorial sensibility" that each work carried, not the paint or canvas. Two years later he went further and sold "Zones of Immaterial Pictorial Sensibility": buyers handed over gold leaf and got a receipt, and Klein asked them to burn the receipt while he threw half the gold into the Seine. Since the buyer kept no object at all, these transactions suggest that Klein ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: considered his patented pigment so valuable that he refused to let collectors own any work made with it.
wanted to show that a painting's value depends mainly on how rare and vivid the materials used to make it are.
aimed to separate an artwork's value from any physical thing a collector could hold, trade, or display.
regretted that his blue monochromes had sold for different prices and tried to make up for it by giving the gold away.
