input.design: 독자는 두 단서를 연결해야 한다. 하나는 똑같아 보이는 그림에 서로 다른 가격을 매긴 일, 다른 하나는 물건 없이 진행한 거래와 영수증 소각이다. 오답은 특허 안료나 가격 차이 같은 지문의 세부 사항을 이용해 만들었다.
input.explanation: 클라인은 거의 똑같은 그림에 서로 다른 가격을 매기면서 값을 치르는 대상이 물감이 아니라 '감수성'이라고 했다. 이후에는 금을 받고 내준 영수증마저 태우게 해서 구매자가 아무 물건도 갖지 못하게 했다. 이 두 사실을 연결하면 작품의 가치를 물리적 소유물과 떼어 놓으려 했다는 C가 정답이다. A는 특허 안료가 언급된 점을 이용했지만, 클라인은 실제로 파란 그림을 팔았으므로 지문과 모순된다. B는 안료가 선명하다는 묘사를 이용했지만 가치가 재료에 있다는 주장으로, 지문과 정반대다. D는 가격 차이를 언급하지만, 그 가격 차이는 클라인이 의도한 것이었고 후회했다는 근거도 없다.
input.explanation_en: Klein put different prices on nearly identical paintings and said buyers were paying for "sensibility," not paint. Later he had buyers burn even the receipt they got for their gold, so they were left with no object at all. If you connect these two facts, the logical conclusion is C: he wanted to separate an artwork's value from any physical possession. A uses the patented pigment, but it contradicts the passage, because Klein actually did sell blue paintings. B uses the description of the vivid pigment, but it says value comes from materials, which is the opposite of the passage's point. D mentions the different prices, but Klein set them on purpose, and nothing in the passage suggests he regretted it.

input.passage: In September 1938, British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain agreed at Munich to let Germany annex the Sudetenland, a border region of Czechoslovakia, in exchange for Adolf Hitler's pledge to make no further territorial demands in Europe. Chamberlain returned to London declaring that the deal had secured "peace for our time," and many Britons, still haunted by the slaughter of the First World War, greeted him as a hero. __Yet in March 1939, German troops marched into Prague and seized the rest of Czechoslovakia, a region with no significant German-speaking population that Hitler could claim to be reuniting with the Reich.__ The occupation stripped away the justification that had made appeasement seem reasonable to its defenders, and within weeks Britain abandoned the policy, issuing a guarantee to defend Poland's independence.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents an event that undermined the reasoning behind a policy described earlier and that led to the shift in that policy noted afterward.
It presents an event that explains why many Britons initially welcomed the outcome of the agreement described earlier.
It presents an event that shows Chamberlain had anticipated Hitler's intentions when he negotiated the agreement described earlier.
It presents an event that confirms the claim of national reunification that Hitler had used to justify the annexation described earlier.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해, 뮌헨 협정 뒤에도 독일이 독일계 주민이 거의 없는 체코 나머지 지역을 점령했다는 사실을 제시한다. 이 사건은 유화정책의 근거를 무너뜨렸고, 이어지는 문장에서 영국이 정책을 버리고 폴란드를 보장하게 된 계기가 된다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 영국인들의 환영을 설명한 것은 앞 문장이므로 틀렸다. C는 지문에 체임벌린이 히틀러의 의도를 예견했다는 내용이 없어 틀렸다. D는 독일계 주민이 없었다는 점이 오히려 '재통합'이라는 명분을 반박하므로 틀렸다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet" and describes Germany seizing the rest of Czechoslovakia after Munich, even though that region had almost no German-speaking population. This event took away the justification for appeasement, and the next sentence shows Britain dropping the policy and guaranteeing Poland. So A is correct. B is wrong because the sentence before the underlined one is what explains why Britons welcomed the deal. C is wrong because the text never says Chamberlain foresaw Hitler's intentions. D is wrong because the lack of German speakers actually undercuts the "reunification" claim instead of confirming it.
input.design: To answer, you have to connect two things: the contrast signaled by "Yet" and the policy change that follows. Each wrong choice ties the sentence to something real in the passage (the public's reaction, Chamberlain, the reunification claim) but gets the relationship wrong.

input.passage: In 1894, French army captain Alfred Dreyfus, who was Jewish, was convicted of passing military secrets to Germany. Evidence later emerged pointing to another officer, Ferdinand Walsin Esterhazy, yet the army acquitted Esterhazy in 1898 and kept Dreyfus imprisoned. Some historians argue that the army's refusal to reopen the case came mainly from a wish to protect the institution's reputation: senior officers, these historians claim, were less driven by hostility toward Jews than by fear that admitting the original error would discredit the General Staff.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' claim?
options: Anti-Semitic newspapers such as La Libre Parole published frequent attacks on Dreyfus and praised the officers who had convicted him.
Several of the officers involved in the 1894 conviction had expressed openly anti-Semitic views in private letters written before the trial.
After the army acquitted Esterhazy, public protests in support of Dreyfus grew larger in Paris and other French cities.
Officers who privately admitted doubts about Dreyfus's guilt nonetheless urged colleagues to suppress the new evidence, warning that a reversal would undermine public trust in the army's leadership.
input.explanation: 이 역사학자들의 주장은 군이 재심을 거부한 주된 이유가 반유대주의보다 조직의 명예를 지키려는 데 있었다는 것이다. D는 드레퓌스의 유죄를 의심한 장교들조차 군 지도부에 대한 신뢰가 무너질까 봐 증거를 은폐하자고 했다는 내용이므로, 편견이 아니라 조직 보호가 동기였음을 직접 보여 준다. A와 B는 이 사건에 반유대주의가 있었음을 보여 주므로 오히려 대안 설명인 편견 쪽을 강화한다. C는 대중의 반응을 다룰 뿐 장교들의 동기에 대해서는 아무것도 말해 주지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The historians claim the army refused to reopen the case mainly to protect its reputation, not mainly out of hostility toward Jews. D shows that even officers who doubted Dreyfus's guilt pushed to hide evidence because a reversal would damage trust in the leadership, so it points straight to protecting the institution as the motive. A and B show that anti-Semitism was part of the affair, which actually backs the competing explanation, prejudice, more than the historians' view. C is about how the public reacted and tells you nothing about why the officers acted as they did.
input.design: To get this right, students have to separate two possible motives, prejudice and protecting the institution, and then pick the finding about the officers' reasoning. The tempting wrong answers really are about the affair and anti-Semitism, but they back the opposite motive.

input.passage: The Catholic Emancipation Act of 1829 allowed Catholics to sit in the British Parliament for the first time in more than a century, and it is often celebrated as a breakthrough for Irish political rights. Historian Fergus Doyle urges caution, however. The same legislation was accompanied by a measure that raised the property qualification for voting in Irish county elections from forty shillings to ten pounds, a change that removed roughly four-fifths of the Irish county electorate, most of them poor Catholic tenant farmers. Doyle notes that these very voters had defied their landlords in 1828 to elect Daniel O'Connell, the campaign that pressured the government into conceding emancipation. Doyle therefore concludes that the 1829 settlement ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: mainly benefited poor Catholic tenant farmers, whose votes had made O'Connell's 1828 victory possible.
extended political standing to Catholic elites while stripping power from the ordinary Catholics whose activism had won it.
had little practical effect, since no Catholics actually took seats in Parliament in the years that followed.
was driven mainly by landlords who wanted to reward tenants for supporting O'Connell's campaign.
input.explanation: 지문은 두 정보를 연결해야 한다. 하나는 이 법이 가톨릭교도의 의회 진출을 허용했다는 점이고, 다른 하나는 함께 통과된 조치가 가난한 가톨릭 소작농의 투표권을 박탈했으며 바로 그들이 해방을 이끌어 냈다는 점이다. 따라서 엘리트는 지위를 얻고 운동의 주역인 평범한 가톨릭교도는 권력을 잃었다는 B가 정답이다. A는 소작농이 오코넬 승리에 기여한 점은 맞지만, 그들이 혜택을 받았다는 결론은 선거권 박탈과 모순된다. C는 지문에 근거가 없으며 의석 허용이라는 실제 변화를 부정하고, D는 지주에 맞선 소작농의 저항을 지주의 보상으로 뒤집었다.
input.explanation_en: You need to connect two facts: the Act let Catholics sit in Parliament, but the measure passed alongside it took the vote away from poor Catholic tenant farmers, who were the very people whose 1828 votes forced the concession. Choice B puts these together: elites gained standing while the ordinary activists lost power. Choice A gets right that the tenants helped elect O'Connell, but it wrongly claims they benefited, even though most of them lost the vote. Choice C has no support in the text and denies the real change of allowing Catholics to sit in Parliament. Choice D turns things around, because the tenants defied their landlords and were not rewarded by them.
input.design: To answer, you have to connect two pieces of information: what the Act granted and what the franchise measure took away from the same group. A and D reuse true details from the passage but draw the wrong conclusion from them, and C is a plausible-sounding claim with no support.

input.passage: In the 1930s, the French dramatist Antonin Artaud argued that European theater had become a polite parlor game. Audiences, he complained, sat safely in the dark while actors on a distant stage untangled the motives of believable characters, and spectators left feeling they had understood something rather than having been changed by it. Artaud's proposed "Theatre of Cruelty" did not mean staging violence for its own sake. Instead, he wanted performances that would bypass the intellect, using piercing sounds, sudden light, ritual gesture, and spectators seated in the middle of the action, so that the audience could no longer observe from a comfortable distance. Although Artaud staged few productions himself, and the ones he did stage mostly failed, directors such as Peter Brook and Jerzy Grotowski later took up his ideas while reshaping how performers and audiences share space.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Artaud believed that theater should depict violence openly, because staged brutality was the surest way to jolt audiences out of their complacency.
Artaud's ideas about theater were too impractical to be staged successfully, so they remained mostly unrealized until later directors simplified them.
Artaud believed that theater should give audiences a deeper understanding of the psychological motives behind characters' believable behavior.
Artaud believed that theater should overwhelm audiences' senses and remove their detached position, an aim that later shaped other directors' work.
input.explanation: 지문은 아르토가 심리적 사실주의와 관객의 안전한 거리두기를 거부하고, 감각을 압도하며 관객을 행위 한가운데 두는 연극을 원했다는 점, 그리고 그 생각이 후대 연출가들에게 영향을 주었다는 점을 중심으로 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 '잔혹'이라는 말에 기대지만 지문은 폭력 자체를 위한 연출이 아니라고 분명히 말한다. B는 그의 공연이 실패했다는 세부 내용만 확대했고, 후대가 그의 생각을 '단순화했다'는 내용은 지문에 없다. C는 아르토가 비판한 바로 그 관습(인물 동기를 풀어내는 연극)을 그의 목표로 뒤집어 놓았다.
input.explanation_en: The text centers on Artaud's rejection of psychologically realistic theater and of the audience's safe distance. He wanted performances that would overwhelm the senses and put spectators in the middle of the action, and the text adds that his ideas later shaped other directors, so D is correct. A leans on the word "cruelty," but the text says outright that Artaud did not mean violence for its own sake. B blows up the detail that his productions failed and adds a claim the text never makes, that later directors simplified his ideas. C flips his position, because explaining characters' believable motives is exactly the convention Artaud attacked.
input.design: To find the main idea, students have to connect what Artaud rejected with what he proposed and then with his later influence. Each wrong choice pulls in a real detail from the text (cruelty, his failed productions, believable characters) but misreads it.

input.passage: When conservator Pinin Brambilla Barcilon began restoring Leonardo da Vinci's Last Supper in 1978, the mural was covered in centuries of dirt and layers of paint added by earlier restorers. Over twenty years, her team removed these later additions bit by bit, often working on an area no larger than a postage stamp in a single day. Critics later argued that so little of Leonardo's original paint survived that the cleaned mural was more restoration than Leonardo. Supporters answered that Barcilon's slow, careful approach was ______: she never added new paint where none was needed, and she left gaps visible rather than inventing details.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: careless
hasty
cautious
decorative
input.explanation: 지문은 Barcilon의 작업이 "slow, careful"했고, 필요 없는 곳에는 물감을 칠하지 않았으며 세부를 지어내지 않았다고 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 '신중한'이라는 뜻의 C가 들어가야 한다. A는 '부주의한'이라는 뜻으로 careful과 정반대이다. B는 '성급한'이라는 뜻이어서 20년에 걸친 느린 작업과 모순된다. D는 '장식적인'이라는 뜻인데, 그녀는 오히려 새로운 세부를 더하지 않았으므로 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The text says Barcilon's approach was "slow, careful," that she added no unnecessary paint, and that she didn't invent details, so the blank needs a word meaning "careful to avoid risk." That's C. A means "careless," which is the opposite of careful. B means "hasty," which contradicts twenty years of slow work. D means "decorative," but she actually avoided adding new details, so it doesn't fit either.
input.design: 빈칸 바로 앞의 "slow, careful"과 콜론 뒤의 설명이 직접적인 단서가 되어, 한 단계 안에서 뜻을 맞춰 풀 수 있게 했다. 오답은 모두 같은 형용사 형태로 맞췄고, 복원 작업이라는 맥락에서는 그럴듯해 보이도록 골랐다.

input.passage: In his 1757 treatise, Edmund Burke described the sublime as a kind of delightful terror: faced with a towering cliff or a raging storm, the observer feels small, and the mind is simply overpowered by forces it cannot resist. Immanuel Kant, writing three decades later, accepted that such scenes at first overwhelm our senses, but he drew a very different conclusion. For Kant, the sublime experience is not ultimately a defeat of the mind, but rather a ______ of it: when our imagination fails to take in nature's vastness, reason discovers in itself an idea of infinity that no mountain can match. Romantic poets such as Wordsworth took up this view and praised the mind's power that is revealed in the moment the senses fail.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: subjugation
capitulation
vindication
indication
input.explanation:
정답 C(vindication, 정당성 입증·승리). 'not ... a defeat of the mind, but rather a ______'는 '패배'를 부정하고 그와 반대되는 개념을 요구한다. 뒤 문장에서 상상력은 실패하지만 이성이 자연보다 큰 무한의 이념을 자기 안에서 발견한다고 했고, 낭만주의 시인들이 '드러난 정신의 힘'을 찬양했다고 한다. 따라서 정신이 오히려 자신의 우월성을 입증받는다는 뜻의 vindication이 맞다.
A(subjugation, 굴복시킴)는 부정어 not을 무시하고 defeat와 같은 뜻의 단어를 고른 경우다. 이는 칸트가 아니라 버크의 견해에 해당한다.
B(capitulation, 항복)는 'not A but B'를 '패배에 그치지 않고 아예 항복까지'라는 강조 구문으로 잘못 읽어서, 대조로 뒤집혀야 할 의미를 다시 부정 쪽으로 되돌린 경우다.
D(indication, 징후)는 vindication과 철자·발음만 비슷할 뿐, 패배와 대조되는 의미가 없고 'an indication of the mind'도 문맥에 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en:
The correct answer is C, "vindication." The sentence says the sublime is "not ultimately a defeat of the mind, but rather a ______ of it," so the blank needs a word that means the opposite of defeat. The next clause backs this up. Imagination fails, but reason finds in itself an idea of infinity "that no mountain can match." The Romantics then praise "the mind's power." So the mind isn't beaten. Instead, its superiority is proven, which is exactly what "vindication" means.
A, "subjugation," ignores the word "not." It means about the same thing as defeat, and it describes Burke's view, not Kant's.
B, "capitulation" (surrender), comes from misreading "not... but rather" as building up ("not just a defeat but even a surrender"). That flips the meaning back to the negative side when the sentence calls for a contrast.
D, "indication," only looks and sounds like "vindication." It isn't the opposite of defeat, and "an indication of the mind" doesn't make sense here.
input.design: 부정+대조 구문 'not a defeat of the mind, but rather a ______ of it'을 만들고, 빈칸에는 defeat와 반대 극성인 vindication을 정답으로 넣었다. 오답은 각각 부정어를 무시한 동의어(subjugation), 'not A but B'를 강조 구문으로 오독해 극성을 다시 뒤집은 단어(capitulation), 철자·발음만 비슷한 단어(indication)로 구성했다.

input.passage:
In the early sixteenth century, the Fugger family of Augsburg became the most powerful financiers in Europe, and historians often credit their success to banking alone. Yet the Fuggers' real leverage came from an unusual arrangement. When Habsburg rulers such as Maximilian I needed cash for wars and elections, Jakob Fugger lent it to them, but he asked to be repaid not in coin but in the output of silver and copper mines in Tyrol and Hungary. As loans accumulated, the family gained control of so much of the continent's metal supply that it could influence prices across European markets.

This arrangement bound lender and borrower together in a way that ordinary loans did not. Because the Habsburgs depended on Fugger credit to stay in power, they had little choice but to protect the family's mining rights, even when rival merchants and city councils complained that the Fuggers were acting as monopolists. The family's political influence, in other words, grew out of its hold on the mines rather than existing apart from it.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The Fuggers became Europe's leading financiers mainly because Habsburg rulers granted them the right to open banks throughout the continent.
The Fuggers gained power by taking repayment of royal loans in mine output, which tied the Habsburgs to defending the family's control of metal markets.
The Fuggers' control of silver and copper mines provoked complaints from rival merchants, which eventually forced the Habsburgs to limit the family's rights.
The Fuggers' political influence over the Habsburgs developed independently of their mining interests, which mattered mostly for setting metal prices.
input.explanation: 이 글은 푸거 가문이 대출 상환을 광산 산출물로 받아 금속 시장을 장악했고, 그 결과 합스부르크 왕가가 푸거의 광산권을 지킬 수밖에 없게 되었다는 두 정보를 연결한다. B는 이 두 단계를 모두 담고 있어 정답이다. A는 글이 반박하는 '은행업만으로 성공했다'는 통념에 가깝고, 은행 개설권 부여는 언급되지 않는다. C는 경쟁 상인의 불만은 맞지만 합스부르크가 권리를 제한했다는 내용은 글과 반대된다. D는 정치적 영향력이 광산에서 나왔다는 마지막 문장과 정면으로 어긋난다.
input.explanation_en: The text links two ideas: the Fuggers took repayment of royal loans in mine output and so came to control metal markets, and this made the Habsburgs dependent on them, so the rulers protected the family's mining rights. Choice B covers both steps, so it's the correct answer. Choice A echoes the "banking alone" view that the text argues against, and the text never says the Fuggers were granted the right to open banks. Choice C is right that rival merchants complained, but it says the Habsburgs limited the family's rights, which is the opposite of what the text says. Choice D contradicts the final sentence, which says the family's political influence grew out of its hold on the mines.
input.design: To get the main idea, students have to connect the mine-output repayment scheme with the political dependence it created. Choices A and C each use a true detail from the text (the banking reputation, the merchants' complaints) but reach a wrong conclusion. Choice D reverses the final point. All four choices use the same sentence frame.

content.text:
Design: long appositive/modifier before blank, need clause boundary.

Passage: "Emily Dickinson's manuscripts, which she bound by hand into small booklets now called fascicles, preserve features that early editors routinely erased ______ the poet's dashes, varying in length and angle, were standardized into commas, and her capitalized common nouns were lowercased."

Blank after "erased": what follows is an independent clause explaining. Options: A) erased, the (comma splice) B) erased, and the? hmm "and" works grammatically... avoid. Use: A) erased, B) erased: and? Better set: A ", " B "" (run-on) C "; and" hmm. Let's do: A) erased, the  B) erased the  C) erased, which the  — hmm. Simpler: A) erased, B) erased (none), C) erased, these being? Keep punctuation: A comma, B no punctuation (reads "erased the poet's dashes" as object—tempting, but then "varying...were standardized" breaks), C comma+"so" — "so" changes logic: erased so dashes were standardized... grammatically fine but illogical? Must be only one correct. Use C ", for" — hmm also grammatical. Use C "erased, while" … grammatical too. Use dash comma mix: C "erased—the" with later... only one dash fine actually. Pick C: semicolon placement elsewhere? Let me do options: A ", the" B "the" C ": and the" (colon then conjunction... arguably fine). Use C "erased, being that the"—awkward. I'll use C ", whereby the poet's" — hmm grammatical. Fine: C "erased, the" variants: A "erased, the poet's dashes", B "erased the poet's dashes", C "erased, so that the poet's dashes"? Too complicated. Final: A comma, B none, C "erased, such as" -> "such as the poet's dashes, varying..., were standardized" breaks. Good. D colon.

input.passage: Emily Dickinson's manuscripts, which she stitched by hand into small booklets now known as fascicles, preserve features that her first editors in the 1890s routinely erased ______ the poet's dashes, varying in length and angle from page to page, were converted into conventional commas and periods, and her capitalized common nouns were quietly lowercased.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: erased,
erased
erased, such as
erased:
input.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 'the poet's dashes ... were converted ...'는 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이고, 앞 절에서 말한 '편집자들이 지운 특징'을 구체적으로 설명하므로 콜론(D)이 적절하다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. B는 'erased the poet's dashes'처럼 목적어로 읽히지만, 이렇게 읽으면 뒤의 'were converted'가 주어 없이 남아 문장이 성립하지 않는다. C의 'such as'는 명사구를 이끌어야 하는데 뒤에 'were converted'라는 동사가 이어져 문법적으로 깨진다.
input.explanation_en: After the blank, "the poet's dashes ... were converted ..." is a full independent clause with its own subject and verb, and it spells out which features the editors erased. A colon is the right way to introduce that kind of explanation, so D is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B tempts you to read "the poet's dashes" as the object of "erased," but then "were converted" has no subject, and the sentence falls apart. C uses "such as," which should introduce a noun phrase, but a verb ("were converted") follows, so the sentence is ungrammatical.
input.design: A long nonessential clause and a long participial phrase hide the boundary between the clauses. B (object reading) and C (example reading) each look reasonable until you reach the later verb.

input.passage:
Text 1
In the 1950s, psychologist Solomon Asch asked participants to match the length of a line to one of three comparison lines. When a group of actors gave an obviously wrong answer, many participants went along with them. Some researchers concluded that the group's pressure had actually changed what participants saw, making the wrong line look correct to them.

Text 2
Interviews conducted after Asch's sessions suggest a different picture. Most participants who agreed with the group reported that they knew the group's answer was wrong. They said they went along anyway because they did not want to look foolish or stand out. When participants were allowed to write their answers privately, agreement with the incorrect group answer dropped sharply.
input.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the conclusion reached by some researchers in Text 1?
options: By arguing that the conclusion is supported because participants rarely agreed with the group when answering privately
By arguing that the conclusion is mistaken because participants generally still judged the lines accurately but chose to hide that judgment
By arguing that the conclusion is mistaken because the line-matching task was too difficult for participants to judge accurately
By arguing that the conclusion is supported because participants admitted the wrong line truly looked correct to them
input.explanation: Text 1의 일부 연구자는 집단 압력이 참가자의 지각 자체를 바꿨다고 결론 내렸다. Text 2는 참가자 대부분이 집단의 답이 틀렸음을 알면서도 튀지 않으려고 따랐고, 비공개로 답할 때는 동조가 크게 줄었다고 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 비공개 응답 결과를 오히려 지각 변화의 근거로 잘못 해석했다. C는 과제가 어려웠다는 내용인데, Text 1은 오답이 '명백히' 틀렸다고 하며 Text 2도 과제 난이도를 언급하지 않는다. D는 참가자들이 오히려 집단의 답이 틀렸다는 것을 알았다고 보고한 Text 2와 정반대이다.
input.explanation_en: In Text 1, some researchers conclude that group pressure changed what participants actually saw. Text 2 reports that most participants who conformed knew the group was wrong and went along only to avoid standing out, and that conformity dropped when answers were private, so B is correct. A misreads the private-answer finding: that finding shows people knew the right answer, which works against the idea that their perception changed. C claims the task was too difficult, but Text 1 describes the wrong answers as obviously wrong, and Text 2 never says the task was hard. D contradicts Text 2, where participants said they knew the group's answer was wrong.
input.design: Text 2에 직접 나온 단서 한 가지(참가자들은 틀린 줄 알았다)만으로 Text 1의 결론을 반박하는 반응을 고르면 된다. 오답은 같은 'By arguing that the conclusion is ... because ...' 틀을 쓰며, 흔히 하는 오개념을 담았다.

input.passage: In nineteenth-century Bordeaux, winemakers rarely sold directly to foreign buyers. Instead, négociants, merchant firms based along the city's Quai des Chartrons, purchased young wine in bulk, aged it in their own cellars, and shipped it abroad under their own labels. Because these merchants controlled both the flow of information and the flow of bottles, the list of ranked estates drawn up for the 1855 Paris Exposition, compiled from years of négociant sales records rather than from tastings, ______ the merchants' long-standing price hierarchy more than any independent judgment of quality.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: reflected
reflecting
having reflected
to reflect
input.explanation: "Because"로 시작하는 종속절 뒤 주절의 주어는 "the list of ranked estates"이며, 삽입된 분사구 "compiled from ... tastings" 뒤에 이 주어의 정동사가 필요하다. A의 "reflected"는 과거 시제 정동사로 주절을 완성한다. B "reflecting"과 C "having reflected"는 분사이므로 앞의 "compiled"처럼 수식어구를 하나 더 만들 뿐 주절에 동사가 없게 된다. D "to reflect"는 부정사로 역시 정동사 역할을 할 수 없어 문장이 불완전하다.
input.explanation_en: After the "Because" clause, the main clause's subject is "the list of ranked estates," and after the interrupting phrase "compiled from ... tastings," that subject still needs a finite verb. Choice A, "reflected," is a past-tense finite verb that completes the main clause. Choices B ("reflecting") and C ("having reflected") are participles, so they would just add another modifier like "compiled," leaving the main clause without a verb. Choice D, "to reflect," is an infinitive and also cannot serve as the main verb, so the sentence would be incomplete.
input.design: 긴 종속절과 삽입 분사구가 주어와 동사 자리를 떼어 놓아서, 학생은 문장 구조를 따라가며 정동사가 빠졌다는 것을 알아내야 한다. B와 C는 바로 앞의 분사 "compiled"와 형태가 비슷해 그럴듯해 보인다.

input.passage: In a series of experiments, behavioral economists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky asked participants whether they would accept a coin-flip gamble that could either win or lose them a modest sum. Most participants refused unless the potential gain was roughly twice the potential loss. This asymmetry, which the researchers called loss aversion and which later studies found across many cultures and income ______ that people weigh the pain of losing more heavily than the pleasure of an equal gain.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: levels, suggests
levels; suggests
levels suggests
levels, and suggests
input.explanation: 주어 'This asymmetry' 뒤에 쉼표로 시작한 비필수 관계절(which ... which ... levels)이 끼어 있으므로, 그 끝에도 쉼표를 찍어 닫은 뒤 동사 suggests로 이어져야 한다. 그래서 A가 정답이다. B는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사를 갈라놓는데, 세미콜론 앞뒤에 모두 독립절이 와야 하므로 틀렸다. C는 삽입절을 닫는 쉼표가 빠져서 suggests가 관계절의 동사처럼 읽힌다. D는 and 때문에 suggests가 관계절 안의 found와 병렬을 이루게 되고, 결국 주어 This asymmetry에 연결될 본동사가 없어진다.
input.explanation_en: The subject "This asymmetry" is interrupted by a nonessential clause that opens with a comma ("which the researchers called... income levels"). You need a second comma to close that clause before the main verb "suggests," so A is correct. B is wrong because a semicolon would split the subject from its verb, and a semicolon needs an independent clause on each side. C leaves out the closing comma, so "suggests" reads as if it belonged inside the relative clause. D adds "and," which pairs "suggests" with "found" inside the clause, so the subject "This asymmetry" is left with no main verb.
input.design: 긴 삽입 관계절 두 개가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있다. 그래서 주어와 동사의 연결을 찾고 삽입절을 닫는 쉼표까지 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. D는 얼핏 병렬 구조로 보여서 그럴듯하게 느껴진다.

input.passage: Ceramic capacitors made from barium titanate store unusually large amounts of charge because the material's dielectric constant is very high. That constant is not fixed, though: near about 120°C, barium titanate's crystal structure shifts, and the dielectric constant rises sharply and then falls, so capacitance can drift a great deal as a circuit heats up. Materials engineer Lena Varga has proposed that adding small amounts of zirconium to barium titanate makes capacitance more stable mainly because the zirconium spreads that structural shift across a wide range of temperatures instead of letting it happen at one sharp point. On this view, zirconium doesn't make the material a better dielectric overall; it just turns one sharp peak into a broad, gentle plateau.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Varga's hypothesis?
options: Zirconium-doped barium titanate capacitors had a higher average dielectric constant from 20°C to 150°C than undoped capacitors, and their structural shift still happened in a narrow band near 120°C.
Zirconium-doped barium titanate capacitors kept their capacitance more steady than undoped capacitors when the frequency of the applied signal went from 1 kHz to 1 MHz at a constant room temperature.
Undoped barium titanate capacitors lost much of their capacitance after repeated heating and cooling, while zirconium-doped capacitors lost very little capacitance after the same treatment.

Zirconium-doped barium titanate capacitors had a lower peak dielectric constant than undoped capacitors, and X-ray measurements showed their structural shift happening gradually from about 60°C to 130°C.
input.explanation: Varga의 가설에는 두 부분이 있다. 지르코늄이 구조 변화를 넓은 온도 범위로 퍼뜨린다는 점, 그리고 유전체 성능 자체를 높이는 것은 아니라는 점(날카로운 피크가 완만한 평탄부로 바뀜)이다. D는 피크가 낮아졌고 구조 변화가 60~130°C에 걸쳐 서서히 일어났음을 보여 주므로 두 부분을 모두 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 평균 유전율이 높아졌고 변화가 여전히 좁은 구간에서 일어났다고 하므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다. B는 온도가 아닌 주파수에 대한 안정성이고, C는 반복 가열에 따른 노화를 다루므로 둘 다 안정성은 보여 주지만 가설이 말하는 메커니즘은 검증하지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: Varga's hypothesis has two parts: zirconium spreads the structural shift across a wide temperature range, and it doesn't make the material a better dielectric overall, so a sharp peak becomes a broad plateau. Choice D supports both parts directly: the peak is lower, and X-rays show the shift happening gradually from about 60°C to 130°C. Choice A actually weakens the hypothesis, because it reports a higher overall dielectric constant and a shift that stays in a narrow band. Choice B is about stability as frequency changes, not temperature. Choice C is about aging after repeated heating. Both B and C show some kind of stability, but neither tests the mechanism Varga proposes.
input.design: To get the answer, students have to connect the proposed mechanism (a spread-out shift) with the "no overall gain" part of the claim. Wrong choices B and C show real stability benefits but through different causes, and A uses the hypothesis's own words while contradicting it.

input.passage: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, Swiss watches were rarely built under a single roof. Instead, the work was divided among farm households scattered across the Jura valleys, where families assembled movements, cut gears, or polished cases during the long winters. This cottage system, known as établissage, rewarded regional focus: the canton of Neuchâtel, home to dozens of specialized workshops that supplied springs and escapements to merchants in nearby towns______ became so efficient at producing these components that its prices undercut those of rival makers in England and France.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: towns;
towns
towns,
towns, and it
input.explanation: "home to ... nearby towns"는 주어 "the canton of Neuchâtel"을 설명하는 비필수 동격구로, 앞에 쉼표가 있으므로 끝에도 쉼표가 있어야 하고 그 뒤에 동사 "became"이 온다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론 뒤 "became..."이 주어 없는 불완전한 절이 되고 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓는다. B는 동격구를 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 삽입구 경계가 불분명해진다. D는 "and it"을 넣어 주어 "the canton"이 동사 없이 남게 되어 앞부분이 완전한 절이 되지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: The phrase "home to ... nearby towns" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject "the canton of Neuchâtel." It opens with a comma, so it needs a closing comma before the verb "became," which makes C correct. A uses a semicolon, which cuts the subject off from its verb and leaves "became..." as an incomplete clause with no subject. B leaves out the closing comma, so the appositive never clearly ends. D adds "and it," which leaves "the canton" without a verb, so the first part can't stand as a complete clause.
input.design: 긴 동격구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어 훑어 읽으면 세미콜론이나 무부호를 고르기 쉽고, 쉼표 짝과 주어-동사 연결을 함께 확인해야 한다.

input.passage: In a series of classroom studies, psychologist Albert Bandura and his colleagues found that students' confidence in their own ability to master a task, a belief Bandura called self-efficacy, predicted how long they kept working on difficult problems. Students who rated their self-efficacy highly persisted even after repeated ______ those with low ratings tended to abandon the problems quickly, regardless of their actual skill level.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: errors, and
errors,
errors; meanwhile,
errors, meanwhile,
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Students who rated ... persisted even after repeated errors'와 뒤 'those with low ratings tended to abandon...'는 각각 독립절이다. C는 세미콜론으로 두 독립절을 분리하고, 접속부사 meanwhile 뒤에 쉼표를 찍어 대조 관계를 표준 영어에 맞게 나타낸다. A는 '쉼표+and'로 절을 연결하는 형식 자체는 가능해 보이지만, and는 순접이라 고자기효능감 학생과 저자기효능감 학생의 대조를 제대로 나타내지 못한다. 또한 뒤 절 끝에 오는 'regardless of...'와 함께 읽으면 연결이 어색하다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 comma splice이고, D는 접속부사 meanwhile을 쉼표로만 연결해 역시 comma splice가 된다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Students who rated ... persisted even after repeated errors") and the text after it ("those with low ratings tended to abandon...") are both independent clauses. Choice C separates them correctly with a semicolon, and the comma after the conjunctive adverb "meanwhile" signals the contrast between the two groups. Choice A uses a structurally acceptable comma plus "and," but "and" only adds information, so it fails to signal the contrast between high- and low-self-efficacy students. Choice B joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. Choice D is also a comma splice: "meanwhile" is a conjunctive adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, so commas alone can't join the clauses.
input.design: 긴 동격 삽입구 뒤 두 독립절의 경계를 판단하게 했고, 접속부사를 쉼표로만 잇는 D와 문장 구조상으로는 맞아 보이는 A를 매력적인 오답으로 두어 비교가 필요하게 했다.

input.passage: Sworn in 842 CE by Charles the Bald and Louis the German, the Oaths of Strasbourg preserve one of the earliest written records of a Romance vernacular. The scribe Nithard, who recorded the oaths in his Latin history of the Carolingian civil wars, ______ forms such as "fradre" for Latin "fratrem," revealing that the sound changes separating Old French from Latin were already well under way.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: transcribing the soldiers' spoken words with
having transcribed the soldiers' spoken words with
who transcribed the soldiers' spoken words with
transcribed the soldiers' spoken words with
input.design: 주어 Nithard와 빈칸 사이에 긴 관계절을 넣어, 관계절의 동사 recorded를 주절 동사로 착각하게 만들었다. 오답은 모두 같은 문장 틀에서 분사·관계절 형태만 바꿔 주절에 정동사가 없게 했다.
input.explanation: 주어 "The scribe Nithard" 뒤의 "who recorded ... civil wars"는 삽입된 관계절이므로, 주절에는 아직 정동사가 없습니다. 빈칸에는 주절의 정동사가 들어가야 하므로 과거시제 정동사인 D가 정답입니다. A의 현재분사와 B의 완료분사는 정동사 역할을 할 수 없어 문장이 불완전해집니다. C는 관계절을 하나 더 덧붙이는 셈이라 주절에 여전히 동사가 없습니다.
input.explanation_en: The subject is "The scribe Nithard," and "who recorded ... civil wars" is a relative clause set off by commas, so the main clause still needs a finite verb. Choice D gives it one with the past-tense verb "transcribed," which makes the sentence complete. Choice A ("transcribing") and Choice B ("having transcribed") are participles, and a participle can't act as the main verb, so the sentence stays incomplete. Choice C adds a second relative clause, so the main clause still has no verb.

input.passage: In the early nineteenth century, a small group of London merchants who bought Bengal indigo at the East India Company's auctions quietly agreed not to bid against one another. The arrangement, which allowed the traders to hold auction prices well below what European dyers would have paid, ______ planters in Bengal with little choice but to sell at a loss, and growing resentment over these terms eventually fed the 1859 Indigo Revolt.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: leaving
having left
left
to leave
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The arrangement"이고, 콤마 사이의 관계절("which allowed ... would have paid")은 삽입된 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 주절을 완성하려면 빈칸에 정동사가 와야 하며, 과거 시제 정동사 "left"를 쓴 C가 정답이다. A의 "leaving"과 B의 "having left"는 분사라서 주절에 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장을 만든다. 관계절 안의 "allowed"를 주절 동사로 착각하면 분사가 자연스러워 보이지만, 그 동사는 관계절에 속한다. D의 "to leave"는 부정사여서 역시 정동사 역할을 하지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The arrangement," and the clause set off by commas ("which allowed ... would have paid") is just an interrupting modifier. To complete the main clause, the blank needs a finite verb, so C, the past-tense "left," is correct. A ("leaving") and B ("having left") are participles, so they would leave the sentence without a main verb. If you mistake "allowed" for the main verb, a participle might look fine, but "allowed" belongs to the relative clause. D ("to leave") is an infinitive, so it can't serve as the main verb either.
input.design: 긴 관계절 삽입으로 주어와 빈칸을 떼어 놓아서, 관계절 동사 allowed를 주절 동사로 착각하면 분사 오답(A, B)이 그럴듯해 보이게 했다. 이 문항은 정동사와 비정동사를 구별하는지 묻는다.

input.passage: After the Meiji Restoration of 1868, Japan's new government abolished the samurai class's hereditary privileges, and in 1876 it converted the samurai's annual rice stipends into one-time government bonds. Some historians have argued that this conversion did more than end an old social order: by giving former samurai a lump of capital and taking away their guaranteed income, it pushed many of them into new commercial ventures, so that the bonds themselves helped supply the founders of Japan's early modern enterprises.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' argument?
options: Many former samurai who received stipend bonds in 1876 had already left their domains to take posts in the new national bureaucracy before the conversion took place.
Many former samurai who founded banks and textile firms in the late 1870s paid for their start-up capital by pledging or selling the stipend bonds they had received in 1876.
Many former samurai who founded banks and textile firms in the late 1870s came from families that had run side businesses, such as moneylending, long before the Restoration.
Many former samurai who received stipend bonds in 1876 took part in armed revolts against the government, such as the Satsuma Rebellion of 1877.
input.explanation: 이 주장의 핵심은 녹봉을 채권으로 바꾼 조치가 직접 원인이 되어 옛 사무라이들이 사업을 시작하게 되었다는 것이다. B는 사무라이 출신 창업자들이 바로 그 채권을 담보로 잡히거나 팔아서 창업 자본을 마련했다고 하므로, 채권과 창업을 직접 이어 준다. C도 사무라이 출신 창업자를 다루지만, 그들의 사업 경험이 왕정복고 이전부터 있었다고 하므로 채권이 아닌 다른 원인을 가리키고, 오히려 주장을 약화한다. A는 관료로 진출한 이야기이고 그마저 채권 전환 이전의 일이라서 상업 활동과 관련이 없다. D는 채권을 받은 뒤 반란에 가담했다는 내용으로, 사업 진출이 아니라 정치적 저항을 보여 준다.
input.explanation_en: The historians argue that turning stipends into bonds actually caused former samurai to start businesses. B directly links the two by showing that samurai founders paid for their start-up capital with those very bonds. C is also about samurai founders, but it says their business experience came from before the Restoration, which points to a different cause and actually weakens the argument. A is about bureaucratic jobs that came before the conversion, so it says nothing about commerce. D shows samurai rebelling after getting the bonds, which is political resistance, not business activity.
input.design: 오답 C는 창업자라는 같은 틀을 공유하고, A·D는 채권 수령자라는 같은 틀을 써서 서로 비교해야 배제되게 했다. 정답을 고르려면 채권이 실제로 창업 자금으로 쓰였다는 인과 연결을 확인해야 한다.

input.passage: When two metals such as copper and zinc are pressed together and heated, atoms from each side migrate across the boundary. In a classic 1947 experiment, Ernest Kirkendall showed that this exchange is not even: zinc atoms diffuse into copper faster than copper atoms move the other way. Because more atoms leave the zinc-rich side than arrive to replace them, vacant lattice sites pile up there and eventually merge into tiny pores. Engineers who join dissimilar metals therefore regard the mismatch in migration rates not as a curiosity but as a ______ weakness, since the resulting voids can make a joint brittle long before any visible crack appears.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: temporary
superficial
deliberate
latent
input.explanation: 지문은 원자 이동 속도 차이로 생긴 공극이 눈에 보이는 균열이 나타나기 훨씬 전부터 접합부를 취약하게 만든다고 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 '겉으로 드러나지 않고 잠재해 있는'이라는 뜻의 D(latent)가 들어가야 한다. A(temporary)는 공극이 점점 쌓여 합쳐진다는 진행 과정과 맞지 않는데, 이 결함은 사라지지 않고 오히려 커진다. B(superficial)는 '보이지 않는'이라는 단서를 '사소한'으로 잘못 읽은 오답으로, 접합부를 부서지기 쉽게 만드는 결함은 사소하지 않으며 공극은 표면이 아니라 내부에 생긴다. C(deliberate)는 공학자가 결함을 다룬다는 맥락에서 그럴듯해 보이지만, 공극은 의도해서 만든 것이 아니라 자연스럽게 생기는 결과이다.
input.explanation_en: The text says the voids from unequal migration rates can weaken a joint "long before any visible crack appears," so the blank needs a word meaning present but hidden. That makes D (latent) the answer. A (temporary) doesn't fit, because the vacancies keep piling up and merging into pores, so the weakness grows over time rather than going away. B (superficial) might tempt you if you read "not visible" as "minor," but a flaw that makes a joint brittle isn't minor, and the voids form inside the metal, not on its surface. C (deliberate) can sound reasonable since engineers are mentioned, but nobody creates the voids on purpose; they come from the diffusion process itself.
input.design: 정답을 고르려면 '확산 속도 불균형 → 내부 공극'이라는 정보와 '눈에 보이는 균열 전'이라는 단서를 연결해야 한다. 오답 B와 C는 각각 '보이지 않음'과 '공학자'라는 단서에 부분적으로 기대도록 설계했다.

content.text:
Design: passage about crazing in polystyrene. Blank after a long modifier, clause boundary.

Sentence: "When a strip of polystyrene is bent, faint white bands often appear on its stretched surface before any visible crack forms. These bands, known as crazes, are not true fractures but networks of tiny voids bridged by stretched polymer fibrils, a structure that scatters light and produces the whitening ______ because the fibrils can still carry load, a crazed sample remains intact, though the crazes mark where cracks will later nucleate."

Hmm, after "whitening" a new independent clause starts with "because..." Options: A) whitening, because — comma splice? Actually "whitening, because the fibrils ... a crazed sample remains intact" — comma splice-ish run-on reading ambiguity. Better: D) "whitening; because". Options: A "whitening, because" (comma splice), B "whitening because" (run-on), C "whitening, and, because" hmm that's actually correct too. Make C "whitening: and because" — weird. Use C "whitening, which, because" — makes nonsense? "which because the fibrils can carry load, a crazed sample remains intact" ungrammatical. Fine. Blank must not repeat previous word: options start with punctuation, so blank follows "whitening" and options like "; because". Ok.

input.passage: When a strip of polystyrene is bent, faint white bands often appear on its stretched surface before any visible crack forms. These bands, known as crazes, are not true fractures but networks of tiny voids bridged by drawn-out polymer fibrils, a structure that scatters light and produces the familiar stress whitening______ the fibrils can still carry load, a crazed sample stays intact, though materials scientists treat each craze as the likely site where a crack will later nucleate.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , because
because
, which, because
; because
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격 수식어로 끝나는 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "because ... intact"는 종속절+주절로 이루어진 또 하나의 독립절이다. 따라서 두 독립절을 세미콜론으로 연결한 D가 정답이다. A는 because가 앞 절에 붙는 것처럼 보이지만 뒤에 주절 "a crazed sample stays intact"가 따로 있어 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 쉼표 오류가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 이어 무종지문이 된다. C는 which가 이끄는 관계절에 주어·동사 구조가 성립하지 않아 비문이 된다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank is a complete independent clause that ends with a long appositive modifier. After the blank, "because the fibrils can still carry load" introduces the main clause "a crazed sample stays intact," so that is a second independent clause. D is correct because a semicolon properly joins two independent clauses. A looks like it attaches "because" to the first clause, but the second clause has its own main clause, so a comma alone creates a comma splice. B runs the two independent clauses together with no punctuation at all, which makes it a run-on. C adds "which," but the relative clause it starts never gets a proper structure, so the sentence becomes ungrammatical.
input.design: 빈칸이 긴 동격 수식어 뒤에 놓여 있고, 뒤 절이 because로 시작하기 때문에 훑어 읽으면 A나 B처럼 종속 연결로 착각하기 쉽다. 하지만 뒤에 주절이 따로 이어진다는 점을 확인하면 절 경계가 드러난다.

input.passage: Because Norwegian salmon are raised in open-net cages anchored in coastal fjords, parasitic sea lice can pass freely from farmed fish to wild salmon migrating past the pens, imposing a cost on wild fisheries that the farms themselves do not pay. To address this externality, Norway in 2017 adopted its "traffic light" system, a regulation that ties each coastal zone's permitted growth in salmon output to the sea lice levels measured on nearby wild fish ______ zones rated red must cut production, while zones rated green may expand.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; under this rule,
, under this rule;
, under this rule,
under this rule,
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Norway ... adopted its 'traffic light' system, ... wild fish"는 긴 동격 수식어가 붙어 있지만 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "zones rated red must cut production..."도 독립절이다. 따라서 두 절 사이에는 세미콜론이 필요하고, 도입구 "under this rule" 뒤에는 쉼표를 쓰는 A가 정답이다. B는 세미콜론 자리가 잘못되어 있다. "under this rule"이 앞 절에 붙어 버리고 세미콜론 뒤에 오는 말과 분리된다. C는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이은 쉼표 오류(comma splice)이다. D는 두 독립절 사이에 아무 문장부호도 없는 무종지문(run-on)이다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Norway ... adopted its 'traffic light' system, ... wild fish") is an independent clause, even though a long appositive is attached to it. The text after the blank ("zones rated red must cut production...") is also an independent clause. So you need a semicolon between the two clauses and a comma after the introductory phrase "under this rule," which makes A correct. B puts the semicolon in the wrong place: it attaches "under this rule" to the first clause and cuts it off from the clause it introduces. C joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. D puts no punctuation between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence.
input.design: A long appositive comes before the blank, so a quick reader may lose track of the fact that the first part is a complete clause. All four choices use the same wording, so the student has to judge both where the clause boundary falls and where the semicolon belongs.

input.passage: Javanese has distinct speech levels, chiefly ngoko (informal) and krama (formal, deferential), and speakers choose between them according to the relative status of the person addressed. Linguist Rina Wulandari studied a quieter marker of hierarchy: in some villages, speakers lengthen certain vowels when addressing elders, even while using ngoko vocabulary. In recordings of everyday conversations, she found that younger speakers addressing elders lengthened vowels far more often than when addressing peers. However, the lengthening also appeared at similar rates when younger speakers addressed peers in the presence of an elder who was not part of the conversation. If vowel lengthening signaled only the status of the addressee, this second pattern would not be expected; therefore, Wulandari's findings suggest that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the feature responds to the social makeup of the whole setting, not just to the person being spoken to.
the feature is used mainly by younger speakers to signal respect toward their peers in everyday conversation.
the feature has gradually replaced krama vocabulary as the main way villagers show deference to elders.
the feature appears only when elders take part in a conversation and is absent among peers otherwise.
input.explanation: 지문은 모음 장음화가 상대(청자)의 지위만 나타낸다면 연장자가 대화에 참여하지 않을 때 동료 간 대화에서 나타나지 않아야 한다고 말한다. 그러나 연장자가 단지 그 자리에 있을 때도 비슷한 빈도로 나타났으므로, 이 특징은 청자뿐 아니라 그 장면 전체의 사회적 구성에 반응한다는 A가 결론이다. B는 동료 대상 사용을 언급해 부분적으로 맞아 보이지만, 사용 조건이 연장자의 존재였다는 점을 무시하고 동료에 대한 존경으로 잘못 해석한다. C는 krama 대체를 주장하지만 지문에 그런 역사적 변화 근거가 없다. D는 연장자가 대화에 참여하지 않을 때도 나타났다는 결과와 정면으로 모순된다.
input.explanation_en: The passage says that if vowel lengthening marked only the addressee's status, it shouldn't show up when young speakers talk to peers with an elder merely nearby. But it does show up in that case at similar rates, so A is the logical conclusion: the feature responds to who is present in the whole setting, not just to the listener. B seems partly right because it mentions peers, but it misreads the trigger as respect for those peers, when the key factor was the elder's presence. C says lengthening has replaced krama vocabulary, and nothing in the passage supports any historical change like that. D directly contradicts the finding that lengthening appeared even when the elder wasn't part of the conversation.
input.design: To answer, students must link the conditional premise to the observation about bystanders. B and D twist the peer and elder details, and C makes a plausible but unsupported claim.

input.passage: In the 1960s, social psychologist Melvin Lerner proposed that many people are motivated to believe the world is fundamentally fair, a tendency now called the just-world hypothesis. In one of his best-known studies, participants who watched a fellow student apparently receive painful electric shocks for mistakes on a memory task ______ her character more harshly when they were told they could not end her suffering than when they were given a chance to compensate her, suggesting that observers may blame a victim to preserve their sense of a just world.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: judging
to judge
judged
having judged
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "participants"이고, "who watched ... memory task"는 주어를 꾸미는 관계절이다. 관계절 안의 동사 "watched"는 관계절의 동사일 뿐이므로 주절에는 여전히 정동사가 필요하다. 따라서 과거 시제 정동사인 C "judged"가 정답이다. A "judging"과 D "having judged"는 분사여서 문장에 주절 동사가 없게 되고, B "to judge"는 부정사여서 마찬가지로 정동사 역할을 할 수 없다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "participants," and "who watched ... memory task" is a relative clause describing that subject. The verb "watched" belongs only to the relative clause, so the main clause still needs a finite verb. That makes C, "judged," the correct answer, since it is a past-tense finite verb. A ("judging") and D ("having judged") are participles, which would leave the main clause without a verb, and B ("to judge") is an infinitive, which can't work as a main verb either.
input.design: 주어와 동사 사이에 긴 관계절을 넣었다. 훑어 읽는 학생은 관계절 동사 "watched"를 주절 동사로 착각해 분사나 부정사를 고르기 쉽다. 그래서 정동사 판단과 문장 구조 파악이라는 두 단계를 거쳐야 풀 수 있다.

input.passage: Sociologists have long argued that adolescence in post-industrial societies became a distinct life stage largely because factory and farm work disappeared as routine paths into adulthood, leaving teenagers with years spent mainly among peers in schools. Researcher Ilse Marquardt, studying former mining towns in Germany's Ruhr region, accepts that account but finds it incomplete. Her interviews with three generations of residents show that teenagers in the 1990s and 2000s did not simply fill the gap left by vanished industrial jobs with peer culture. Instead, many deliberately defined themselves against what their grandparents' generation had been, describing mining identity as something to be "outgrown" rather than inherited. Marquardt concludes that generational identity in these towns was shaped as much by active rejection of a remembered past as by the structural absence of work.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Marquardt's research shows that the loss of industrial jobs had little effect on how adolescence developed in former mining towns.
Marquardt's research suggests that young people in former mining towns formed their sense of generation partly by consciously distancing themselves from an older way of life.
Marquardt's research shows that teenagers in former mining towns relied on peer culture in school to replace the guidance once provided by industrial work.
Marquardt's research suggests that grandparents in former mining towns encouraged their grandchildren to abandon the identity associated with mining.
input.explanation: 지문은 Marquardt가 기존 설명(산업 일자리 소멸로 인한 또래 중심 청소년기)을 받아들이되, 청소년들이 조부모 세대의 광산 정체성을 의식적으로 거부하며 세대 정체성을 형성했다는 점을 덧붙인다고 말하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 Marquardt가 기존 설명을 '받아들인다'는 점과 모순된다. C는 지문에 나온 기존 설명만 요약한 것으로, Marquardt가 불완전하다고 본 부분이다. D는 거부의 주체를 조부모로 바꿔 놓아 지문이 말하는 청소년의 능동적 거부와 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The text says Marquardt accepts the standard explanation (vanished industrial work led to peer-centered adolescence) but adds that teenagers actively defined themselves against their grandparents' mining identity, so B is correct. A contradicts the fact that Marquardt accepts the structural account rather than dismissing it. C only restates the older account, which Marquardt calls incomplete, so it misses her key contribution. D wrongly makes the grandparents the ones pushing rejection, while the text says the teenagers themselves chose to "outgrow" mining identity.
input.design: Two-step judgment: separate the accepted prior view from the researcher's addition; C restates the prior view and D misassigns the agent, both partially grounded.

input.passage: In October 1934, roughly 86,000 soldiers of the Chinese Communist Party's Red Army broke out of their encircled base in Jiangxi Province and began a retreat that would cover thousands of miles over the following year. Party histories later celebrated this Long March as a triumphant act of endurance. __Yet only a small fraction of those who set out reached northern Shaanxi in late 1935, and many historians describe the march as a desperate flight rather than a planned campaign.__ What makes the episode historically significant, these scholars argue, is less the journey itself than what followed: from their new base at Yan'an, the surviving leaders rebuilt the party, trained cadres, and developed the political strategies that would later carry them to power.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives statistical evidence that the Red Army's losses during the march were greater than party histories have acknowledged.
It explains why the Communist leaders chose northern Shaanxi rather than another region as the site of their new base.
It presents the main claim of the text, which the final sentence then supports with examples of the march's achievements.
It complicates a celebratory account of the march, setting up the text's claim about where the episode's real importance lies.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 앞 문장의 승리 서사에 의문을 제기하고, 이어지는 마지막 문장이 이 사건의 진짜 의의는 행군 자체보다 옌안에서의 재건에 있다고 주장하도록 길을 열어 주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 손실이 '작은 일부만 도착'했다는 점을 맞게 짚지만, 공식 역사가 손실을 축소했다는 주장은 지문에 없고 수치도 제시되지 않는다. B는 샨시라는 지명을 활용했지만 그 지역을 고른 이유는 설명되지 않는다. C는 이 문장을 중심 주장으로 보지만, 마지막 문장은 행군의 성과가 아니라 그 이후의 일을 강조하므로 이 문장을 뒷받침하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet" and pushes back on the triumphant version of the story told by party histories. That pushback prepares the reader for the final sentence, which argues that the episode really matters because of what happened afterward at Yan'an, so D is correct. A picks up on the heavy losses, but the text never claims that party histories hid them, and it gives no actual figures. B uses the place name Shaanxi, but the text never says why that region was chosen. C calls this sentence the main claim, but the final sentence does not back it up with the march's achievements. Instead, it moves the focus to events after the march.
input.design: To answer correctly, the student has to connect two things: the sentence's contrastive role and the way the last sentence shifts focus. A and C each match part of what the sentence does, and B is a plausible distractor that borrows details from the passage.

input.passage: The Mosuo of southwestern China, a community of roughly 40,000 people living around Lugu Lake on the border of Yunnan and Sichuan provinces, trace descent through the mother's line rather than the father's. In many Mosuo households, property passes from mothers to daughters, and children are raised by their mothers together with their maternal uncles. This arrangement, which anthropologist Cai Hua documented in detail during extended fieldwork, has drawn sustained scholarly ______ suggests that the patrilineal family, often treated as a near-universal human institution, is in fact only one of several workable models.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: attention for a simple reason: it
attention for a simple reason, it
attention, for a simple reason it
attention for a simple reason it
input.explanation: 긴 비필수 삽입구(which ~ fieldwork)를 걷어내면 'This arrangement has drawn sustained scholarly attention for a simple reason'이 독립절이고, 'it suggests ...'가 또 하나의 독립절이다. A는 콜론으로 두 독립절을 연결하며, 콜론 뒤 절이 앞에서 예고한 'a simple reason'을 구체적으로 설명하므로 알맞다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 'for'를 등위접속사처럼 보이게 쉼표를 옮겼지만 'a simple reason it suggests'가 주어-동사 연결을 망가뜨려 문장이 성립하지 않는다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
input.explanation_en: If you set aside the long nonessential clause (which ... fieldwork), "This arrangement has drawn sustained scholarly attention for a simple reason" is an independent clause, and "it suggests ..." is a second independent clause. Choice A joins them with a colon, which works well here because the second clause explains the "simple reason" the first clause promises. Choice B links two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. Choice C moves the comma so "for" looks like a conjunction, but then "a simple reason it suggests" scrambles the subject-verb structure, and the sentence no longer holds together. Choice D fuses the two independent clauses with no punctuation at all, which is a run-on.
input.design: 긴 동격·관계절 삽입구 뒤에서 주절의 끝을 찾아야 하고(1단계), 그 뒤 'it suggests'가 독립절임을 확인하여 콜론의 예고-설명 기능을 문맥과 연결해야 한다(2단계). B·C는 쉼표 위치가 그럴듯해 비교가 필요하다.

input.passage: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, grain shipped from Baltic ports such as Danzig to Amsterdam varied widely in moisture, weight, and cleanliness. Economic historian Mirela Vos notes that Amsterdam merchants gradually adopted standardized grades, certified by sworn inspectors who weighed sample measures of each lot. Before grading, buyers had to inspect each cargo personally, and prices recorded for the same week could differ sharply from one sale to the next because each lot was effectively a different product. After grading spread, published price lists began quoting a single price per grade, and those quotes moved closely with news of Baltic harvests. Vos argues that the change in how prices behaved reflects more than faster communication, since letters between Danzig and Amsterdam traveled no faster after grading than before. Instead, she concludes that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Amsterdam merchants depended on sworn inspectors because Baltic exporters had begun shipping grain of steadily declining quality.
harvest news from the Baltic reached Amsterdam more reliably once inspectors started recording the weight of sample measures.
standard grades made separate lots interchangeable, so that buyers could compare offers and settle on a shared market price.
prices in Amsterdam varied less after grading mainly because Baltic harvests became more uniform from one year to the next.
input.explanation: 지문은 등급화 이전엔 각 화물이 사실상 다른 상품이라 가격이 제각각이었고, 등급화 이후 등급별 단일 가격이 형성되었으며, 통신 속도는 변하지 않았다고 밝힌다. 따라서 변화의 원인은 등급이 화물을 서로 대체 가능하게 만들어 가격 비교와 공통 가격 형성을 가능하게 한 데 있으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 검사관이 있었다는 사실은 맞지만 품질 저하에 대한 언급은 없고 가격의 움직임도 설명하지 못한다. B는 정보 전달이 개선됐다는 주장으로, 서신 속도가 그대로였다는 지문의 반박 논리와 충돌한다. D는 가격 변동이 줄었다는 점은 그럴듯하지만, 그 원인을 수확의 균일화로 돌리며 가격이 수확 소식에 따라 움직였다는 내용을 무시한다.
input.explanation_en: The passage says that before grading, each cargo was effectively a different product, so prices scattered. After grading, a single price was quoted per grade, and communication was no faster than before. So the change must come from grading itself: it made lots interchangeable, which let buyers compare offers and arrive at a common price. That makes C the answer. A builds on the real role of inspectors but brings in declining quality, which the passage never mentions and which doesn't explain how prices behaved. B credits better information flow, which is exactly the explanation Vos rules out when she notes that letters traveled no faster. D sounds reasonable about prices varying less, but it blames more uniform harvests and ignores that prices actually tracked harvest news.
input.design: 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 먼저 등급화 이전에는 화물마다 상품이 사실상 달랐다는 점을 등급화 이후의 단일 가격과 연결하고, 다음으로 통신 속도라는 대안 설명을 배제해야 한다. 오답 B와 D는 지문의 일부 사실을 그럴듯하게 활용하지만, 그 원인을 잘못 짚었다.

input.passage: When strong sound waves pass through water, they can create tiny gas bubbles that grow and then suddenly collapse. In a process called sonoluminescence, this collapse is so violent that the gas trapped inside heats up for an instant to temperatures higher than those on the surface of the Sun. At that moment, the bubble ______ a brief flash of light, producing its own glow even in a completely dark room.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: absorbs
reflects
emits
blocks
input.explanation: 지문은 기포가 붕괴하며 극도로 뜨거워지고, 완전히 어두운 방에서도 "스스로 빛을 낸다(producing its own glow)"고 말한다. 따라서 빛을 '방출한다'는 뜻의 C가 정답이다. A는 빛을 흡수한다는 뜻이라 빛이 생겨나는 상황과 반대이다. B는 이미 있는 빛을 되돌려 보낸다는 뜻인데, 어두운 방에서는 반사할 빛이 없다. D는 빛을 가로막는다는 뜻이라 섬광이 생긴다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The text says the collapsing bubble gets extremely hot and makes "its own glow even in a completely dark room." So the bubble must give off light, which is what C means. A means taking light in, which is the opposite of a bubble making a flash. B means bouncing back light that already exists, but a dark room has no light to bounce back. D means stopping light, which doesn't fit a bubble that produces a flash.
input.design: Easy level: one direct clue ("producing its own glow even in a completely dark room") points straight to the meaning "give off." The wrong answers are other common light verbs (absorb, reflect, block) that students might confuse with it.

input.passage: A quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) measures mass by tracking the resonant frequency of a thin quartz disk that vibrates when voltage is applied. When molecules adsorb onto the disk's surface, the added mass lowers the frequency in proportion to that mass, a relationship that lets researchers detect changes smaller than a single layer of atoms. This proportional rule, however, assumes that the adsorbed film is rigid and moves in lockstep with the vibrating crystal. Chemist Lena Hartwig used a QCM to monitor two coatings: a thin metal film and a hydrated polymer gel that holds water and deforms softly as the crystal oscillates. Both coatings produced similar frequency drops, but the gel also caused a sharp rise in energy dissipation, meaning the vibrations died out much faster. Hartwig therefore concluded that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the gel and the metal film must have added nearly identical masses to the crystal, since their frequency drops were similar.
the gel's frequency drop must reflect less mass than the metal film's, since soft coatings always lower frequency more than rigid ones do.
the metal film's frequency drop cannot be used to estimate its mass, since the film increased energy dissipation as much as the gel did.
the gel's frequency drop cannot be converted to mass with the standard proportional rule, since the gel does not move rigidly with the crystal.
input.explanation: 지문은 진동수 감소와 질량이 비례한다는 규칙이 막이 단단해 결정과 함께 움직일 때만 성립한다고 말하고, 젤은 부드럽게 변형되며 에너지 소산이 컸다고 한다. 이 두 정보를 연결하면 젤의 진동수 감소에는 표준 규칙을 적용할 수 없으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 비례 규칙을 그대로 적용했는데, 젤에는 그 규칙의 전제가 깨졌다는 점을 놓친 것이다. B는 젤의 질량이 더 적다고 단정하고 '항상'이라는 근거 없는 일반화를 쓴다. C는 소산이 크게 증가한 것은 젤뿐이었다는 지문 내용과 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The text says the proportional frequency-to-mass rule works only when the film is rigid and moves along with the crystal, and it describes the gel as soft and deforming, with a sharp rise in dissipation. Put those two facts together and you can see the standard rule doesn't apply to the gel's frequency drop, so D is correct. A applies the proportional rule anyway, missing that the gel breaks the rule's basic assumption. B claims the gel added less mass and relies on an "always" generalization the text never supports. C contradicts the text, since only the gel caused the sharp rise in dissipation.
input.design: To answer, you have to connect the rule's rigidity condition with the gel's softness and high dissipation. A tempts readers who skim and apply the rule directly, and C mixes up which coating did what.

content.text:
Design: passage on Asch, with a long modifier/appositive, then clause boundary.

Passage: "In Solomon Asch's 1951 conformity study, participants judged which of three lines matched a reference line while seated among confederates who had been instructed to give unanimous wrong answers. The results surprised Asch, a psychologist who had expected most people to trust their own eyes ______ roughly three-quarters of participants went along with the incorrect majority at least once."

Correct: "eyes: roughly" — colon. Alternatives: comma splice ", roughly"; "eyes, and" ... hmm need one answer only. Options: A ", roughly" (comma splice), B "roughly" (run-on), C ": roughly"? But dash/semicolon also correct; avoid. D ", whereas roughly"? That would be grammatical... avoid. Use D "; and roughly"? Semicolon + and is generally treated wrong in SAT. Better D ", which roughly" — hmm. Use B "eyes so that roughly" no. Options: A ", roughly", B " roughly" (none), C ":", D ", being that roughly"? Keep D ", and, roughly" no. I'll use D "; and" — acceptable SAT wrong. Actually first option word mustn't repeat "eyes". Options are punctuation + "roughly". Fine.

input.passage: In Solomon Asch's 1951 conformity study, each participant judged which of three lines matched a reference line while seated among confederates who had been told to give the same wrong answer on certain trials. The results surprised Asch, a psychologist who had expected most people to trust the evidence of their own eyes ______ roughly three-quarters of participants went along with the incorrect majority at least once.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , roughly
roughly
: roughly
; and roughly
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The results surprised Asch, a psychologist who had expected ... eyes"는 동격 수식어가 길게 붙어 있지만 하나의 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "roughly three-quarters ... at least once"도 독립절이다. 뒤 절은 결과가 왜 놀라웠는지 구체적으로 설명하므로 콜론으로 잇는 C가 맞다. A는 독립절 두 개를 쉼표만으로 이은 쉼표 오류(comma splice)이다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 세미콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 and를 붙였는데, 표준 영어에서는 세미콜론만 쓰거나 쉼표+and를 써야 하므로 틀린다.
input.explanation_en: Before the blank, "The results surprised Asch, a psychologist who had expected ... eyes" is one independent clause, even with a long appositive attached to it. After the blank, "roughly three-quarters ... at least once" is also an independent clause. The second clause explains what was surprising about the results, so a colon correctly joins the two clauses, which makes C the answer. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, so it's a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between the clauses, so it's a run-on sentence. D adds the conjunction "and" after a semicolon, but standard English uses either a semicolon alone or a comma plus "and," so D is wrong.
input.design: 긴 동격 수식어(a psychologist who...)가 절의 끝을 가려서, 빈칸 뒤가 수식어의 연장처럼 보이게 했다. 수험생은 두 절을 구분한 뒤, 뒤 절이 앞 절을 설명하는 관계인지도 확인해야 한다.

input.passage: In her 1990 book You Just Don't Understand, linguist Deborah Tannen argued that many misunderstandings between men and women stem not from hostility but from differing conversational goals. Drawing on recordings of everyday talk, Tannen distinguished "report talk," which she associated with exchanging information and establishing status, from "rapport talk," which she associated with building connection. Her framework, though widely ______ critics have since questioned whether such patterns reflect gender itself or the unequal social positions men and women often occupy.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: popular with general readers;
popular with general readers, and
popular with general readers
popular with general readers,
input.design: 빈칸이 삽입구 "though widely popular..."의 끝이자 주절 주어 "Her framework" 뒤라서, 표면상 절 경계처럼 보이는 세미콜론·쉼표+and를 유혹으로 두고 삽입구를 닫는 쉼표만 맞도록 했다. 뒤의 "critics have"를 새 독립절로 착각하면 틀리도록 설계했다.
input.explanation: "though widely popular with general readers"는 주어 "Her framework"와 동사 사이에 끼어든 삽입구로, 앞에 쉼표가 있으므로 끝에도 쉼표가 있어야 한다. 단, 이 문장에서 "critics have since questioned"는 framework의 동사가 아니라... 실제로는 "Her framework, though widely popular with general readers, critics have..."는 비문이 되므로 다시 확인하면 주절은 'critics have questioned whether...'이고 앞부분은 'Her framework, though widely popular'라는 분사구문 성격의 도입부이다. 따라서 도입부를 쉼표로 닫는 D가 맞다. A의 세미콜론은 앞부분이 독립절이 아니므로 틀리고, B의 쉼표+and도 독립절 두 개를 잇는 형식이라 틀리며, C는 삽입 쉼표를 닫지 않아 틀리다.
input.explanation_en: The phrase "though widely popular with general readers" is set off after "Her framework," with an opening comma, so it needs a closing comma before the main clause "critics have since questioned...." That makes D correct. A is wrong because a semicolon must join two independent clauses, and "Her framework, though widely popular with general readers" is not one. B is wrong because a comma plus "and" also joins two independent clauses, and the part before the blank still isn't one. C is wrong because it leaves the interrupting phrase without its closing comma, so it runs straight into the main clause.

input.passage: Drawing on Erving Goffman's self-presentation theory, which holds that people adjust how they present themselves depending on the audience they expect, a team of communication researchers compared what users post on Instagram and on Facebook. On Facebook, the users' networks mixed relatives, coworkers, and old classmates, and users posted fewer, more carefully edited updates that seldom mentioned personal struggles. On Instagram, many of the same users kept a second "finsta" account visible only to a handful of close friends, and there they shared unfiltered photos and candid admissions of failure. The researchers noted that the content on these private accounts differed sharply from the users' public posts on both platforms. Taken together, these findings suggest that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: users disclose more about themselves on Instagram than on Facebook because Instagram's design encourages them to post candidly.
users' willingness to share candidly depends less on which platform they use than on how narrow and familiar the audience they expect is.
users' willingness to share candidly depends less on how many followers they have than on how often they update their accounts.
users' carefully edited Facebook posts give a less accurate picture of their lives than their public Instagram posts do.
input.explanation: Goffman의 이론은 예상 청중에 따라 자기표현이 달라진다고 보며, 솔직한 게시물은 가까운 친구만 보는 비공개 계정에서만 나타났고 두 플랫폼의 공개 게시물과는 달랐다. 따라서 솔직함을 결정하는 것은 플랫폼이 아니라 청중의 범위와 친밀도이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 Instagram에서 더 솔직하다는 부분적 관찰에 근거하지만, 공개 Instagram 게시물도 솔직하지 않았으므로 플랫폼 설계를 원인으로 볼 수 없다. C는 B와 같은 틀이지만 게시 빈도는 솔직함의 원인으로 제시되지 않았다. D는 공개 Instagram 게시물이 더 정확하다는 근거가 없으며, 지문은 두 플랫폼의 공개 게시물이 모두 비공개 계정과 달랐다고 말한다.
input.explanation_en: Goffman's theory says people change how they present themselves based on the audience they expect, and the candid posts showed up only on private accounts seen by close friends, which differed from public posts on both platforms. That means candor tracks the audience, not the platform, so B is correct. A builds on the partial observation that users were more candid on Instagram, but their public Instagram posts weren't candid either, so you can't credit Instagram's design. C uses the same structure as B, but the text never connects posting frequency to candor. D isn't supported, because the text says public posts on both platforms differed from the private ones, so it gives you no reason to think public Instagram posts are more accurate.
input.design: Two steps are required: apply the audience-based theory, then notice that the candor appears only on private accounts, not on public posts on either platform. Choice A tempts readers who skim and see that candor showed up on Instagram, while C copies the correct answer's structure.

input.passage: In the 1870s and 1880s, cheap wheat from the American Midwest, carried by railroads and steamships, began flooding European markets. Large grain estates in eastern Prussia, owned by the landed nobility known as Junkers, relied on armies of seasonal laborers working the fields by hand. Some economic historians argue that the Junkers' political push for high tariffs on imported grain stemmed less from general hostility to trade than from a specific weakness: their labor-intensive methods left them unable to match the falling production costs of mechanized American farms, so that without protection their estates would have operated at a loss.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' argument?
options: Junker estates that switched from grain to sugar beets in the 1880s hired even more seasonal laborers than before, though their landowners kept lobbying for grain tariffs.
Junker landowners publicly opposed tariffs on imported manufactured goods during the same decades in which they pushed for tariffs on imported grain.
American wheat shipped to German ports in the 1880s sold for roughly the same price as wheat grown on small family farms in western Germany.
Estate account books show that per-bushel costs on Junker estates in the 1880s exceeded the price at which American wheat was then selling in Berlin.
input.explanation: 이 주장의 핵심은 융커 영지의 생산비가 미국 밀 가격을 따라가지 못해 보호 없이는 손실을 봤다는 것이다. D는 융커 영지의 부셸당 비용이 베를린에서 팔리던 미국 밀 가격보다 높았음을 보여 주므로 이를 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 무역 전반에 대한 적대감이 아니라는 점과는 맞지만, 비용 열세를 보여 주지는 않는다. C는 융커 영지가 아니라 서부 독일 소농과 비교한 것이므로 융커의 비용을 알 수 없다. A는 노동 집약성은 언급하지만 곡물 생산비 문제와 연결되지 않고, 곡물을 재배하지 않는데도 관세를 원했다면 오히려 주장을 약화시킬 수 있다.
input.explanation_en: The core of the argument is that Junker estates couldn't match American production costs, so without tariffs they would have lost money. D shows that the Junker estates' per-bushel costs were higher than the price of American wheat in Berlin, which supports that point directly. B fits the idea that the Junkers weren't hostile to trade in general, but it says nothing about their costs being too high. C compares American wheat with small farms in western Germany, not with Junker estates, so it tells you nothing about Junker costs. A brings up heavy use of labor, but not grain costs. And if estates that no longer grew grain still lobbied for grain tariffs, that could actually weaken the argument.
input.design: The two incorrect choices B and C each partly echo the claim (the point about general hostility to trade, and cheap American wheat). To rule them out, students have to connect the claim's actual point, Junker costs compared with American prices, to the evidence. Only D makes that connection.

content.text:
Design: subject-verb agreement after a long intervening modifier, plus a finite vs nonfinite choice.

Passage: "Granted by Elizabeth I in 1600, the charter of the English East India Company, which barred all other English merchants from trading east of the Cape of Good Hope, ______ the company to raise its own armed forces to defend that monopoly at sea."

Subject: "charter" is singular, so the verb should be "permitted" or "permits." Past tense fits the historical context, but "permits" might also work, so I'll leave it out. Options: A "were permitting" (plural, agrees with "merchants"), B "permitted", C "permitting" (nonfinite, leaves the sentence without a main verb), D "have permitted" (plural). That gives two plural distractors and one nonfinite form. Fine.

input.passage: Granted by Elizabeth I in 1600, the charter of the English East India Company, which barred all other English merchants from trading east of the Cape of Good Hope, ______ the company to raise its own armed ships and soldiers to enforce that monopoly along oceanic trade routes.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were permitting
permitted
permitting
have permitted
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'the charter'이고, 'which'로 시작하는 관계절은 삽입된 수식어이므로 빈칸에는 주어와 수가 일치하는 정동사가 필요하다. B는 과거 시제 정동사로 단수 주어와 맞고, 1600년이라는 역사적 문맥에도 맞는다. A와 D는 정동사이지만 복수형이어서 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'merchants'에 맞춘 오류다. C는 분사이므로 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of the main clause is the singular noun "the charter." The "which" clause is just an interrupting modifier, so the blank needs a main verb that agrees with "charter." B gives a past-tense main verb that fits the singular subject and the historical setting of 1600. A and D are main verbs, but both are plural forms, which wrongly agree with the nearby plural noun "merchants." C is a participle, so the sentence would have no main verb.
input.design: A long participial phrase and a relational clause separate the singular subject from the blank, and the nearby plural noun "merchants" acts as a lure. Two plural main verbs and one nonfinite form are the distractors.

content.text:
