A talks about how readers reacted in the 1960s, and the passage never mentions this. B is right that she revised, but the looping, repeated structure is still in the finished novel, so the claim that she made it linear contradicts the passage. C uses the drafts as evidence too, but the passage never says the drafts are more reliable than the published book, so C goes beyond the argument.
input.design: 이 문항은 반대 견해를 먼저 소개한 뒤 원고 증거로 반박하는 두 단계 구조입니다. 오답 B와 C는 '수정했다', '원고가 근거다'라는 부분적으로 맞는 내용을 담고 있어, 지문의 논리와 꼼꼼히 비교해야 배제할 수 있습니다.

input.passage: Many pet owners describe their dogs and cats as feeling guilt, jealousy, or embarrassment. Psychologist Lena Varga and colleagues propose that such anthropomorphic attributions are not simply a result of spending a lot of time with an animal. Instead, they argue, owners attribute complex humanlike mental states to a pet mainly because they are emotionally attached to it: the stronger the bond, the more an owner reads humanlike minds into the animal's behavior, even when the amount of daily contact is the same.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Varga and colleagues' claim?
options: Owners who spent more hours per day with their pets attributed more complex emotions such as guilt to those pets than did owners who spent fewer hours with their pets.
Owners who were strongly attached to their pets reported spending more hours per day with those pets than did owners who were weakly attached to their pets.
Owners who were strongly attached to their pets and owners who were weakly attached to their pets attributed simple emotions such as fear to those pets at similar rates.

Among owners who spent the same number of hours per day with their pets, those who were strongly attached attributed more complex emotions such as guilt to those pets than did those who were weakly attached.
input.design: 정답이 되려면 두 가지를 연결해야 한다: 애착이 원인이라는 주장, 그리고 접촉 시간을 통제하는 조건이다. 오답은 같은 문장 틀을 쓰고, 그중 둘은 이 연결의 한쪽만 담고 있다.
input.explanation: 연구진의 주장은 하루 접촉 시간이 같을 때에도 애착이 강할수록 반려동물에게 복잡한 인간적 정신 상태를 더 많이 부여한다는 것이다. D는 접촉 시간을 같게 맞춘 상태에서 애착이 강한 집단이 죄책감 같은 복잡한 감정을 더 많이 부여했다고 보여 주므로 주장을 직접 지지한다. A는 접촉 시간이 원인일 수 있음을 보여 줄 뿐이어서 연구진이 배제하려는 설명에 더 가깝다. B는 애착과 접촉 시간이 함께 움직인다는 것만 보여 주므로 두 요인을 구분하지 못하고, 감정 부여에 대해서도 아무것도 말하지 않는다. C는 공포 같은 단순한 감정에 관한 결과라서 복잡한 정신 상태에 관한 주장과 직접 연결되지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The researchers claim that stronger emotional attachment leads owners to attribute more complex humanlike mental states to their pets, even when daily contact time is the same. D directly supports this: it holds contact time constant and shows that strongly attached owners attributed more complex emotions, such as guilt. A points to time spent together as the cause, which is the explanation the researchers argue against. B shows only that attachment and contact time tend to go together, so it can't separate the two factors, and it says nothing about attributing emotions. C is about simple emotions such as fear, not the complex mental states the claim is about.

input.passage: Graphene aerogels are among the lightest solids ever made: some samples have densities below 0.2 milligrams per cubic centimeter, lighter than the air they displace. Their structure is hierarchical, with micrometer-scale cells whose walls are themselves riddled with nanometer-scale pores. Engineers testing these materials as thermal insulators have found that heat moving through the solid graphene walls is limited mainly by how thin and sparse those walls are, and that this effect works the same way at any pore size. Heat carried by gas trapped inside the material, however, depends strongly on pore size: when pores are narrower than the average distance a gas molecule travels before striking another molecule (about 70 nanometers for air at room pressure), molecules hit pore walls more often than one another, and gas conduction drops sharply. A research team compared two aerogels of identical density, one with mostly micrometer-scale pores and one in which most of the volume consisted of pores smaller than 50 nanometers. Based on these findings, the team should expect that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the aerogel with mostly micrometer-scale pores will insulate better, because its larger cells leave less solid graphene to carry heat.
the two aerogels will insulate about equally well, because heat moving through their solid walls should be limited to the same degree.
the aerogel with mostly sub-50-nanometer pores will insulate better, because the air inside it should carry noticeably less heat.
the aerogel with mostly sub-50-nanometer pores will insulate better, because its finer structure should make its graphene walls less dense.
input.explanation: 두 에어로젤의 밀도가 같으므로 고체 벽을 통한 열전도는 같은 수준이고, 차이는 기체 전도에서만 생긴다. 50nm보다 작은 기공은 공기 분자의 평균 이동 거리(약 70nm)보다 좁아 기체 전도가 급격히 줄어든다. 따라서 C가 맞다. A는 밀도가 같다는 조건을 무시하고 고체량 차이를 가정한다. B는 고체 전도가 같다는 점은 맞지만 기공 크기에 따른 기체 전도 차이를 놓친다. D는 결론은 맞지만, 밀도가 같으니 벽이 덜 조밀해진다는 근거가 지문과 모순된다.
input.explanation_en: Because the two aerogels have the same density, heat moving through their solid walls should be about the same, so any difference has to come from the gas inside. Pores smaller than 50 nanometers are narrower than air's roughly 70-nanometer mean free path, so gas conduction in that sample drops sharply. That makes C correct. A ignores that the densities are equal and assumes one sample has less solid graphene. B is right that solid conduction should match, but it misses how pore size changes gas conduction. D reaches the right conclusion for the wrong reason: since the densities are equal, the passage gives no support for the walls being less dense.
input.design: Students have to connect two facts: equal density means the solid conduction matches, and pores under 50 nm are smaller than the ~70 nm mean free path, which cuts gas conduction. Option B gets only the first step right, and D picks the right sample but gives a mechanism the passage contradicts.

input.passage: Psychologists use the term "savoring" for the deliberate practice of attending to and prolonging positive experiences, including anticipating pleasant events before they occur. In a three-year longitudinal study, researchers measured participants' tendency to savor upcoming events and their life satisfaction at yearly intervals. Participants who reported savoring more at the start showed greater increases in life satisfaction over the following years. However, the researchers also found that these participants did not report more pleasant events in their lives than other participants did; the two groups experienced roughly the same number of enjoyable occasions, such as trips, celebrations, and visits with friends. These findings suggest that the savoring participants' rising life satisfaction is best explained by ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the greater number of trips, celebrations, and visits that frequent savorers arranged for themselves over the three years.
the higher levels of life satisfaction that frequent savorers already had when the study began.
the tendency of frequent savorers to forget unpleasant events more quickly than other participants did.
the way frequent savorers mentally engaged with their pleasant events, not how often such events occurred.
input.explanation: 지문은 savoring을 많이 한 참가자들이 삶의 만족도가 더 크게 증가했지만, 즐거운 사건의 수는 다른 참가자와 비슷했다고 말한다. 따라서 차이는 사건의 빈도가 아니라 사건을 마음속으로 다루는 방식에서 와야 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 사건 수가 같았다는 진술과 정면으로 모순된다. B는 연구가 측정한 것이 초기 수준이 아니라 만족도의 '증가'라는 점을 놓쳤고, C는 불쾌한 사건에 대한 정보가 지문에 없어 근거가 없다.
input.explanation_en: The passage says frequent savorers had larger gains in life satisfaction, yet they had about the same number of pleasant events as everyone else. That means the difference can't come from how often good things happened. It has to come from how these people mentally engaged with those events, so D is correct. A contradicts the finding that both groups had similar numbers of events. B misses that the study tracked increases in satisfaction, not starting levels, and C brings in unpleasant events, which the passage never discusses.
input.design: 이 문제는 두 가지 정보를 연결해야 풀 수 있습니다. 하나는 만족도가 더 크게 증가했다는 점이고, 다른 하나는 즐거운 사건의 수가 비슷했다는 점입니다. 지문을 훑어 읽으면 "사건이 더 많았다"는 A나 "원래 만족도가 높았다"는 B를 고르기 쉽습니다. 모든 선택지는 같은 'the ... of/that frequent savorers' 문장 틀로 썼습니다.

input.passage: By the 1920s, vast sugar estates known as latifundia controlled much of Cuba's farmland, and smallholders who had once grown food crops increasingly worked for wages on the estates. In an essay from that period, one Cuban critic described what this concentration of land in a single crop had done to the island's economy: Cuba, he wrote, "sold one crop to the world, bought nearly everything else it consumed, and ______ at the mercy of a single price set in New York."
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: lives
living
lived
would live
input.explanation:
정답 C(lived). 인용문 안에서 "sold … , bought … , and ______"로 세 개의 동사가 병렬로 이어지며, 앞의 두 동사가 모두 단순과거이다. 따라서 빈칸에도 단순과거 lived가 와야 시제와 형태가 일치한다. 인용문을 감싸는 문장(wrote, had done)도 과거 시점의 진단을 다루므로 맥락과도 맞는다.
A(lives): 현재 시제로, 인용문 안의 과거 시제 sold·bought와 어긋난다. 섬이 지금도 종속 상태라고 느끼게 하는 '일반적 진술' 착각을 노린 오답이다.
B(living): 병렬 구조에서 한 항목만 분사로 바꾸어 정동사 sold·bought와 형태가 맞지 않는다. 'and living'을 분사구문으로 잘못 읽게 만드는 오답이다.
D(would live): 'he wrote … that' 같은 과거 주절 안의 간접화법이라면 과거 속 미래로 어울릴 수 있지만, 이 인용문은 이미 일어난 상황을 과거형 병렬로 서술하고 있어 전체 맥락과 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en:
The answer is C, "lived." Inside the quotation, three verbs are listed in parallel: "sold … , bought … , and ______." The first two are both simple past, so the blank also needs the simple past "lived" to keep the tense and form consistent. The sentence around the quotation ("wrote," "had done") is also about a diagnosis made in the past, so "lived" fits there too.
A ("lives") is present tense. It clashes with "sold" and "bought" inside the quotation. It might seem right if you read the line as a general, timeless statement, but the critic is describing Cuba as it was.
B ("living") breaks the parallel structure. It turns one item into a participle, while the others are finite verbs ("sold," "bought").
D ("would live") could work in reported speech after a past-tense verb like "wrote," where it would describe a future in the past. But this quotation describes a situation that already existed, using past-tense verbs in a series, so "would live" doesn't fit the whole sentence.
input.design: To fill the blank, you have to look at the parallel series inside the quotation (sold, bought, ___) and also at the past-tense sentence around it. The wrong answers are built from three traps: a tense that clashes with the quotation (lives), a form that breaks the parallel series (living), and a "future in the past" that fits only the reporting verb "wrote" (would live).

input.passage: Conventional sintering bakes compacted ceramic powder in a furnace for hours, often at temperatures above 1,600°C. Spark plasma sintering, a technique that sends pulsed electric current directly through the powder and its graphite die, concentrates heat at the contact points between ______ the material can reach nearly full density in minutes and at temperatures several hundred degrees lower.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: grains, as a result
grains, as a result,
grains; as a result,
grains as a result,
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "Spark plasma sintering ... concentrates heat at the contact points between grains"는 동격 삽입구가 길게 들어 있어도 하나의 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤의 "the material can reach..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 이어야 하며, 접속부사 "as a result" 뒤에는 쉼표를 찍으므로 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 접속 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 "as a result" 앞뒤에 쉼표를 찍어 삽입어처럼 보이지만, 접속부사가 있어도 쉼표로는 두 절을 이을 수 없다. D는 두 절 사이에 아무 문장부호도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
input.explanation_en: The part before the blank, "Spark plasma sintering ... concentrates heat at the contact points between grains," is one independent clause, even though a long appositive sits inside it. The part after the blank, "the material can reach...," is also an independent clause. You need a semicolon to join two independent clauses, and the conjunctive adverb "as a result" takes a comma after it, so C is correct. A and B join the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B puts commas on both sides of "as a result" so it looks like an aside, but a conjunctive adverb can't join two clauses with just a comma. D has no punctuation between the clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence.
input.design: 긴 동격 삽입구 때문에 주절의 끝이 흐려지게 했다. 그래서 학생이 빈칸 앞이 독립절인지 먼저 확인하고, 그다음 접속부사에 맞는 문장부호를 골라야 한다. 오답 B는 쉼표 위치가 그럴듯해 보이도록 만들었다.

input.passage: For much of the early eighteenth century, the Navigation Acts, which required that many colonial goods be shipped only to England and carried on English or colonial vessels, existed largely on paper in British North America. Customs officers were few, often underpaid, and frequently willing to accept bribes, so colonial merchants routinely traded with French and Dutch Caribbean ports without consequence. Historians sometimes call this period one of "salutary neglect." After 1763, however, Parliament, burdened by debt from the Seven Years' War, began enforcing the laws in earnest: it expanded the customs service, authorized general search warrants known as writs of assistance, and moved smuggling cases to vice-admiralty courts that operated without juries. Many colonists who had long accepted the Acts in principle now viewed them as intrusive, and their complaints about searches and jury-less trials became early arguments in the broader case against British authority.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Colonial merchants turned to French and Dutch Caribbean ports mainly because the Navigation Acts made trade with England unprofitable.
Parliament passed the Navigation Acts after 1763 as a way to pay off debts left over from the Seven Years' War.
Colonial opposition grew less from the Navigation Acts themselves than from Britain's shift toward strictly enforcing laws it had long overlooked.
Colonists objected to the Navigation Acts chiefly because vice-admiralty courts punished smugglers more harshly than juries had.
input.design: 정답을 고르려면 앞부분의 오랜 '방치'와 1763년 이후의 엄격한 집행을 연결해 '변화'가 핵심임을 파악해야 한다. 오답 B와 D는 지문 속 세부(부채, 배심원 없는 재판)를 비틀어 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 갖게 했다.
input.explanation: 지문은 항해법이 오랫동안 사실상 집행되지 않다가 1763년 이후 엄격히 집행되면서, 원칙적으로는 이를 받아들이던 식민지인들이 침해적이라고 느끼게 되었다고 설명하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 카리브해 무역이 처벌받지 않았다는 점만 언급될 뿐, 영국과의 무역이 수익성이 없었다는 내용은 없다. B는 전쟁 부채라는 세부를 쓰지만, 이 법은 1763년 이전부터 존재했고 1763년 이후 바뀐 것은 집행이었다. D는 배심원 없는 재판이라는 세부를 쓰지만, 처벌의 엄격함을 비교하지 않으며 글 전체의 요지도 아니다.
input.explanation_en: C is correct. The text explains that the Navigation Acts went mostly unenforced for decades, and then after 1763 Britain began enforcing them strictly, so colonists who had accepted the laws in principle started seeing them as intrusive. A is wrong because the text only says trade with Caribbean ports went unpunished; it never says trade with England was unprofitable. B uses the war-debt detail, but the Acts already existed before 1763, and what changed afterward was enforcement, not the laws themselves. D picks up the detail about jury-less trials, but the text never compares how harsh the punishments were, and that point isn't the passage's main idea anyway.

input.passage: For centuries, engineers assumed that the longevity of Roman vaults such as the Pantheon's dome resulted mainly from the careful selection of volcanic ash, which reacts with lime to form a strong binding matrix. Recent analyses of opus caementicium samples, however, have drawn attention to small white lumps of lime scattered throughout the material, long dismissed as evidence of sloppy mixing. __Researchers led by Admir Masic found that these lumps form when quicklime is mixed in hot, and that when cracks later admit water, the lumps dissolve and recrystallize as calcium carbonate, sealing the fractures.__ This finding suggests that Roman builders may have relied not only on durable ingredients but also on a mixing method that allowed their concrete to repair itself over time.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that reinterprets a feature of the material previously regarded as a flaw.
It presents evidence that confirms the long-held view about why volcanic ash made Roman vaults strong.
It presents a criticism of Roman builders for mixing their concrete carelessly.
It presents an example of how modern engineers have copied Roman concrete in new buildings.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞 문장에서 '부주의한 혼합의 증거'로 여겨지던 석회 덩어리가 실제로는 균열을 메우는 자가 치유 기능을 한다는 연구 결과를 제시하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 화산재 설명을 언급하지만, 밑줄 문장은 기존 견해를 확인하는 것이 아니라 새로운 요인을 추가한다. C는 '부주의한 혼합'이라는 표현을 활용하지만, 그것은 밑줄 문장이 뒤집는 과거의 해석이다. D의 현대 건물 적용은 지문에 나오지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence reports findings showing that the lime lumps, once dismissed as signs of sloppy mixing, actually seal cracks, so it reinterprets a supposed flaw. That makes A correct. B mentions volcanic ash, but the sentence adds a new factor instead of confirming the old view. C picks up the "sloppy mixing" idea, but that is the old interpretation the sentence overturns. D is wrong because the text never talks about modern buildings copying Roman concrete.
input.design: This needs two steps: link the underlined finding to the earlier "dismissed as sloppy" claim, then see that it changes the meaning of that feature. Choices B and C each reuse a detail from the text, so they look partly right.

input.passage: In The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life (1959), sociologist Erving Goffman described social interaction as a kind of performance: on a "front stage," people manage the impressions they make on an audience, while "backstage" they let those performances slip. Researchers studying online identity have found the framework especially useful. The carefully chosen photographs that a typical user posts to a public profile, along with the witty captions that accompany each one, ______ what Goffman called a "front," an idealized version of the self shaped with an imagined audience in mind.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: functioning as
functions as
having functioned as
function as
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "photographs"이고, "that a typical user posts to a public profile"과 "along with the witty captions..."는 주어를 꾸미거나 덧붙이는 수식어구일 뿐이므로 문장에는 복수형 정동사가 필요하다. 따라서 복수형 정동사인 D가 정답이다. B는 정동사이긴 하지만 단수형이어서, 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "one"이나 "profile", 또는 "along with" 구문에 끌려 잘못 고른 답이다. A와 C는 분사 형태여서 문장에 본동사가 없게 되므로 완전한 문장이 되지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "photographs." The phrases "that a typical user posts to a public profile" and "along with the witty captions..." just modify or add to that subject, so the sentence needs a plural finite verb. That makes D correct, since it is the plural main verb. B is a finite verb, but it's singular, so you'd only pick it if you got distracted by a nearby singular noun like "one" or "profile," or by the "along with" phrase. A and C are participles, which leave the sentence with no main verb, so it isn't a complete sentence.
input.design: 긴 관계절과 'along with' 삽입구로 주어와 동사를 떨어뜨려 놓았다. 그래서 학생은 정동사가 필요하다는 점과 복수 주어에 맞춰야 한다는 점을 둘 다 판단해야 한다. B는 앞의 판단은 맞고 뒤의 판단에서 틀리는 오답이다.

input.passage: Historians of Victorian public health long assumed that the health visitors sent into working-class homes in 1890s Manchester did little to improve infant survival, since the women offered advice rather than medicine or money. However, when historian Alys Brennan compared parish burial registers from districts with and without regular visits, she found that infant deaths from diarrheal illness fell markedly only where visitors had taught mothers to boil milk and keep feeding bottles clean. Brennan concludes that the visitors' influence on infant health was far from negligible; it was, in fact, ______.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: inconsequential
modest
controversial
substantial
input.explanation: 정답 D(substantial). 통념은 방문원이 영아 생존에 거의 기여하지 못했다는 것이었으나, 'However' 뒤의 증거(방문 지역에서만 설사성 질환 사망이 크게 감소)와 'far from negligible; in fact'가 통념과 정반대인 '상당한' 영향을 요구한다. A(inconsequential)는 통념을 그대로 반복한 단어로 'far from negligible'과 모순된다. B(modest)는 전환을 반만 반영한 약한 정도의 표현으로, '현저히(markedly)' 감소했다는 증거와 'far from'의 강한 부정을 담아내지 못한다. C(controversial)는 영향의 크기가 아니라 논란 여부라는 무관한 의미이며, 지문에 논쟁에 관한 근거가 없다.
input.explanation_en: The correct answer is D (substantial). The old assumption was that health visitors did little for infant survival. After "However," the burial-register evidence shows infant deaths fell markedly only in visited districts, and the phrase "far from negligible; it was, in fact" calls for a word meaning the opposite of the old view: a large effect. A (inconsequential) just repeats the old view and contradicts "far from negligible." B (modest) only half follows the reversal. A "markedly" large drop and the strong wording "far from" point to a big effect, not a small one. C (controversial) is about whether people dispute the effect, not how big it is, and nothing in the text mentions a dispute.
input.design: "not far from" 구조는 피하고, 통념(효과 미미) 뒤에 However와 반박 증거를 두어 빈칸이 정반대 의미를 갖게 했다. 오답은 통념 단어, 같은 방향이지만 약한 단어, 무관한 제3의 의미 단어로 구성했다.

input.passage: In his 1961 study at Stanford University, psychologist Albert Bandura arranged for preschool children to watch an adult strike, kick, and shout at an inflatable Bobo doll. The children who observed this aggressive model, when later left alone in a room full of toys, ______ many of the same actions, often repeating the adult's exact words.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: imitating
imitated
having imitated
who imitated
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'The children'이고, 'who observed this aggressive model'은 관계절이며 'when later left alone in a room full of toys'는 삽입된 수식어구이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 주어에 대응하는 정동사가 필요하고, 과거시제 정동사 imitated를 쓴 B가 정답이다. A의 imitating과 C의 having imitated는 분사여서 정동사 역할을 하지 못하므로 문장이 완성되지 않는다. D의 who imitated는 관계절을 하나 더 만들 뿐이어서 주절의 동사가 여전히 없다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The children." The phrase "who observed this aggressive model" is a relative clause, and "when later left alone in a room full of toys" is a modifier inserted between the subject and the blank. That means the blank needs a finite verb for the subject, and B, the past-tense "imitated," fills that role. A ("imitating") and C ("having imitated") are participles, not finite verbs, so the sentence would be left incomplete. D ("who imitated") just adds another relative clause, so the main clause still has no verb.
input.design: 주어와 빈칸 사이에 관계절과 삽입 수식어구를 넣어 주절 동사가 없다는 점을 놓치기 쉽게 했다. 오답은 분사형 두 개와 관계절 하나로, 모두 문맥상 그럴듯해 보이도록 구성했다.

input.passage: After the Compromise of 1867 divided the Habsburg realm into Austrian and Hungarian halves, the empire's many nationalities, including Czechs, Croats, Slovaks, Romanians, and others, pressed for greater recognition. Some historians argue that ethnic nationalism alone did not doom the Dual Monarchy. Historian Pieter Judson, for one, contends that before 1914 most nationalist movements sought expanded rights, such as language use in schools and courts, within the empire rather than independence from it, and that the empire's collapse resulted mainly from the strains of the First World War.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Judson's claim?
options: Programs issued by major Czech and Croatian parties between 1890 and 1910 demanded official status for their languages in local administration while explicitly endorsing continued loyalty to the Habsburg crown.
Programs issued by major Czech and Croatian parties between 1890 and 1910 demanded official status for their languages, and some party leaders later headed independent states formed after 1918.
Programs issued by major Czech and Croatian parties between 1890 and 1910 grew increasingly popular, with membership in nationalist associations rising sharply across the empire.

Programs issued by major Czech and Croatian parties between 1890 and 1910 were frequently debated in parliament, where disputes over language laws repeatedly brought legislative business to a standstill.
input.explanation: 저드슨의 주장은 1914년 이전 민족주의 운동이 독립이 아니라 제국 '안에서' 권리 확대를 추구했다는 것이다. A는 언어 권리를 요구하면서 합스부르크 왕실에 대한 충성을 명시해 두 요소를 모두 충족한다. B는 언어 요구는 맞지만, 지도자들이 1918년 이후 독립국가를 이끌었다는 내용은 전쟁 이전 목표가 무엇이었는지 보여주지 못하고 오히려 분리주의로 읽힐 수 있다. C는 민족주의가 성장했다는 점만 보여줄 뿐 그 목표가 자치였는지 독립이었는지 알려주지 않는다. D는 민족 갈등이 제국을 마비시켰다는 의미로 읽혀, 민족주의가 불안정을 낳았다는 반대 견해에 더 가깝다.
input.explanation_en: Judson claims that before 1914, nationalist movements wanted more rights within the empire, not independence from it. Choice A shows parties asking for language rights while openly pledging loyalty to the Habsburg crown, so it matches both parts of the claim. Choice B includes the language demands, but the fact that leaders later headed independent states says nothing about what they wanted before the war, and it may even suggest separatism. Choice C only shows that nationalism grew, not whether its goal was autonomy or independence. Choice D suggests that ethnic conflict paralyzed the government, which fits the opposing view that nationalism destabilized the empire.
input.design: Every option uses the same opening frame. To get the answer, students have to connect two things: the movements' demands and their stance toward the empire. B and C each give part of the picture, and D sounds relevant but actually points the other way.

input.passage: In capillary electrophoresis, charged molecules are separated as an electric field pulls them through a narrow silica tube. The tube's inner wall carries negative charges that drag the surrounding fluid toward one end, a bulk movement called electroosmotic flow. Because this flow pushes fluid evenly across the whole width of the tube, bands of molecules stay sharp instead of spreading out, which is why the method can tell apart molecules whose speeds differ only slightly. But when chemist Lena Ortiz ran samples containing proteins that stick readily to silica, she found that the proteins coated parts of the wall and canceled its charge there, leaving uneven flow along the tube. Given this, Ortiz concluded that for samples with such proteins, the method's usual ability to distinguish closely related molecules ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: would get better, since proteins covering the wall would stop the molecules from losing speed through contact with the silica.
would stay the same, since the electric field pulling the charged molecules would still be at full strength along the whole tube.
would matter less, since proteins that stick to silica would all leave the tube at the same time no matter how fast they moved.
would probably be weakened, since the condition that keeps the molecule bands narrow would no longer be met.
input.explanation: 지문에 따르면 분해능은 관 벽 전체에서 고른 전기삼투 흐름이 생겨 띠가 날카롭게 유지되는 데서 나온다. 단백질이 벽의 전하를 상쇄하면 흐름이 고르지 않게 되므로 이 조건이 깨지고, 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 벽 접촉이라는 그럴듯한 이유를 대지만, 지문은 흐름이 고르지 않게 된다고만 말한다. B는 전기장이 그대로라는 점은 맞을 수 있으나, 분해능을 좌우하는 것은 흐름의 균일성이다. C는 모든 단백질이 동시에 나온다는 근거가 지문에 없다.
input.explanation_en: The passage says the method can resolve close molecules because electroosmotic flow is even across the tube, which keeps bands sharp. Ortiz found that sticky proteins canceled the wall's charge in some places and made the flow uneven, so that condition breaks down. That makes D the answer. A offers a plausible-sounding idea about wall contact, but the passage only says the coating makes flow uneven, not that it helps. B may be right that the field stays at full strength, but what drives resolution here is even flow. C claims the proteins all exit at the same time, and nothing in the passage supports that.
input.design: To answer, students have to connect two pieces of the passage: even flow keeps bands sharp, and protein coating makes the flow uneven. Choices A and B each use a real detail from the passage (the wall, the electric field) to make them tempting.

input.passage: In 1291, Venetian authorities ordered the city's glassmakers to relocate their furnaces to the island of Murano, officially to reduce the risk of fire. The move also served an economic purpose: concentrating the industry in one place allowed the guild to monitor its members closely. Artisans who mastered techniques such as producing nearly colorless cristallo glass were granted social privileges, yet the secrets of their craft, guarded by strict guild regulations that threatened deserters with heavy penalties, ______ within the lagoon for centuries.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: remained largely confined
remaining largely confined
having remained largely confined
to remain largely confined
input.explanation: "yet" 뒤의 절은 주어 "the secrets of their craft"를 가지며, 삽입된 분사구 "guarded by ... penalties" 뒤에 정동사가 필요하다. A의 과거형 "remained"가 이 절의 정동사가 되어 문장이 완성된다. B의 현재분사 "remaining"은 정동사가 아니므로 절이 미완성으로 남는다. C의 "having remained"도 분사구라 동사 역할을 할 수 없다. D의 부정사 "to remain"도 정동사가 아니어서 절이 성립하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The clause after "yet" has the subject "the secrets of their craft," and after the interrupting phrase "guarded by ... penalties," it still needs a main verb. Choice A gives it one with the past-tense "remained," which completes the clause. Choice B's "remaining" is a present participle, not a main verb, so the clause is left unfinished. Choice C's "having remained" is also a participial phrase and can't work as the main verb. Choice D's infinitive "to remain" isn't a main verb either, so the clause is still incomplete.
input.design: 긴 분사 삽입구가 주어와 동사 사이를 갈라놓아서, 훑어 읽으면 이미 동사가 있다고 착각하고 분사형 선택지를 고르기 쉽게 만들었다.

input.passage: Art historians have long praised Gian Lorenzo Bernini's marble sculptures, such as The Ecstasy of Saint Teresa (1647–1652), for their dramatic sense of movement and emotional intensity. Most scholars attribute this intensity mainly to the carving itself: the twisting drapery, parted lips, and strained limbs. Art historian Lena Varga argues for a different explanation. She contends that much of the emotional effect depends on Bernini's control of the viewing environment, especially hidden windows and architectural framing that direct light onto the figures. In Varga's view, the same marble seen under ordinary, even lighting would seem noticeably calmer to viewers.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Varga's claim?
options: When viewers rated photographs of Bernini's figures taken under concealed directional light and under uniform studio light, they judged the same figures far more emotionally agitated in the first set than in the second.

When viewers rated photographs of Bernini's figures alongside photographs of works by his contemporaries, they judged Bernini's twisting drapery and strained poses far more emotionally agitated than his rivals' calmer carving.

When viewers rated photographs of Bernini's chapels taken from several angles, they judged the hidden windows and gilded framing to be among the most admired architectural features of seventeenth-century Rome.

When viewers rated photographs of Bernini's figures taken under concealed directional light, they judged the figures in his later works far more emotionally agitated than the figures in his earlier works.
input.design: 정답 A는 대리석은 그대로 두고 조명만 바꿔 비교하므로 Varga의 주장을 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 조각 기법 쪽 설명을 지지하고, C는 감정 효과가 아니라 건축에 대한 평가이며, D는 조명은 같고 시기만 다르다. 오답들도 정답과 같은 문장 틀을 따르도록 써서 겉모습으로 정답을 고를 수 없게 했다.
input.explanation: Varga의 주장은 같은 대리석이라도 균일한 조명 아래에서는 덜 격정적으로 보인다는 것이다. A는 같은 조각을 숨겨진 방향성 조명과 균일한 조명 아래에서 비교해 앞의 경우에 훨씬 격정적으로 평가되었음을 보여 주므로, 이 주장을 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 비틀린 옷주름 같은 조각 기법이 감정의 원천이라는 기존 학자들의 견해를 지지한다. C는 창과 테두리 장식에 대한 평가일 뿐, 그것이 조각의 감정 효과를 만든다는 증거가 아니다. D는 조명 조건이 같은 상태에서 제작 시기만 비교하므로 조명의 효과를 따로 떼어 보여 주지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: Varga claims that the same marble would look calmer to viewers under ordinary, even lighting. Choice A compares the same figures under concealed directional light and under uniform light, and viewers found them far more agitated under the first, so it directly supports her claim. Choice B supports the opposing view that carving techniques such as twisting drapery are the source of the emotion. Choice C only shows that the windows and framing are admired as architecture, not that they create the sculptures' emotional effect. Choice D keeps the lighting the same and compares earlier works with later ones, so it can't show what effect the lighting has on its own.
